name: AnimPreviewInfo
documentation: AnimPreviewInfo is the state of a character's animation preview, returned by Instance:AnimationPreview.

name: CloudStore
documentation: CloudStore is a collection of records shared by every server of the game, opened with `CloudStore.open`. See CloudStore for the request budget and size limits.

name: Color3
documentation: Color3 creates colors. A color is a Luau `vector` whose `R`, `G` and `B` run from 0 to 1; lights and glowing surfaces take values above 1 to shine brighter.

name: ColorSequence
documentation: ColorSequence creates a color curve over time from 0 to 1, such as the color of a particle over its life. A sequence has 2 to 8 keypoints, and each channel changes in a straight line between them. To read the keypoints, see `ColorSequence`.

name: ColorSequence
documentation: ColorSequence is an immutable curve of colors over time from 0 to 1, read from a component field of type `ColorSequence`. To change a field, assign a new sequence from `ColorSequence.new`. A field that was never assigned reads as constant white.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local fade = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 1, 1), Color3.new(0, 0, 0))

print(#fade.Keypoints) -- prints 2
print(fade) -- prints ColorSequence(0 1 1 1, 1 0 0 0)

name: ColorSequenceKeypoint
documentation: ColorSequenceKeypoint creates one point of a `ColorSequence`. To read a keypoint, see `ColorSequenceKeypoint`.

name: ColorSequenceKeypoint
documentation: ColorSequenceKeypoint is one immutable point of a `ColorSequence`: a color at a time.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local fade = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 0.5, 0), Color3.new(0, 0, 0))
local first = fade.Keypoints[1]

print(first.Time) -- prints 0
print(first) -- prints ColorSequenceKeypoint(0, 1, 0.5, 0)

name: Component
documentation: Component reads and writes the fields of one component on an instance. `Instance:Component` returns one; index a field name to read or write it. A built-in component uses the field names in Component views.

name: ContentAsset
documentation: ContentAsset is one downloaded asset in memory, passed to the callback of `Content.Fetch`. The engine drops the least recently used asset when memory is full, so check `IsValid` before using an asset fetched a while ago.

name: ContentRequest
documentation: ContentRequest is a content request that has not finished, returned by `Content.Fetch` and `Content.Avatar`.

name: DynamicImage
documentation: runtime image constructor

name: DynamicMesh
documentation: DynamicMesh builds a 3D shape from vertices and triangles while the game runs, such as generated terrain. A dynamic mesh exists only on the client that builds it. Reserve room with `:SetCounts(vertices, indices)`, copy `count` items from byte `offset` in `data` to mesh position `start` with `:WriteVertices(data, offset, start, count)` and `:WriteIndices(data, offset, start, count)`, and show the mesh on an instance with `:Apply(target)`. A mesh takes up to 60000 vertices and 60000 indices; a client has room for 64 dynamic meshes, which share one pool of 262144 vertices and 786432 indices.

name: DynamicMesh
documentation: DynamicMesh builds a 3D shape from vertices and triangles while the game runs, such as generated terrain. A dynamic mesh exists only on the client that builds it. Reserve room with `:SetCounts(vertices, indices)`, copy `count` items from byte `offset` in `data` to mesh position `start` with `:WriteVertices(data, offset, start, count)` and `:WriteIndices(data, offset, start, count)`, and show the mesh on an instance with `:Apply(target)`. A mesh takes up to 60000 vertices and 60000 indices; a client has room for 64 dynamic meshes, which share one pool of 262144 vertices and 786432 indices.

name: EventColumn
documentation: EventColumn reads the values of one field across the events an event table received this tick. Index an EventTable with a field name, `sender` or `tick` to get one, then index the column from 1 to the table's `count`.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local CastSpell = game.EventTable("CastSpell", game.EventTable.ToServer, {
    {"spellId", game.EventTable.U8},
    {"target", game.EventTable.Vec3},
})

function Update(dt: number)
    for i = 1, CastSpell.count do
        if CastSpell.spellId[i] == 1 then
            game.Physics.Explode(CastSpell.target[i], 8, 500)
        end
    end
end

name: EventDirection
documentation: EventDirection is which way an event table sends events: `game.EventTable.ToServer` from client scripts to the server, or `game.EventTable.ToClients` from the server to clients.

name: EventFieldType
documentation: EventFieldType is the kind of value one field of an event table stores.

name: EventTable
documentation: EventTable is a network event table that `game.EventTable` returns. See EventTable for how to declare one and for its limits. Index it with a declared field name to get that field's EventColumn. A table can send at most 64 events in one tick; the next send raises an error.

name: EventTableDump
documentation: EventTableDump prints every event table, its fields, and how many events it has queued, sent, received and refused, to help find a missing or dropped event.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
EventTableDump()

name: FrameStats
documentation: FrameStats is how long each part of the engine took in the last frame, in milliseconds, and how much memory Luau uses. `game.Profiler.Frame` returns it.
code_sample:
-- Client script: warn when a frame takes longer than 1/30 second.
function Update(dt: number)
    local frame = game.Profiler.Frame()
    if frame and frame.interval > 33 then
        local logic = math.round(frame.sim)
        local drawing = math.round(frame.render)
        warn(`slow frame: {logic} ms logic, {drawing} ms drawing`)
    end
end

name: Identity
documentation: Identity is a record type for a player's user id, display name and admin flag. No engine function returns it.

name: Instance
documentation: Instance is an entity in the scene tree: a part, a light, a sound, a character or a user interface element. It has a name, a parent, children and the values of its components.

name: Instance
documentation: Instance is an entity in the scene tree: a part, a light, a sound, a character or a user interface element. It has a name, a parent, children and the values of its components.

name: MaterialAudio
documentation: MaterialAudio configures footstep or impact sounds.

name: MaterialEmission
documentation: MaterialEmission configures glow texture, color, and brightness.

name: MaterialEntry
documentation: MaterialEntry is one entry from `Materials.GetMaterials`.

name: MaterialPhysics
documentation: MaterialPhysics configures density, friction, and bounce.

name: MaterialSpec
documentation: MaterialSpec describes a material for `Materials.DefineMaterial` and `Materials.GetMaterial`.

name: MaterialStuds
documentation: MaterialStuds configures top and bottom stud textures for `"Stud"` materials.

name: MaterialSurface
documentation: MaterialSurface configures surface textures and shading multipliers.

name: MaterialWater
documentation: MaterialWater configures optics, foam, flow, and waves for `"Water"` materials.

name: MoveIntent
documentation: MoveIntent is the movement and facing table from the deprecated `Instance:GetMoveIntent` method. Read `CharacterMoveIntent` with `World.Query` instead.

name: NumberRange
documentation: NumberRange creates a range of numbers, such as a particle lifetime, where each particle picks its own value between the ends. To read the ends, see `NumberRange`.

name: NumberRange
documentation: NumberRange is an immutable `[Min, Max]` interval from `NumberRange.new`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local lifetime = NumberRange.new(2, 5)
print(lifetime.Max - lifetime.Min) -- prints 3

name: NumberSequence
documentation: NumberSequence creates a number curve over time from 0 to 1, such as the size of a particle over its life. A sequence has 2 to 8 keypoints, and values change in a straight line between them. To read the keypoints, see `NumberSequence`.

name: NumberSequence
documentation: NumberSequence is an immutable curve of numbers from time 0 to 1, created with `NumberSequence.new`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local fade = NumberSequence.new(1, 0)
print(#fade.Keypoints, fade.Keypoints[1].Value) -- prints 2 1

name: NumberSequenceKeypoint
documentation: NumberSequenceKeypoint creates one point of a `NumberSequence`. To read a keypoint, see `NumberSequenceKeypoint`.

name: NumberSequenceKeypoint
documentation: NumberSequenceKeypoint is one immutable point on a `NumberSequence` from `NumberSequenceKeypoint.new`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local point = NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, 10, 2)
print(point.Value, point.Envelope) -- prints 10 2

name: OperatorSpec
documentation: OperatorSpec is passed to plugin:Operator to configure an operator.

name: OrderedCloudStore
documentation: OrderedCloudStore is a shared leaderboard of integer scores opened with `CloudStore.open_ordered`; see `CloudStore` for request budgets. Keys are integers or strings of 1 to 50 printable characters, and Luau numbers represent integers without rounding in `[-2^53, 2^53]`.

name: OverlayItem
documentation: OverlayItem describes one 3D viewport shape in a tool's `Modal` overlay list (up to 1,024 items), in `Part`'s unscaled local frame.

name: Pair
documentation: Pair is an entity relationship (`"ChildOf"`, `"Tag"`, or `"WornBy"`) built with `World.Pair` and has no fields or methods. Pass it to `World.Query`, `World.Each`, `Query:With`, `Query:Without`, or `Instance` component methods.

name: ParamSpec
documentation: ParamSpec describes one parameter in `OperatorSpec.Params`.

name: PartOperationComponent
documentation: PartOperation is a union, an intersection, or a negative part that `game.Csg` makes. Its parts stay inside it. The server and every client rebuild the combined shape from them, so moving or resizing a part inside rebuilds it. Setting the operation's `Size` stretches the shape without a rebuild.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a wall part: cut a doorway and paint the wall white.
self.Anchored = true
self.Size = Vector3.new(12, 8, 1)

local doorway = Instance.new("Part")
doorway.Anchored = true
doorway.Size = Vector3.new(4, 7, 2)
doorway.Position = self.Position

local wall = game.Csg.Subtract(self, { doorway }) :: PartOperation?
if wall then
    print(wall.Type) -- prints Union
    wall.UsePartColor = true
    wall.Color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1)
end

name: Plugin
documentation: Plugin is the type of the `plugin` global, which registers a Studio plugin's operators, viewport tools, and Plugins tab buttons. Declare each operator before any tool or ribbon group that references its `Id`.

name: PluginContext
documentation: PluginContext passes Studio's selection, snap steps, camera state, and (inside `Execute`) `Edit` to `Poll`, `Execute`, and `Modal`. Studio builds a fresh context per call; do not store it across calls.

name: PluginEdit
documentation: PluginEdit modifies the edit place inside an operator's `Execute` via `ctx.Edit`. World edits form one undo step and roll back if `Execute` returns `false` or errors; `Select` and `SetCamera` apply after `Execute` succeeds, outside the undo step.

name: PluginEvent
documentation: PluginEvent describes one viewport input event passed to `ToolSpec.Modal`.

name: PluginHit
documentation: PluginHit describes where a PluginEvent cursor ray hits an unlocked part within 1000 units. Local coordinates are in units from the part's center along its unscaled axes.

name: ProductReceipt
documentation: ProductReceipt describes a consumable purchase passed to `Marketplace.ProcessReceipt`.

name: ProductType
documentation: ProductType is a token from `Marketplace.ProductType` passed to `Marketplace.PromptProductPurchase`: `Consumable` (repeatable receipt), `Durable` (permanent unlock), or `Subscription` (recurring access).
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local VIP_PASS = 9012

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Instance)
    if not game.Marketplace.OwnsProduct(player, VIP_PASS) then
        game.Marketplace.PromptProductPurchase(
            player,
            VIP_PASS,
            game.Marketplace.ProductType.Durable
        )
    end
end)

name: Query
documentation: Query matches entities by component or relationship and exposes their values as `QueryColumn` handles. Create one with `World.Query`, then call `Refresh` or pass it to `World.System`.

name: QueryColumn
documentation: QueryColumn reads and writes one value per entity matched by a `Query`, indexed from `1` to `Query.count`. Read and write single-field components (`Position`, `Velocity`, `Scale`) directly at `column[i]`; for multi-field components (`Timer`, `Light`, `UIRect`), index the field name first (`query.Timer.WaitTime[i]`).
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Position = Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)
self:AddComponent("Timer")
self.WaitTime = 2

local timed = game.World.Query("Position", "Timer")
for i = 1, timed:Refresh() do
    timed.Position[i] = timed.Position[i] + Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)
    timed.Timer.WaitTime[i] = 5
end
print(math.round(self.Position.Y), self.WaitTime) -- prints 10  5

name: QueryParams
documentation: QueryParams filters colliders tested by `Physics.Raycast`, `Physics.OverlapSphere`, `Physics.OverlapBox`, and `Physics.Shapecast`. Each instance in `ExcludeInstances` or `IncludeInstances` matches itself and its descendants; if an instance matches both, `ExcludeInstances` wins.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Name = "Crate"
self.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
task.wait()

local origin = Vector3.new(0, 5, 10)
local aim = Vector3.new(0, 0, -1)
local hit = game.Physics.Raycast(origin, aim, 20, { IncludeInstances = { self } })
local skipped = game.Physics.Raycast(origin, aim, 20, { ExcludeInstances = { self } })
print(hit and hit.Instance and hit.Instance.Name, skipped) -- prints Crate  nil

name: RaycastResult
documentation: RaycastResult describes a hit from `Physics.Raycast`.

name: Rect
documentation: Rect creates a 2D rectangle from the pixel positions of two corners, such as an image's `SliceCenter`. In `CornerRadii`, the four numbers are the top-left, top-right, bottom-right and bottom-left corner radii. To read a rectangle, see `Rect`.

name: Rect
documentation: Rect is an immutable 2D rectangle `(minX, minY, maxX, maxY)` in pixels, created with `Rect.new`.

name: RibbonSpec
documentation: RibbonSpec configures a button group passed to plugin:Ribbon.

name: ScriptCost
documentation: ScriptCost reports per-script callback timings from `Profiler.Scripts`.

name: ShapecastHit
documentation: ShapecastHit describes one contact along a sweep from `Physics.Shapecast`.

name: Signal
documentation: Signal runs functions when something happens in the game. Built-in signals include instance properties such as `Touched`; `Instance:GetSignal` returns a named signal of your own.

name: SignalConnection
documentation: SignalConnection is a subscription from `Signal:Connect` or `Signal:Once`.

name: Store
documentation: Store reads and writes per-key tables in a local server save file opened with `Store.open`; see `Store` for file paths. Keys are integers from `0` to `2^53` or decimal digit strings, up to 4,096 unique keys per store.

name: SubscriptionStatus
documentation: SubscriptionStatus describes a player's subscription from `Marketplace.GetSubscriptionStatus`.

name: SwingTwistJointDesc
documentation: SwingTwistJointDesc configures a swing-twist joint for the deprecated `Instance:SetSwingTwistJoint` method. Set the `SwingTwistJoint` properties on `Instance` directly instead.

name: SwingTwistJointInfo
documentation: SwingTwistJointInfo holds the joint settings returned by the deprecated `Instance:GetSwingTwistJoint` method. Read the `SwingTwistJoint` properties on `Instance` directly instead.

name: ToolSpec
documentation: ToolSpec configures a viewport tool passed to plugin:Tool.

name: TouchEvent
documentation: TouchEvent records a contact change from `Physics.DrainTouchEvents`.

name: Tween
documentation: Tween controls a running property animation from `Tween.TweenProperty`; see `Tween` for tweenable types and frame timing.

name: UDim
documentation: UDim creates one axis of an interface size or position: a share of the parent's size plus pixels. To read one, see `UDim`.

name: UDim
documentation: UDim is an immutable single-axis UI coordinate of parent-relative `Scale` plus pixel `Offset` from `UDim.new`.
code_sample:
-- Client script in a part.
local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
bar.UIRect.Size = UDim2.new(0.75, -8, 0, 12)
local x = bar.UIRect.Size.X
print(x.Scale, x.Offset) -- prints 0.75 -8

name: UDim2
documentation: UDim2 creates the position or size of an interface element. Each axis is a scale, a share of the parent's size where 1 is 100%, plus an offset in pixels. To read one, see `UDim2`.

name: UDim2
documentation: UDim2 is an immutable 2D UI coordinate of `X` and `Y` `UDim` axes, created with `UDim2.new`, `UDim2.fromScale`, or `UDim2.fromOffset`.
code_sample:
-- Client script in a part.
local panel = Instance.new("Frame")
panel.UIRect.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, -100, 0, 24)
print(panel.UIRect.Position.X.Scale, panel.UIRect.Position.Y.Offset) -- prints 0.5  24

name: Vector2
documentation: Vector2 creates 2D vectors for interface positions and texture coordinates. A 2D vector is a Luau `vector` with `Z` set to 0, so it has the properties, methods and operators of a `Vector3`.

name: Vector3
documentation: Vector3 creates 3D vectors for positions, directions and sizes, in units. A vector is a Luau `vector`: read `X`, `Y` and `Z`, its length as `Magnitude` and its direction as `Unit`, and call `:Dot`, `:Cross` and `:Lerp` with a colon. Arithmetic works one component at a time, and `*` and `/` also scale by a number. Luau's `vector` library works on these values too; read `Unit` rather than `vector.normalize` when a vector can be zero, because `Vector3.zero.Unit` is `Vector3.zero` while `vector.normalize(Vector3.zero)` is NaN.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local offset = Vector3.new(3, 0, 4)
print(offset.Magnitude) -- prints 5
print(offset:Dot(Vector3.xAxis)) -- prints 3
self.Position = self.Position + offset.Unit * 10

name: World
documentation: World is the top of the place's tree of parts and entities. It also runs queries over scene entities and schedules per-frame systems. The server and each client have their own world, and a call acts on the world of the side that makes it.

name: geometry
documentation: geometry splits flat 2D outlines into triangles, for meshes a script builds.

name: handles
documentation: `handles` is a table of the instances picked for the script's instance in Studio, keyed by slot name. The engine fills it once, when the script starts: a slot with no target or an already-destroyed target is `nil`, while a target destroyed later stays in the table as a destroyed instance.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part with handle slots Door and Switch.
local door = handles.Door
local switch = handles.Switch
if not door or not switch then
    return
end

switch.Touched:Connect(function()
    door.Transparency = 0.5
    door.Position = door.Position + Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)
end)

name: print
documentation: print writes its arguments, separated by tabs, to Output and the in-game console (F9). A game server sends players' consoles at most 256 lines or 32768 bytes a second from server scripts and drops the rest.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
print("score", 10, true) -- prints score    10  true

name: rotation
documentation: rotation builds, combines and converts rotation vectors. Each vector points along the axis of the turn, and its length is the angle in radians. A positive angle turns counterclockwise as seen from the tip of the axis. An unrotated instance faces -Z, with +Y up. `Orientation` is in degrees, so convert with to_euler and from_euler, or use RotationVector and PivotTo, which take rotation vectors.

name: self
documentation: `self` is the instance that runs the script, usually the part the script is attached to. Every script on that instance gets the same `self`. In a script under `scripts/autorun/`, `self` is `nil`; see scripts that run for the whole place.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: the part disappears when something touches it.
self.Touched:Connect(function()
    self:Destroy()
end)

name: shared
documentation: `shared` is a table that all server scripts, or all client scripts of one player, read and write. It works like `_G`, except that reading an unset name gives `nil` instead of a built-in global.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
shared.SpawnInterval = shared.SpawnInterval or 2
print(shared.print) -- prints nil

name: task
documentation: task runs functions later or in their own threads, and pauses the running thread. Scheduled threads belong to the calling script: the engine drops them if the script reloads or its instance is destroyed. Waits and delays count update ticks, so they end on the first tick at or after the time.

name: tick
documentation: tick returns the time in seconds from a clock that only moves forward. Subtract two readings to measure how long something took.
code_sample:
-- Server script: time a loop.
local start = tick()
local sum = 0
for i = 1, 100000 do
    sum += i
end
print("took", tick() - start, "seconds")

name: warn
documentation: warn writes its arguments to the output as a warning, like `print`. The script keeps running.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local config: { [string]: number } = { MaxPlayers = 8 }
if config.SpawnInterval == nil then
    warn("SpawnInterval is missing; using 2 seconds")
end

name: clip
documentation: clip is the name of the previewed clip, or nil if the clip has no name.

name: playing
documentation: playing is true while the preview plays and false while it is paused.

name: shared
documentation: shared is true if something else changed the character's pose after the preview set it.

name: speed
documentation: speed is the playback multiplier from 0 to 10; 1 is normal speed.

name: time
documentation: time is the preview's position in the clip, in seconds.

name: fetch
type: function fetch(self, key: number | string, callback: (any, number, string?) -> ()): ()
documentation: fetch loads the table saved under a key. The callback gets the table, its version and nil; `(nil, 0, nil)` if the key has no record; or an error string as the third value if the request failed.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local profiles = game.CloudStore.open("profiles")

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Instance)
    profiles:fetch(player.UserId, function(data, version, err)
        if err then
            warn("could not load profile: " .. err)
            return
        end
        player.attr.Gold = if data then data.gold else 0
    end)
end)

name: keys
type: function keys(self, after: string?, limit: number?, callback: ({string}, string?) -> ()): ()
documentation: keys lists the keys of the store in key order, at most `limit` (up to 100) per call. Pass the last key of one page as `after` to get the next page.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local profiles = game.CloudStore.open("profiles")

local function listFrom(after: string?)
    profiles:keys(after, 100, function(keys, err)
        for _, key in keys do
            print(key)
        end
        if not err and #keys == 100 then
            listFrom(keys[#keys])
        end
    end)
end

listFrom(nil)

name: put
type: function put(self, key: number | string, value: {[string]: any}, expect_version: number?, callback: ((number?, string?) -> ())?): ()
documentation: put saves a table under a key, replacing the record there. Pass a version from `fetch` as `expect_version` to fail with `"conflict"` if another server wrote first, or nil to write regardless. The callback gets the new version, or nil and an error string.

name: remove
type: function remove(self, key: number | string, callback: ((boolean, string?) -> ())?): ()
documentation: remove deletes the record saved under a key. The callback gets true if a record was deleted.
code_sample:
-- Server script: delete the profile of user 42.
local profiles = game.CloudStore.open("profiles")

profiles:remove(42)

name: update
type: function update(self, key: number | string, transform: (any, number) -> any, callback: ((number?, string?) -> ())?): ()
documentation: update loads a record, passes it to `transform`, and saves the table `transform` returns, or nothing if it returns nil. If another server saved the key in between, `transform` runs again on the newer record, up to 3 more times, so keep it free of other effects.

name: fromHSV
type: (hue: number, saturation: number, value: number) -> vector
documentation: `Color3.fromHSV` creates a color from hue, saturation and value, each from 0 to 1. Hue goes around the color wheel from red (0) through green (0.33) and blue (0.67), and wraps past 1.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: cycle through the rainbow every 5 seconds.
local hue = 0

function Update(dt: number)
    hue = (hue + dt / 5) % 1
    self.Color = Color3.fromHSV(hue, 1, 1)
end

name: fromHex
documentation: `Color3.fromHex` creates a color from a six-digit hex code, with or without a leading `#`. The short form `"#F80"` is an error.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Color = Color3.fromHex("#FF8800")

name: fromRGB
type: (r: number?, g: number?, b: number?) -> vector
documentation: `Color3.fromRGB` creates a color from red, green and blue from 0 to 255, the scale of color pickers.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Color = Color3.fromRGB(255, 170, 0)
print(Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0)) -- prints 1, 0, 0

name: new
type: (r: number?, g: number?, b: number?) -> vector
documentation: `Color3.new` creates a color from red, green and blue, each from 0 to 1.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Color = Color3.new(1, 0.5, 0)
print(self.Color) -- prints 1, 0.5, 0

name: Keypoints
documentation: Keypoints is a new array of the sequence's 2 to 8 keypoints in time order.

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns true if both sequences have the same keypoints.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns the time, red, green and blue of each keypoint.

name: new
documentation: `ColorSequence.new` creates a sequence of one color, a blend from `c0` to `c1`, or a sequence from a list of `ColorSequenceKeypoint` values. A list must start at time 0, end at time 1 and be in time order.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: sparks that fade from yellow to red.
local sparks = Instance.new("Sparks")
sparks:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleColorRamp")
sparks.ParticleColorRamp.Color = ColorSequence.new(Color3.new(1, 1, 0), Color3.new(1, 0, 0))
sparks.Parent = self

name: Time
documentation: Time is the keypoint's position on the curve, from 0 at the start to 1 at the end.

name: Value
documentation: Value is the color at `Time`, as a vector of red, green and blue.

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns true if both keypoints have the same time and color.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns the time, red, green and blue.

name: new
documentation: `ColorSequenceKeypoint.new` creates a keypoint with `color` at `time`, from 0 to 1.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local flames = Instance.new("Flames")
flames:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleColorRamp")
flames.ParticleColorRamp.Color = ColorSequence.new({
    ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0, Color3.new(1, 0.9, 0.4)),
    ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(0.4, Color3.new(1, 0.4, 0)),
    ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(1, Color3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2)),
})
flames.Parent = self

name: __iter
documentation: __iter visits every field of the component in declaration order, with its name and current value.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent("Timer")
local timer = self:Component("Timer")
if timer then
    timer.WaitTime = 5
    for name, value in timer do
        print(name .. " = " .. tostring(value))
    end
end
-- prints WaitTime = 5, then TimeLeft = 0

name: Id
documentation: Id is the asset id as a string of decimal digits.

name: IsValid
documentation: IsValid returns true while the asset is still in memory.
code_sample:
-- Server script: spawn the obstacle course again each round.
local course: ContentAsset? = nil

game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset)
    course = asset
end)

while true do
    task.wait(60)
    if course and course:IsValid() then
        game.Content.Spawn(course)
    end
end

name: Size
documentation: Size is the size of the downloaded asset in bytes.

name: Type
documentation: Type is the kind of asset: `"scene"`, `"texture"`, `"audio"`, `"mesh"`, or `"unknown"`. `Content.Spawn` spawns only `"scene"` assets.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset)
    if asset and asset.Type == "scene" then
        game.Content.Spawn(asset)
    end
end)

name: Cancel
documentation: Cancel stops the request, so its callback never runs. It does nothing if the request has already finished.
code_sample:
-- Server script: give up if the course has not loaded in 30 seconds.
local request = game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset)
    if asset then
        game.Content.Spawn(asset)
    end
end)

task.wait(30)
request:Cancel()

name: Pending
documentation: Pending is true until the request finishes or is cancelled.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local request = game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset)
    if asset then
        game.Content.Spawn(asset)
    end
end)

task.wait(10)
if request.Pending then
    warn("the obstacle course is still loading")
end

name: WriteIndices
type: (self: DynamicMesh, data: buffer, offset: number, start: number, count: number) -> ()

name: WriteVertices
type: (self: DynamicMesh, data: buffer, offset: number, start: number, count: number) -> ()

name: new
documentation: `DynamicMesh.new` creates an empty mesh.
code_sample:
-- Client script: a 4 by 4 unit floor tile.
local mesh = DynamicMesh.new()
mesh:SetCounts(4, 6)

local vBuf = buffer.create(4 * 32)
local function writeVertex(
    idx: number,
    x: number,
    y: number,
    z: number,
    u: number,
    v: number,
    nx: number,
    ny: number,
    nz: number
)
    local base = idx * 32
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 0, x)
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 4, y)
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 8, z)
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 12, u)
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 16, v)
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 20, nx)
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 24, ny)
    buffer.writef32(vBuf, base + 28, nz)
end

writeVertex(0, -2, 0, -2, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0)
writeVertex(1, 2, 0, -2, 1, 0, 0, 1, 0)
writeVertex(2, 2, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0)
writeVertex(3, -2, 0, 2, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0)

local iBuf = buffer.create(6 * 4)
local indices = { 0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 2 }
for i, vertIdx in indices do
    buffer.writeu32(iBuf, (i - 1) * 4, vertIdx)
end

mesh:WriteVertices(vBuf, 0, 0, 4)
mesh:WriteIndices(iBuf, 0, 0, 6)

local platform = Instance.new("Platform")
platform.Position = Vector3.new(0, 1, 10)
mesh:Apply(platform)

name: FireAllClients
documentation: FireAllClients sends an event from the server to every player.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local RoundStarted = game.EventTable("RoundStarted", game.EventTable.ToClients, {})

task.wait(5)
RoundStarted:FireAllClients()

name: FireClient
documentation: FireClient sends an event from the server to one player.

name: FireServer
documentation: FireServer sends an event from a client script to the server, with one value per declared field.
code_sample:
-- Client script. The server declares Buy with one String field.
local Buy = game.EventTable("Buy")

Buy:FireServer("Speed")

name: OnClientEvent
documentation: OnClientEvent is a Signal that runs on a client once for each event the server sent to it, with the field values.
code_sample:
-- Client script in a text label. The server declares Notice
-- with one String field.
local Notice = game.EventTable("Notice")

Notice.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(text: string)
    self.Text = text
end)

name: OnServerEvent
documentation: OnServerEvent is a Signal that runs on the server once for each event a client sent, with the sending player and then the field values. Handlers run before `Update`, and skip events whose player has left.

name: Push
documentation: Push sends an event to every client on a `ToClients` table, or to the server on a `ToServer` table.
deprecation: Call `FireServer` from a client script or `FireAllClients` from a server script.

name: PushTo
documentation: PushTo sends an event from the server to the player with a user id.

name: count
documentation: count is the number of events the table received this tick. It is 0 at the top level of a script, so read it in `Update`.

name: sender
documentation: sender is the column of the user id of the player who sent each event. Only server scripts can read it, and only on a `ToServer` table.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local Vote = game.EventTable("Vote", game.EventTable.ToServer, {
    {"choice", game.EventTable.U8},
})

function Update(dt: number)
    for i = 1, Vote.count do
        local player = game.Players.Get(Vote.sender[i])
        if player then
            player.attr.Vote = Vote.choice[i]
        end
    end
end

name: tick
documentation: tick is the column of the server tick of each event, numbered like `game.Session.ServerTick`. On the server, it is the tick of the world the sending player saw when they sent the event.

name: gcAllocKBs
documentation: gcAllocKBs is how fast the Luau heap grows, in kilobytes per second, smoothed over recent frames in which it grew.

name: gcKB
documentation: gcKB is the size of the Luau heap in kilobytes. If it keeps rising, scripts are keeping references to data they are done with.

name: interval
documentation: interval is the time from the start of the previous frame to the start of this one, or 0 on the first frame.

name: network
documentation: network is the time spent sending and receiving network messages.

name: physics
documentation: physics is the time spent on physics.

name: render
documentation: render is the time the client took to prepare its last drawn frame. It is 0 on the server.

name: script
documentation: script is the time spent running Luau scripts. `game.Profiler.Scripts` gives the time per script.

name: sim
documentation: sim is the time spent on game logic: scripts, physics and networking.

name: displayName
documentation: displayName is the player's display name.

name: isAdmin
documentation: isAdmin is true if the player is an admin.

name: userId
documentation: userId is the player's user id.

name: AbsoluteCanvasSize
documentation: AbsoluteCanvasSize is the width and height in pixels of the canvas a scrolling frame scrolls over, as `(Width, Height, 0)`. On a frame with a vertical list or grid layout, the height is the height of its children.

name: AbsolutePosition
documentation: AbsolutePosition is the top-left position of a user interface element on the screen or canvas, in logical pixels: `(X, Y, 0)`.

name: AbsoluteSize
documentation: AbsoluteSize is the width and height of a user interface element in logical pixels: `(Width, Height, 0)`. On `game.World.Screen` it is the size of the viewport.

name: Action
documentation: Action is what a button in the platform's core menu does when pressed; a button elsewhere ignores it. `"Toggle"` opens or closes the core menu and works only on the menu button of the core `TopBar` prefab.

name: Activated
documentation: Activated fires on the client when a click or tap activates this element. On a tool, it fires when the holder uses it, on that client and then on the server with the player and the hit point.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Parent = screen

button.Activated:Connect(function()
    screen.Visible = false
end)

name: ActiveAnimation
documentation: ActiveAnimation returns the name of the clip the character plays, or nil when it plays none.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
npc:PlayAnimation("sit")
task.wait(0.5)
print(npc:ActiveAnimation()) -- prints sit

name: AddAccessory
documentation: AddAccessory puts an accessory (an instance or a `ContentAsset`) on the character and returns it. The accessory needs an `Attachment` with `IsRoot` set; its `Slot` picks the socket.
code_sample:
-- Server script: give a character a hat.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
local hat = Instance.new("Part")
hat.Size = Vector3.new(2, 1, 2)
hat:AddComponent("Attachment")
hat.IsRoot = true
hat.Slot = "Hat"
print(npc:AddAccessory(hat) == hat) -- prints true

name: AddComponent
documentation: AddComponent adds one or more components, built-in or declared by the place, or `Tag` pairs to the instance. Built-in components start with their default values.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent("Light", "SpotCone")
print(self:HasComponent("SpotCone")) -- prints true

name: Adornee
documentation: Adornee is the 3D instance the handles go on. While it is nil, the handles do not show.

name: AdornmentHandles
documentation: create 3D drag handles that report drags on a target

name: AdvancePreview
documentation: AdvancePreview advances a playing animation preview by the time since it last advanced, and returns whether the pose changed. A paused preview does not advance.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local rig = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
rig:PreviewAnimation("walk", true)
task.wait(0.5)
print(rig:AdvancePreview()) -- prints true

name: AirAccelerate
documentation: AirAccelerate is how fast the character speeds up in the air toward the movement keys, in multiples of `WalkSpeed` per second. Turning while strafing keeps adding speed.

name: AirJumps
documentation: AirJumps is how many jumps the character has made in the air since it last landed.

name: AirMaxWishSpeed
documentation: AirMaxWishSpeed is the speed, in units/s, at which holding the movement keys in a straight line in the air stops adding speed. Strafing still builds speed past it.

name: Albedo
documentation: Albedo is the asset id of the texture that gives a mesh its base colors, along the mesh's UV coordinates. `"0"` shows the part's `Color` or its material's textures.

name: Align
documentation: Align places a list's children across the direction it stacks them: `"Start"`, `"Center"` or `"End"`. It is horizontal when `Axis` is `"Vertical"` and vertical when `Axis` is `"Horizontal"`.

name: AmbientLightColor
documentation: AmbientLightColor is the sRGB color of the ambient light, the light that fills shadows and surfaces no light reaches.

name: AmbientLightEnergy
documentation: AmbientLightEnergy is the brightness of the ambient light, from 0 to 16. At 0, surfaces in shadow are dark.

name: AmbientLightSkyContribution
documentation: AmbientLightSkyContribution is how much of the ambient light comes from the sky instead of AmbientLightColor, from 0 to 1. At 1, upward faces get the sky's color and downward faces get light bounced off the ground.

name: AmbientLightSource
documentation: AmbientLightSource is where the ambient light comes from, one of `game.Enum.AmbientSource`:

name: Anchor
documentation: Anchor is the pivot of a swing-twist joint, in units in the parent part's frame. The joint links this part to its parent part and forms when this part has a dynamic body.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: hang a lantern under it that swings up to 30 degrees.
self.Anchored = true

local lantern = Instance.new("Part")
lantern.Size = Vector3.new(1, 2, 1)
lantern.Position = self.Position - Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
lantern.Parent = self
lantern.Anchor = Vector3.new(0, -2, 0)
lantern.TwistAxis = Vector3.new(0, -1, 0)
lantern.PlaneCone = 30
lantern.NormalCone = 30

name: AnchorPoint
documentation: AnchorPoint is the point of the element that its position places, as a fraction of its size: (0, 0) is the top left, (0.5, 0.5) the center and (1, 1) the bottom right.

name: Anchored
documentation: Anchored locks the part in place, so gravity, collisions and forces do not move it. One anchored part makes its whole welded assembly static, but a part welded to a character follows the character even when anchored.

name: Angle
documentation: Angle turns the texture, in degrees, around the UV center (0.5, 0.5).

name: AngularDamping
documentation: AngularDamping is the drag that slows the body's spin. 0 is no drag.

name: AnimLayers
documentation: AnimLayers lists the animation layers that blend together on this character.
code_sample:
-- Server script: blend a looping climb into a character's pose for 2 s.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
local layer = game.Animation.FirstScriptLayer
npc.AnimLayers[layer] = { clip = "climb", weight = 0.5, loop = true }
task.wait(2)
npc.AnimLayers[layer] = nil

name: AnimationPreview
documentation: AnimationPreview returns the open animation preview as a table with `clip`, `time` in seconds, `speed`, `playing` and `shared`, or nil when no preview is open.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local rig = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
rig:PreviewAnimation("walk", false)
local info = assert(rig:AnimationPreview())
print(info.clip) -- prints walk

name: AnimationWeight
documentation: AnimationWeight returns how much of the character's pose a clip makes up, from 0 to 1, or nil when no clip has that name.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
npc:PlayAnimation("sit")
task.wait(1)
print(npc:AnimationWeight("sit")) -- prints 1

name: ApplyForce
documentation: ApplyForce pushes the part with a world-space force for the next physics step. Calls in the same step add up, so a steady push needs a call every step. The optional `at` is the world point where the force acts; without it, the force acts at the center of mass, or at the part's own position when the part is welded to another part. ApplyForce warns and does nothing on a part without a dynamic body, such as an anchored part.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a rocket: push it up with twice its weight.
self.Anchored = false
task.wait()
local thrust = -2 * game.Physics.Gravity * assert(self:GetMass())
while task.wait() do
    self:ApplyForce(Vector3.new(0, thrust, 0))
end

name: ApplyImpulse
documentation: ApplyImpulse gives the part a sudden world-space push that changes its velocity at once. The optional `at` works as for ApplyForce. ApplyImpulse warns and does nothing on a part without a dynamic body.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a ball: kick it up at 50 units per second.
self.Anchored = false
task.wait()
self:ApplyImpulse(Vector3.new(0, 50 * assert(self:GetMass()), 0))

name: ApplyTorque
documentation: ApplyTorque twists the part with a torque for the next physics step.
deprecation: Attach `SubstepTorque` with Instance:AddComponent and write the `SubstepTorque` column on World.Query.

name: ApplyTorqueImpulse
documentation: ApplyTorqueImpulse gives the part a sudden world-space twist that changes its spin at once. It warns and does nothing on a part without a dynamic body.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a spinning top.
self.Anchored = false
task.wait()
self:ApplyTorqueImpulse(Vector3.new(0, 50, 0))

name: Area
documentation: Area is the wing area in square units. Every physics step, lift is `0.5 * air density * Area * speed ^ 2 * C_L` and drag is the same with `C_D`. `speed` is only the airflow across the span (the part's X axis); the chord runs along -Z and lift acts toward the part's +Y. On an assembly member the forces push the whole assembly.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a flat wing part, so it glides instead of dropping.
self.Size = Vector3.new(8, 0.2, 2)
self:AddComponent("AeroSurface")
self.Area = 16
self.Velocity = Vector3.new(0, 0, -60)

name: ArrowDirection
documentation: ArrowDirection is the direction the button's arrow points: `"Left"`, `"Right"`, `"Up"` or `"Down"`.

name: AspectRatio
documentation: AspectRatio is the element's width divided by its height; 0 keeps the shape that `Size` gives. The element takes the largest box of this ratio that fits in its `Size`, so `Size = UDim2.new(0.2, 0, 0.2, 0)` with `AspectRatio = 1` is a square on any screen.

name: Assembly
documentation: Assembly makes a Model one rigid body when true. A plain model is a group.

name: Asset
documentation: Asset is the asset id the accessory was spawned from, or `"0"` for an accessory built in the place.

name: Attacker
documentation: Attacker is the instance that last damaged the character with `TakeDamage`, or nil.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a trap part.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:TakeDamage(10, self)
print(npc.Attacker == self) -- prints true

name: AttributeChanged
documentation: AttributeChanged fires with the attribute name when an attribute in `attr` changes or is removed, by a script or by the server.
notes: The engine compares attributes once per tick, before `Update` runs. Several writes to one name in a tick fire once, writing the same value again does not fire, and a change made while nothing is connected does not fire later.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.AttributeChanged:Connect(function(name)
    print(name, self.attr[name])
end)
self.attr.Coins = 5
self.attr.Coins = 7 -- same tick: fires once, prints Coins 7

name: AutoLocomotion
documentation: AutoLocomotion plays the character's walk, idle and jump animations from how it moves. It needs CharacterAnimation.

name: AutoRotate
documentation: AutoRotate turns the character to face the direction it walks. Shift lock turns it toward the camera direction instead.

name: Axis
documentation: Axis is the direction a list stacks its children: `"Vertical"` top to bottom, or `"Horizontal"` left to right.

name: Axle
documentation: Axle is the direction the wheel spins around, in the wheel's own frame. The default spins a `Cylinder` wheel the way it rolls.

name: BackgroundColor
documentation: BackgroundColor is the sRGB color behind everything when the Environment has no `AtmosphereSky`, `PanoramaSky` or `SixSidedSky`.

name: BackgroundColor3
documentation: BackgroundColor3 is the fill color of the element's background.

name: BackgroundEnergyMultiplier
documentation: BackgroundEnergyMultiplier is the brightness, from 0 to 16, of the background color and of panorama and six-sided skies. The atmosphere sky ignores it.

name: BackgroundMode
documentation: BackgroundMode is whether the Environment draws a sky or clears to BackgroundColor.
deprecation: Add `AtmosphereSky`, `PanoramaSky` or `SixSidedSky` with Instance:AddComponent, or remove them with Instance:RemoveComponent.

name: BackgroundTransparency
documentation: BackgroundTransparency is the transparency of the element's background, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: BackpackChanged
documentation: BackpackChanged fires on a character when its hotbar changes: a tool enters or leaves a slot, the held tool changes, or a slotted tool's `Tool.icon` or `Name` changes. Several changes in one tick fire it once. See Tools.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc.BackpackChanged:Connect(function()
    local tool = npc:GetTool()
    print("holding " .. (if tool then tool.Name else "nothing")) -- prints holding Tool
end)
npc:EquipTool(Instance.new("Tool"))

name: BarWidth
documentation: BarWidth is the width in pixels of the hue strip along the right edge of a color picker.

name: BillboardColor
documentation: BillboardColor is the text color of the camera-facing 3D billboard label.

name: BillboardGui
documentation: create a camera-facing interface surface

name: BillboardMaxDistance
documentation: BillboardMaxDistance is how far from the camera, in world units, the billboard text shows; it fades out near this distance. 0 shows it at any distance.

name: BillboardOffset
documentation: BillboardOffset is the center of the billboard text, in world units from the instance's position.

name: BillboardOnTop
documentation: BillboardOnTop, when true, draws the billboard text in front of everything.

name: BillboardScreenSize
documentation: BillboardScreenSize is the part of the text height in screen points, the same at any distance. It adds to BillboardWorldSize.

name: BillboardText
documentation: BillboardText is the text of the camera-facing 3D billboard label. An empty string hides the label.

name: BillboardWorldSize
documentation: BillboardWorldSize is the part of the text height in world units, which looks smaller farther away. It adds to BillboardScreenSize.

name: BodyColorHead
documentation: BodyColorHead is the color of the `Head` part when the part has no `Color` of its own. Until a script sets it, the head keeps its default color.

name: BodyColorLeftArm
documentation: BodyColorLeftArm is the color of the `LeftArm` part when the part has no `Color` of its own. Until a script sets it, the left arm keeps its default color.

name: BodyColorLeftLeg
documentation: BodyColorLeftLeg is the color of the `LeftLeg` part when the part has no `Color` of its own. Until a script sets it, the left leg keeps its default color.

name: BodyColorRightArm
documentation: BodyColorRightArm is the color of the `RightArm` part when the part has no `Color` of its own. Until a script sets it, the right arm keeps its default color.

name: BodyColorRightLeg
documentation: BodyColorRightLeg is the color of the `RightLeg` part when the part has no `Color` of its own. Until a script sets it, the right leg keeps its default color.

name: BodyColorTorso
documentation: BodyColorTorso is the color of the `Torso` part when the part has no `Color` of its own. Until a script sets it, the torso keeps its default color.

name: BodyHead
documentation: BodyHead is the asset id of the head mesh, or `"0"` for the bundled mesh.

name: BodyLeftArm
documentation: BodyLeftArm is the asset id of the left arm mesh, or `"0"` for the bundled mesh.

name: BodyLeftLeg
documentation: BodyLeftLeg is the asset id of the left leg mesh, or `"0"` for the bundled mesh.

name: BodyRightArm
documentation: BodyRightArm is the asset id of the right arm mesh, or `"0"` for the bundled mesh.

name: BodyRightLeg
documentation: BodyRightLeg is the asset id of the right leg mesh, or `"0"` for the bundled mesh.

name: BodyTorso
documentation: BodyTorso is the asset id of the torso mesh, or `"0"` for the bundled mesh.

name: Bold
documentation: Bold reads true when FontWeight is 600 or more. Writing true sets `FontWeight` to 700 and false sets it to 400.

name: BorderColor3
documentation: BorderColor3 is the color of the border around the element.

name: BorderFocusOnly
documentation: BorderFocusOnly, when true, draws the border only while a text box on or inside the element is typed in or is `game.Input.Selected`. That text box then draws no selection ring, so a search field shows one outline around the whole field.

name: BorderSizePixel
documentation: BorderSizePixel is the width in pixels of the border, drawn inside the element's edges; 0 draws none.

name: BorderTransparency
documentation: BorderTransparency is the transparency of the border, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: BoxColor3
documentation: BoxColor3 is the fill color of a checkbox's box.

name: BoxTransparency
documentation: BoxTransparency is the transparency of a checkbox's box, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: BranchColor3
documentation: BranchColor3 is the color of the lines that join parent and child nodes in a tree view.

name: BranchTransparency
documentation: BranchTransparency is the transparency of the tree view lines.

name: BreakForce
documentation: BreakForce is the reaction force in Newtons that breaks the part's weld or assembly link. When a physics step pulls harder, the part and the members below it fly off as one body. 0 never breaks, and a weld to a character never breaks.

name: BreakLink
documentation: BreakLink breaks the part off its parent or weld target. The part and everything welded under it fly on as one body at the velocity of the link point, and the part keeps its place in the hierarchy.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: weld a wing to it, then break the wing off.
local wing = Instance.new("Part")
wing.Position = self.Position + Vector3.new(3, 0, 0)
wing.Parent = game.World
wing.Other = self

task.wait(1)
wing:BreakLink()
print(wing.Other) -- prints nil

name: BreakTorque
documentation: BreakTorque is the reaction torque in Newton-meters that breaks the part's weld or assembly link, as BreakForce does for force.

name: Brightness
documentation: Brightness is the value (the V of HSV) picked in a color picker, from 0 (black) to 1. Dragging up or down changes it.

name: Bus
documentation: Bus is the mix bus the sound plays through: `"Master"`, `"Music"`, `"SFX"` or `"UI"`. The sound plays at `Volume * bus volume * Master volume`, and on `"Master"` the Master volume counts once.

name: BusyColor3
documentation: BusyColor3 is the color of the moving segment of a busy progress bar, one that shows work with no known end.

name: BusySpeed
documentation: BusySpeed is how many times a second a busy progress bar sweeps. Positive values sweep left to right, negative values sweep right to left, and 0 stops it.

name: BusyTransparency
documentation: BusyTransparency is the transparency of the moving segment of a busy progress bar.

name: BusyWidth
documentation: BusyWidth is the width of the moving segment as a fraction of the bar's width, drawn clamped to 0 to 1.

name: Camera
documentation: create a camera with the default lens

name: CameraFly
documentation: free-camera yaw, pitch, and zoom controls

name: CameraLens
documentation: perspective projection settings for a camera entity

name: CameraOrbit
documentation: third-person orbit camera controls; smoothed fields are written by the rig

name: CancelText
documentation: CancelText is the cancel button text; empty shows Cancel.

name: Canceled
documentation: Canceled fires when the player cancels the dialog.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local ui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
ui.Parent = game.Overlay
local dialog = Instance.new("Frame")
dialog.DialogTitle = "Quit"
dialog.Parent = ui
dialog.Canceled:Connect(function() print("stay") end)

name: CanvasPosition
documentation: CanvasPosition is the vertical scroll offset of a scrolling frame in pixels, as `(0, Y, 0)`. Writing it scrolls the frame, and a `ScrollFollowing` frame then stops following until the player scrolls back to the end.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local pane = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
pane.CanvasSize = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 1000)
pane.Parent = screen

-- Back to the top after swapping pages.
pane.CanvasPosition = Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)
print(pane.CanvasPosition.Y) -- prints 0

name: CanvasSize
documentation: CanvasSize is the size of the area a scrolling frame scrolls over. When the area is wider or taller than the frame, the frame scrolls that way.

name: CaptureFocus
documentation: CaptureFocus puts keyboard focus on this text box, so the player types into it. A box that gains focus fires Focused.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local box = Instance.new("TextBox")
box.Parent = screen
box:CaptureFocus()

name: CellPadding
documentation: CellPadding is the gap in pixels between neighboring cells of a grid, across and down.

name: CellSize
documentation: CellSize is the width and height in pixels of each cell of a grid. The grid's children take this size instead of their own.

name: CenterOfPressure
documentation: CenterOfPressure is the point where lift and drag act, in the part's frame relative to its position. An offset from the center of mass makes lift and drag turn the body.

name: ChangeState
documentation: ChangeState puts a character into a movement state at its next physics step, so `State` keeps the old name until then. A `"Ragdoll"` character goes limp and gets up once it is at rest after at least 1 second, or after 8 seconds; a `"FallingDown"` character gets up after 3 seconds. These are the defaults of the place's character tuning.
code_sample:
-- Server script: knock a character over.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:ChangeState("Ragdoll")
print(npc.State) -- prints FreeFall
task.wait(0.1)
print(npc.State) -- prints Ragdoll

name: Changed
documentation: Changed fires on the client when the player edits the text of this text box, with the property name `"Text"`. Script writes do not fire it; use GetPropertyChangedSignal for those.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local box = Instance.new("TextBox")
box.Parent = screen
local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Parent = screen
box.Changed:Connect(function(property)
    if property == "Text" then
        label.Text = box.Text
    end
end)

name: Character
documentation: Character is the character this instance is or controls: a player gives its character, a character root gives itself, a body part gives its character root, and any other instance gives nil.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: kill any character that touches it.
self.Touched:Connect(function(hit: Instance)
    local character = hit.Character
    if character then
        character.Health = 0
    end
end)

name: Character
documentation: Character is the character this instance is or controls: a player gives its character, a character root gives itself, a body part gives its character root, and any other instance gives nil.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: kill any character that touches it.
self.Touched:Connect(function(hit: Instance)
    local character = hit.Character
    if character then
        character.Health = 0
    end
end)

name: CharacterAdded
documentation: CharacterAdded fires when a character spawns for this player, on the first spawn and on every respawn. The callback receives the character. On a client it does not fire for a character that existed before the client scripts started; read `player.Character` instead.

name: CharacterAnimation
documentation: CharacterAnimation animates the body parts under the character root. A part without `BodyPart` is not animated: it moves with the torso and never collides with it.

name: CharacterPhysics
documentation: CharacterPhysics gives the torso a physics body so the character moves under physics. The character controller also needs `Locomotion`; without it the instance is an ordinary physics body.
code_sample:
-- Server script: make a block that walks like a character.
local mob = Instance.new("Mob")
mob:AddComponent("Shape")
mob.Size = Vector3.new(2, 3, 2)
mob:AddComponent("CharacterPhysics")
mob:AddComponent("Locomotion")
mob.WalkSpeed = 8

name: CharacterRig
documentation: CharacterRig gives the limbs physics bodies that follow the torso and the animation. It needs CharacterPhysics. The limbs collide only in the `"Ragdoll"`, `"FallingDown"` and `"Dead"` states.

name: CharacterSurfaceAlign
documentation: CharacterSurfaceAlign turns UpDirection toward the normal of the floor the character stands on, so it can walk up walls. It needs GravityVector.

name: Chassis
documentation: Chassis is the body this wheel hangs from. The wheel spins around `Axle` and moves up and down `Travel` units on a spring; it does not collide with its chassis. The joint forms only between parts with physics bodies in different assemblies, and setting nil or destroying either part removes it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a level car body part: put a wheel under each corner and drive.
local corners = {
    Vector3.new(-3.5, -1, 4), Vector3.new(3.5, -1, 4),
    Vector3.new(-3.5, -1, -4), Vector3.new(3.5, -1, -4),
}
for _, corner in corners do
    local wheel = Instance.new("Cylinder")
    wheel.Size = Vector3.new(2.4, 1, 2.4)
    wheel.Position = self.Position + corner
    wheel.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 0, 90)
    wheel.Parent = game.World
    wheel.Chassis = self
    wheel.DriveTorque = 2000
    wheel.SpinSpeed = 10
end

name: Chatted
documentation: Chatted fires on the server when this player sends a chat message. The callback receives the message text.

name: CheckColor3
documentation: CheckColor3 is the color of a checkbox's check mark.

name: CheckTransparency
documentation: CheckTransparency is the transparency of the check mark, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: Checked
documentation: Checked, when true, shows the checkbox's check mark. Clicking the checkbox flips it and fires `Activated`.

name: ChildAdded
documentation: ChildAdded fires with the child when an instance becomes a direct child of this one: a new instance, a moved one, a clone or a child that replicates from the server. Deeper descendants do not fire it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
    print("added " .. child.Name) -- prints added Lamp
end)
local lamp = Instance.new("Part")
lamp.Name = "Lamp"
lamp.Parent = self

name: ChildRemoved
documentation: ChildRemoved fires with the child when a direct child moves to another parent or is destroyed. A destroyed child cannot be indexed, but it is still the same table key, so a script can use it to clean up.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local lamp = Instance.new("Part")
lamp.Name = "Lamp"
lamp.Parent = self

self.ChildRemoved:Connect(function(child)
    print(child == lamp) -- prints true
end)
lamp:Destroy()

name: CircleColor3
documentation: CircleColor3 is the color of a radio button's outer ring.

name: CircleTransparency
documentation: CircleTransparency is the transparency of a radio button's outer ring, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: Climbable
documentation: Climbable makes characters that walk into the part climb it, as on a ladder. A character climbs a moving ladder as if the ladder stood still and rides along when it holds still.

name: ClipsDescendants
documentation: ClipsDescendants, when true, cuts off the elements under this one at its edges.

name: Clone
documentation: Clone returns a copy of the instance and all its descendants. The copy has a new id and no parent until you set one.
notes: The copy keeps the attributes and tags of the original and runs its own copy of every script attached to it, with `self` set to the copy. A script that clones the part it runs on therefore also runs in the clone and clones again.
The copy has no `SessionOwner`, so a cloned character belongs to no player and `player.Character` stays on the original.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.Name = "Crate"
crate.Parent = game.World

local copy = crate:Clone()
copy.Parent = game.World
copy.Position = crate.Position + Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
print(copy.Name, copy == crate) -- prints Crate false

name: CloudAnisotropy
documentation: CloudAnisotropy is which way clouds scatter sunlight. Positive values make clouds brightest when the camera looks toward the sun, negative values when the sun is behind the camera, and 0 scatters evenly. Values are clamped to `[-0.98, 0.98]`.

name: CloudBaseHeight
documentation: CloudBaseHeight is the height, in units above y = 0, of the bottom of the cloud layer, from 1 to 100000. A higher base also makes the cloud shapes larger.

name: CloudBottomDarkening
documentation: CloudBottomDarkening is how much darker cloud bottoms are than their tops, from 0 to 1.

name: CloudColor
documentation: CloudColor tints the clouds.

name: CloudCoverage
documentation: CloudCoverage is how much of the sky the clouds cover, from 0 (clear) to 1 (an unbroken layer); around 0.3 gives scattered patches.

name: CloudDensity
documentation: CloudDensity is how thick the cloud is per unit of distance, from 0 to 1. 0 makes clouds invisible. Values from about 0.005 to 0.02 give white clouds; higher values turn them gray and then storm dark.

name: CloudErosion
documentation: CloudErosion is how much cloud edges break into wisps, clamped to `[0, 0.99]`. At 0 clouds keep smooth shapes.

name: CloudEvolutionSpeed
documentation: CloudEvolutionSpeed is how fast the clouds change shape, from 0 to 100, apart from drifting with the wind. At 0 they keep their shape.

name: CloudMultipleScattering
documentation: CloudMultipleScattering is how much light bounces inside the clouds, from 0 to 2. Higher values lighten the inside of thick clouds.

name: CloudPowderStrength
documentation: CloudPowderStrength is how much the thin edges of thick clouds brighten against the sun, from 0 to 2. 0 turns it off.

name: CloudQuality
documentation: CloudQuality is how many steps the renderer takes through the clouds per pixel: 0 is 16 steps, 1 is 24, and 2 or more is 32. Graphics quality Levels 3 to 5 always take 16 steps, and Levels 9 and 10 take 64 in place of 32.

name: CloudSeed
documentation: CloudSeed is a whole number from 0 to 2147483647 that picks the random layout of the clouds.

name: CloudShadowStrength
documentation: CloudShadowStrength is how dark cloud shadows on the ground are, from 0 to 4. 0 casts no cloud shadows, and 1 casts the physical shadow.

name: CloudThickness
documentation: CloudThickness is how tall the cloud layer is, in units from 1 to 50000. Low values make flat sheets and high values let clouds tower.

name: CloudWindSpeed
documentation: CloudWindSpeed is how fast the clouds drift, in units/s from 0 to 1000, along (CloudWindX, CloudWindZ).

name: CloudWindX
documentation: CloudWindX is the X part, from -1 to 1, of the direction the clouds drift. When `CloudWindX` and `CloudWindZ` are both 0, the clouds drift along +X.

name: CloudWindZ
documentation: CloudWindZ is the Z part, from -1 to 1, of the direction the clouds drift.

name: Collider
documentation: Collider is the collision shape of the part, separate from its visual shape.

name: CollisionGroup
documentation: CollisionGroup is the name of the collision group that decides what this part collides with. A group must be registered with game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup before a part can join it.
notes: On a character, every limb joins the group too.

A character in `"Default"`, `"Character"` or `"CharacterNoCollide"` walks through the sides of a part whose group does not collide with its group, but still stands on its top; set the part's `Trigger` to let it fall through. A character in a group a script registered falls through such a part.
A part parented under a character never collides with that character, and the character never stands on it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a floor part: ghost crates fall through it.
self.Anchored = true
game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup("Ghost")
game.Physics.SetCollisionRule("Ghost", "Default", false)

local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.CollisionGroup = "Ghost"
crate.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
crate.Parent = game.World
task.wait(2)
print(crate.Position.y < 0) -- prints true

name: Color
documentation: Color tints the part's base color, its mesh texture, or a decal's image. It is an sRGB color: `Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)` leaves the texture as it is and `Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)` makes it black.
notes: Any write, black included, turns a mesh with a texture id such as Albedo into a clothing layer: the mesh file's textures are not used, and Underlay, then `Albedo`, blend over `Color`.

name: ColumnWidths
documentation: ColumnWidths is the width in pixels of up to 16 columns of a grid or table. A non-zero entry replaces the shared cell width for that column; entries left out are 0.

name: Columns
documentation: Columns is the number of columns of a grid before items wrap to the next line, clamped between 1 and 8192 in layout.

name: Component
documentation: Component returns a view of one component of the instance, or nil when the instance does not have it. The view reads and writes the same values as the flat properties.
notes: Reading or writing a view after the instance lost the component is an error; a view never adds the component.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent("Health")
local health = self:Component("Health")
if health then
    health.MaxHealth = 200
end
print(self.MaxHealth) -- prints 200
print(self:Component("Light")) -- prints nil

name: Cone
documentation: create a cone part

name: ConeInnerAngle
documentation: ConeInnerAngle is the full angle, in degrees, of the cone in which the sound plays at full volume. The cone points out of the instance's Front face (-Z) and turns with it. At 360 the sound is the same in every direction.

name: ConeOuterAngle
documentation: ConeOuterAngle is the full angle, in degrees, of the cone outside which the sound plays at ConeOuterGain. Between ConeInnerAngle and this angle, the volume drops linearly.

name: ConeOuterGain
documentation: ConeOuterGain is the volume multiplier outside ConeOuterAngle. 0 silences the sound there.

name: ConfirmText
documentation: ConfirmText is the confirm button text; empty shows OK.

name: Confirmed
documentation: Confirmed fires when the player accepts the dialog.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local ui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
ui.Parent = game.Overlay
local dialog = Instance.new("Frame")
dialog.DialogTitle = "Quit"
dialog.Parent = ui
dialog.Confirmed:Connect(function() print("ok") end)

name: ConnectedAnchor
documentation: ConnectedAnchor is where the rope attaches to `ConnectedRigidbody`, in units in that part's frame.

name: ConnectedBody
documentation: ConnectedBody is the part this part is linked to by a hinge around `HingeAxis` at `HingeAnchor`. The hinge forms only between parts with physics bodies in different assemblies, and setting nil or destroying either part removes it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a door frame part: hang a door on its left edge.
self.Anchored = true

local door = Instance.new("Part")
door.Size = Vector3.new(4, 7, 0.2)
door.Position = self.Position + Vector3.new(2, 0, 0)
door.Parent = game.World
door.HingeAnchor = Vector3.new(-2, 0, 0)
door.HingeAxis = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
door.UseLimits = true
door.LimitsMin = -90
door.LimitsMax = 90
door.ConnectedBody = self

name: ConnectedRigidbody
documentation: ConnectedRigidbody is the part this part is tied to by a rope that keeps them at most `Distance` units apart. The rope forms only between parts with physics bodies in different assemblies, and setting nil or destroying either part removes it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a ceiling part: hang a lamp on a 6-unit rope.
self.Anchored = true

local lamp = Instance.new("Part")
lamp.Size = Vector3.new(1, 1, 1)
lamp.Position = self.Position - Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)
lamp.Parent = game.World
lamp.Distance = 6
lamp.ConnectedRigidbody = self

name: ConsolePrompt
documentation: ConsolePrompt, when true, makes this element the developer console command input.

name: ConsoleRowLine
documentation: ConsoleRowLine, when true, makes this element show the text of a developer console message.

name: ConsoleRowPrefix
documentation: ConsoleRowPrefix, when true, makes this element show the time or source of a developer console message.

name: ContinuousCollision
documentation: ContinuousCollision stops a small fast body from passing through other bodies. It costs more simulation time.

name: CoreMenuDimmer
documentation: CoreMenuDimmer marks a descendant of the core menu as the menu's backdrop, which fades in and out with the menu. Only the first one marked counts.

name: CornerRadii
documentation: CornerRadii is the radius in pixels of each corner of the background: `Min.X` and `Min.Y` are top-left and top-right, and `Max.X` and `Max.Y` are bottom-right and bottom-left. When all four are 0, CornerRadius applies.

name: CornerRadius
documentation: CornerRadius is the radius in pixels of the corners of the background and border, never more than half the element's width or height.

name: CorneringStiffness
documentation: CorneringStiffness is the sideways grip a tire gains per radian of slip angle, as a multiple of its load. A stiffer tire reaches `PeakFriction`, and starts to slide, at a smaller angle.

name: Cursor
documentation: Cursor is the cursor shape shown while the pointer is over the element. It takes a name from `game.Enum.CursorShape`, such as `"Pointer"` or `"Text"`. `"Auto"` uses the nearest ancestor's cursor.

name: CursorColor3
documentation: CursorColor3 is the color of the blinking caret of a text box being typed in.

name: CursorPosition
documentation: CursorPosition is the byte position of the caret in a focused text box, counted from 1 as `string.sub` counts, or -1 while the box has no focus. Writing it moves the caret; without focus, a write does nothing.

name: CursorTransparency
documentation: CursorTransparency is the transparency of the caret, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: Cylinder
documentation: create a cylinder part

name: Decal
documentation: create an image projected onto a face

name: Density
documentation: Density is the mass per cubic unit of the part, so its mass is `Density * volume`. A part without its own Density reads its material's density, or 0.7 without a material.

name: Destroy
documentation: Destroy deletes the instance and all its descendants at once and disconnects their signal connections. It does nothing on an instance that is already destroyed.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local bullet = Instance.new("Part")
bullet.Parent = game.World
task.delay(2, function()
    bullet:Destroy()
    print(bullet:IsAlive()) -- prints false
end)

name: DialogTitle
documentation: DialogTitle is the dialog's title.

name: DirectionalColor
documentation: DirectionalColor is the sRGB color of the sunlight. The light shines along the instance's `Orientation`; only the first directional light in the world lights the scene.

name: DirectionalEnergy
documentation: DirectionalEnergy is the brightness of the sunlight, from 0 to 20. At 0 surfaces get only ambient light.

name: DirectionalShadowFill
documentation: DirectionalShadowFill is the share of diffuse sunlight that still reaches surfaces in the sun's shadow. 0 leaves shadows dark, and 1 lights them fully except for the sun's highlight.

name: DirectionalShadowMode
documentation: DirectionalShadowMode is whether the sun casts shadows: `"None"` casts none, and `"Hard"` casts sharp-edged shadows out to MaxDistance from the camera.

name: Disabled
documentation: Disabled, when true, dims the element and stops it from taking the pointer, so no hover, click or activation events fire.

name: DisabledImage
documentation: DisabledImage is the asset id of the image shown in place of `Image` while the element or any ancestor is disabled. `"0"` keeps `Image`.

name: DisplayName
documentation: DisplayName is the name on the character's nametag and in the player list.

name: Distance
documentation: Distance is the longest the rope stretches, in units. The parts can move closer. A running rope motor changes Distance as it reels.

name: DockPrefab
documentation: DockPrefab is the name of a prefab whose spawned UI root draws in this element's box instead of its own. Writing it adds the `UIDock` component. While the root exists, this element and its children do not draw. Writing `""` returns both to their own places, and destroying either restores the other.

name: DotColor3
documentation: DotColor3 is the color of the dot of a selected radio button.

name: DotTransparency
documentation: DotTransparency is the transparency of a radio button's dot, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: Down
documentation: Down is the Input.Key on an `InputBinding` that adds -1 on Y to a `Direction2D` action while held. 0 binds no key.

name: DragEnded
documentation: DragEnded fires on the client when the player finishes dragging this control. It passes true if the drag changed the control's value.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Parent = screen

button.DragEnded:Connect(function(edited)
    print("drag ended", edited)
end)

name: DragMoved
type: Signal<(a: number, b: number, c: number) -> ()>
documentation: DragMoved fires on the client while a pointer drags this control. It passes the movement in pixels. On adornment handles it passes the face index and the distance in units.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Parent = screen

button.DragMoved:Connect(function(dx, dy)
    button.UIRect.Position += UDim2.fromOffset(dx, dy)
end)

name: DriveTorque
documentation: DriveTorque is the most torque the wheel's motor applies to reach `SpinSpeed`. At 0 the wheel rolls freely.

name: Drives
documentation: Drives is the character control an `InputAction` drives, so a touch stick, a UI button or a key can make the local character walk or jump. `"Move"` walks along a `Direction2D` action's vector (+Y forward from the camera, its length the fraction of walk speed); `"Jump"` jumps while a `Bool` action is on.
notes: The action drives the character only while the escape menu is closed and InputMove is true on the default camera.
code_sample:
-- Client script: the J key also makes the character jump.
local controls = Instance.new("InputContext")
local jump = Instance.new("InputAction")
jump.Drives = "Jump"
jump.Parent = controls
local j = Instance.new("InputBinding")
j.KeyCode = game.Input.Key.J
j.Parent = jump

name: Emissive
documentation: Emissive is the asset id of a texture that makes parts of a mesh glow in any light; black gives no glow. `"0"` means none.

name: Emit
documentation: Emit fires a named signal on the instance and runs every connected function before it returns.
notes: Emit does nothing unless a script created this signal with GetSignal. With no connected function, it prints `signal '<name>' fired with no connected handlers`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:GetSignal("Alert"):Connect(function(level)
    print("alert level " .. level) -- prints alert level 3
end)
self:Emit("Alert", 3)

name: Enabled
documentation: Enabled is whether an `InputContext` or `InputAction` takes input. Turning off a context turns off every action under it.

name: EquipTool
documentation: EquipTool puts a tool in this character's hand. A tool without a slot gets the lowest free one. The tool the character held before goes back to its slot.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
local pistol = Instance.new("Tool")
pistol.Name = "Pistol"
npc:EquipTool(pistol)
print(assert(npc:GetTool()).Name) -- prints Pistol

name: Equipped
documentation: Equipped fires when a character equips this tool, on the server and on the client of the player who equips it. The callback receives the player, or nil for a character no player controls.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local sword = Instance.new("Tool")
sword.Equipped:Connect(function(player: Instance?)
    print("equipped by " .. (if player then player.Name else "an NPC"))
end)
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:EquipTool(sword) -- prints equipped by an NPC

name: Face
documentation: Face is the asset id of the face texture, or `"0"` for none.

name: FillAmount
documentation: FillAmount is how much of a round progress fill shows, from 0 (empty) to 1 (the full circle).

name: FillColor3
documentation: FillColor3 is the color of the slider track between its start and the thumb.

name: FillColumns
