documentation: FillColumns, when true, fits as many `CellSize.X` columns across a grid as its inner width has room for, ignoring `Columns`. `FitColumns` and `ColumnWidths` override it.

name: FillImage
documentation: FillImage is the asset id of the image on the filled part of the slider track. `"0"` draws plain `FillColor3`.

name: FillMode
documentation: FillMode is the way a round progress fill sweeps: `"Clockwise"`, `"Counterclockwise"`, or `"BothWays"` from the top center.

name: FillTransparency
documentation: FillTransparency is the transparency of the filled part of the slider track, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: FindAncestorWithComponent
documentation: FindAncestorWithComponent returns the instance itself or its nearest ancestor that has the named component or Pair, or nil when none has it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local hat = Instance.new("Part")
hat.Parent = self
self:AddComponent("Light")
print(hat:FindAncestorWithComponent("Light") == self) -- prints true

name: FindFirstChild
type: (self: Instance, name: string, recursive: boolean?) -> Instance?
documentation: FindFirstChild returns the first child with a matching `Name`, or nil. With `recursive` set to true it searches every descendant, nearest levels first.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local lamp = Instance.new("Part")
lamp.Name = "Lamp"
lamp.Parent = self

print(self:FindFirstChild("Lamp") == lamp) -- prints true
print(self:FindFirstChild("Door")) -- prints nil

name: FitColumns
documentation: FitColumns, when true, makes each grid column as wide as its widest cell.

name: FlareGhostIntensity
documentation: FlareGhostIntensity is the brightness, from 0 to 10, of the extra reflections of the sun's lens flare. 0 keeps only the main flare disk.

name: FlareIntensity
documentation: FlareIntensity is the brightness, from 0 to 10, of the sun's lens flare and sun rays; 0 turns both off.

name: FlareRaysIntensity
documentation: FlareRaysIntensity is the brightness, from 0 to 10, of the rays of light around the sun that shine past clouds and objects. Rays draw only at graphics quality Level 6 and above.

name: FlareScale
documentation: FlareScale multiplies the size of every lens flare element, from 0.1 to 5.

name: FlareTint
documentation: FlareTint is the sRGB tint of the lens flare and the sun rays.

name: Floating
documentation: Floating, when true, takes the element out of its parent's list or grid layout. Its `Position` and `AnchorPoint` place it in the parent's box.

name: FocusLost
documentation: FocusLost fires on the client when this text box loses keyboard focus. The callback receives true when the player pressed the return key.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local box = Instance.new("TextBox")
box.Parent = screen
box.FocusLost:Connect(function(enterPressed)
    if enterPressed then
        print("submitted " .. box.Text)
    end
end)

name: Focused
documentation: Focused fires on the client when this text box gains keyboard focus from a click, a tap or CaptureFocus.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local box = Instance.new("TextBox")
box.Parent = screen
box.Focused:Connect(function()
    box.PlaceholderText = ""
end)
box.FocusLost:Connect(function()
    box.PlaceholderText = "Search"
end)

name: FogColor
documentation: FogColor is the sRGB color of the fog that objects blend into with distance. The fog is lit by the same sun and sky as the ground. The sky is not fogged.

name: FogDensity
documentation: FogDensity is how thick the fog is in the `"Exponential"` and `"ExponentialSquared"` modes, from 0 to 1.

name: FogEnd
documentation: FogEnd is the distance from the camera, in units, where `"Linear"` fog hides objects fully.

name: FogMode
documentation: FogMode is how the fog thickens with distance, one of `game.Enum.FogMode`:

name: FogStart
documentation: FogStart is the distance from the camera, in units, where `"Linear"` fog begins.

name: Folded
documentation: Folded, when true, collapses the tree node and hides everything under it.

name: Folder
documentation: create an empty instance named Folder

name: FontFamily
documentation: FontFamily is the typeface of the text: `"Arimo"`, `"Montserrat"`, `"Fredoka"`, `"Nunito"`, `"Roboto"`, `"RobotoMono"`, `"Oswald"`, `"Merriweather"`, `"Bangers"`, `"LuckiestGuy"`, `"PressStart2P"`, `"PermanentMarker"` or `"Creepster"`. Spaces and case do not count, so `"Press Start 2P"` works. A character the family lacks draws in Arimo, then in the emoji font.

name: FontWeight
documentation: FontWeight is the weight of the text, from 100 (thin) through 400 (regular) and 700 (bold) to 900 (black). Values clamp between 1 and 1000.

name: Frame
documentation: create a rectangle interface element

name: FreezePosition
documentation: FreezePosition locks movement along world axes: X 1, Y 2, Z 4. Add the values to lock several axes.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part that slides only up and down.
self.FreezePosition = 1 + 4 -- X and Z

name: FreezeRotation
documentation: FreezeRotation locks rotation around world axes: X 1, Y 2, Z 4. Add the values to lock several axes.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a crate that must not tip over.
self.FreezeRotation = 1 + 4 -- X and Z

name: FreezeRows
documentation: FreezeRows is the number of header lines that stay at the top of a scrolling table while the others scroll under them.

name: Friction
documentation: Friction is the friction coefficient of the part's surface. 0 is frictionless. A part without its own Friction reads its material's friction, or 0.2 without a material.

name: FrictionTorque
documentation: FrictionTorque is the torque in Newton-meters that keeps a settled swing-twist joint still. At 0 the joint turns freely.

name: GetAccessories
documentation: GetAccessories returns an array of the accessories this character wears.
deprecation: Iterate `WornBy` pairs with World.Each and World.Pair.

name: GetAngularVelocity
documentation: GetAngularVelocity returns the world angular velocity of the physics body in radians per second.

name: GetAttributeChangedSignal
documentation: GetAttributeChangedSignal returns a Signal that fires when the named attribute in `attr` takes a new value, whether a script or the server changed it. The attribute does not need to exist yet.
notes: The engine compares the value once per tick, before `Update` runs, and fires once with no arguments. Adding, removing and changing the type of the attribute each count as a change.
Each connected signal adds one comparison per tick, so disconnect it when the handler has nothing left to do.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a door part.
self:GetAttributeChangedSignal("Open"):Connect(function()
    self.Transparency = if self.attr.Open then 0.5 else 0
    print(self.Transparency) -- prints 0.5
end)
self.attr.Open = true

name: GetChildren
documentation: GetChildren returns an array of the direct children of this instance.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
for _ = 1, 3 do
    Instance.new("Part").Parent = self
end
for _, child in self:GetChildren() do
    child.Transparency = 0.5
end
print(#self:GetChildren()) -- prints 3

name: GetComponents
documentation: GetComponents returns the names of the components on the instance: built-in components first, then custom components in the order the place declares them. The list omits relationship pairs; query `game.World.Pair("Tag", "*")` with World.Query for tags.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent("Light")
print(table.find(self:GetComponents(), "Light") ~= nil) -- prints true

name: GetDescendants
documentation: GetDescendants returns an array of every descendant of this instance, shallowest first.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local box = Instance.new("Part")
box.Parent = self
Instance.new("Part").Parent = box
print(#self:GetDescendants()) -- prints 2

name: GetHandle
documentation: GetHandle returns the instance in this instance's handles slot `name`, or nil when the slot is empty or its target is destroyed. A clone's slots point at the copies inside the cloned tree, so each clone of a template finds its own parts.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a list part. In the editor, its Template slot points at
-- an entry part, and the entry's Label slot points at a child of the entry.
local template = self:GetHandle("Template")
if template then
    local entry = template:Clone()
    local label = entry:GetHandle("Label") -- the copy's own child
    if label then
        label.Name = "Score"
    end
    entry.Parent = self
end

name: GetHearingSense
documentation: GetHearingSense returns how well the instance hears and the bitmask of the collision groups it hears.

name: GetLastHeardStimulus
documentation: GetLastHeardStimulus returns the source, world position, age in seconds and tag of the last sound the instance heard, or nothing when it has heard none.

name: GetLinearVelocity
documentation: GetLinearVelocity returns the world velocity of the physics body in units per second.

name: GetMass
documentation: GetMass returns the mass of the part's physics body. It returns nil until the body exists, which is after the part's first physics step. On a welded part it returns the mass of the whole assembly; on a part worn by a character or welded to one of its limbs, the part's own mass.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Size = Vector3.new(2, 2, 2)
self.Density = 1
task.wait()
print(self:GetMass()) -- prints 8

name: GetMoveIntent
documentation: GetMoveIntent returns which way the character tries to move and whether it wants to jump, or nil.
deprecation: Query the CharacterMoveIntent component with World.Query.

name: GetNearestPerceivedTarget
documentation: GetNearestPerceivedTarget returns the closest instance in the instance's vision cone and its distance, or nothing when it sees none.

name: GetPropertyChangedSignal
documentation: GetPropertyChangedSignal returns a Signal that fires when the named property takes a new value, whether a script, physics, the player or the server changed it.
notes: The engine compares the value once per tick, before `Update` runs. A value that changes and changes back within one tick does not fire.
Each connected signal adds one comparison per tick.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Transparency"):Connect(function()
    print(self.Transparency) -- prints 0.5
end)
self.Transparency = 0.5

name: GetSignal
documentation: GetSignal returns a Signal for a custom event name on this instance. Fire it with Emit.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local died = self:GetSignal("Died")
died:Connect(function(cause)
    print("died from " .. cause) -- prints died from lava
end)
self:Emit("Died", "lava")

name: GetState
documentation: GetState returns whether an `InputAction` is pressed, or for a `Direction2D` action its vector (+Y up, length 0 to 1). It returns false or the zero vector while the action or its `InputContext` is off. Only client scripts can call it.
code_sample:
-- Client script: print while the player holds Left Shift.
local gameplay = Instance.new("InputContext")
local sprint = Instance.new("InputAction")
sprint.Parent = gameplay
local shift = Instance.new("InputBinding")
shift.KeyCode = game.Input.Key.LeftShift
shift.Parent = sprint

function Update(dt: number)
    if sprint:GetState() then
        print("sprinting")
    end
end

name: GetStateEnabled
documentation: GetStateEnabled returns whether a character enters a movement state by itself. Every state is enabled until `SetStateEnabled` turns it off.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
print(npc:GetStateEnabled("Jumping")) -- prints true

name: GetSwingTwistJoint
documentation: GetSwingTwistJoint returns the limits, anchor and axes of the swing-twist joint, or nil when there is none.
deprecation: Read the `SwingTwistJoint` properties such as Anchor.

name: GetTool
documentation: GetTool returns the tool the character holds, or with `slot`, the tool in that hotbar slot. It returns nil when there is none.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:EquipTool(Instance.new("Tool"))
npc:UnequipTools()
print(assert(npc:GetTool(1)).Name) -- prints Tool

name: GetVisionCone
documentation: GetVisionCone returns the range, field of view in degrees, eye height offset and collision group bitmask of the instance's vision cone.

name: GraphOffset
documentation: GraphOffset is how far a graph canvas is panned, in pixels.

name: GraphZoom
documentation: GraphZoom is the zoom of a graph canvas.

name: GraphZoomMax
documentation: GraphZoomMax is the highest zoom the mouse wheel reaches.

name: GraphZoomMin
documentation: GraphZoomMin is the lowest zoom the mouse wheel reaches.

name: GraphZoomStep
documentation: GraphZoomStep is the zoom factor of one mouse wheel notch.

name: GravityScale
documentation: GravityScale multiplies the world's gravity for this body. 1 is normal gravity, 0 is none, and a negative value pulls the body up.

name: GravityVector
documentation: GravityVector is the acceleration in units/s² that replaces world Gravity for this character.

name: GridLineColor3
documentation: GridLineColor3 is the color of the lines between table cells.

name: GridLineThickness
documentation: GridLineThickness is the width in pixels of the lines between table cells; 0 draws none.

name: GridLineTransparency
documentation: GridLineTransparency is the transparency of the lines between table cells, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: GripSize
documentation: GripSize is the size in pixels of the square resize handle in a window's corner.

name: GroupTransparency
documentation: GroupTransparency fades the element and every element under it, from 0 (as authored) to 1 (invisible), including an open popup, menu, dropdown panel or dialog. On a `SurfaceGui` or `BillboardGui` it fades the whole canvas. An element at 1 still takes the pointer; set `Visible` to false to stop it.

name: Handles
documentation: create 3D drag handles that report drags on a target

name: HandlesColor3
documentation: HandlesColor3 is the color of the 3D handles.

name: HandlesFaces
documentation: HandlesFaces is a bitmask of the bounding box faces that show handles: bits 0 to 5 are Right (+X), Top (+Y), Back (+Z), Left (-X), Bottom (-Y) and Front (-Z). 63 shows all six.

name: HandlesStyle
documentation: HandlesStyle is the look of the move handles: `"Resize"` draws ball pins and `"Movement"` draws arrows.

name: HandlesTransparency
documentation: HandlesTransparency is the transparency of the 3D handles.

name: HandlesType
documentation: HandlesType is whether the handles move the instance along each axis (`"Translation"`) or turn it about each axis with rings (`"Rotation"`).

name: HasComponent
documentation: HasComponent returns true when the instance has the component or Pair.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
print(self:HasComponent("Light")) -- prints false
self:AddComponent("Light")
print(self:HasComponent("Light")) -- prints true

name: HeaderCell
documentation: HeaderCell, when true, makes the grid cell look and work as a clickable column header.

name: HeaderColor3
documentation: HeaderColor3 is the color of the header bar of a collapsible section.

name: HeaderHeight
documentation: HeaderHeight is the height in pixels of a collapsible section's header bar. A collapsed section shrinks to this height; values below 0 count as 0.

name: HeaderTransparency
documentation: HeaderTransparency is the transparency of a collapsible section's header bar.

name: Health
documentation: Health is the character's health. At 0 the character enters the `"Dead"` state at the next physics step. `Health` is on the character root, so to hurt a body part's character, call TakeDamage on the part or write `Health` on its Character.
code_sample:
-- Server script: heal a character by 25 without going past MaxHealth.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:TakeDamage(10)
npc.Health = math.min(npc.Health + 25, npc.MaxHealth)
print(npc.Health) -- prints 100

name: HighValue
documentation: HighValue is the step of the upper thumb of a two-thumb range slider, from 0 to `Steps - 1`. Dragging never puts it below the lower thumb.

name: HighlightColor3
documentation: HighlightColor3 is the background color of a menu item or dropdown entry under the pointer.

name: HighlightTransparency
documentation: HighlightTransparency is the transparency of the background of a menu item or dropdown entry under the pointer.

name: HingeAnchor
documentation: HingeAnchor is the pivot of the hinge, in units in this part's frame.

name: HingeAxis
documentation: HingeAxis is the direction the hinge turns around, in this part's frame.

name: HipHeight
documentation: HipHeight is how high, in units, the bottom of the torso stands above the ground.

name: Hit
type: Signal<(other: Instance, position: vector, normal: vector, speed: number) -> ()>
documentation: Hit fires during each physics step for each body this part's collider hit, with the other instance, the contact position, the contact normal and the relative speed in units per second.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a floor part: print how hard a crate lands on it.
self.Anchored = true
self.Hit:Connect(function(other: Instance, position: vector, normal: vector, speed: number)
    if speed > 20 then
        print(other.Name, math.round(speed))
    end
end)

local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.Name = "Crate"
crate.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
crate.Parent = game.World

name: HitSlopBottom
documentation: HitSlopBottom is how many points below the element's box the pointer still hits it, without changing drawing or layout; values below 0 count as 0. Writing it adds the `UIHitSlop` component.

name: HitSlopLeft
documentation: HitSlopLeft is how many points left of the element's box the pointer still hits it; see HitSlopBottom for behavior.

name: HitSlopRight
documentation: HitSlopRight is how many points right of the element's box the pointer still hits it; see HitSlopBottom for behavior.

name: HitSlopTop
documentation: HitSlopTop is how many points above the element's box the pointer still hits it; see HitSlopBottom for behavior.

name: HoverImage
documentation: HoverImage is the asset id of the image shown in place of `Image` while the pointer is over the element and not pressing it. `"0"` keeps `Image`.

name: Hovered
documentation: Hovered fires on the client with true when a pointer enters this control and false when it leaves.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Parent = screen

button.Hovered:Connect(function(entered)
    button.TextTransparency = if entered then 0 else 0.3
end)

name: Hue
documentation: Hue is the hue picked in a color picker, from 0 to 1 around the color wheel: red through green and blue back to red. Values outside 0 to 1 wrap.

name: IconAlign
documentation: IconAlign is the side of the text the icon goes on: `"Left"`, `"Right"`, `"Top"` or `"Bottom"`.

name: IconGap
documentation: IconGap is the gap in pixels between the icon and the text.

name: IconSize
documentation: IconSize is the width and height in pixels of the icon.

name: Image
documentation: Image is the asset id of the image drawn over the element's box. `"0"` draws none.

name: ImageButton
documentation: create a clickable image

name: ImageColor3
documentation: ImageColor3 tints the image: each pixel is multiplied by this color.

name: ImageLabel
documentation: create an image interface element

name: ImageRectOffset
documentation: ImageRectOffset is the top-left corner, in texture pixels, of the region of the texture the image shows. With ImageRectSize it picks one sprite of a sprite sheet.

name: ImageRectSize
documentation: ImageRectSize is the size, in texture pixels, of the region of the texture the image shows. A zero side shows the whole texture.

name: ImageRotation
documentation: ImageRotation turns the image clockwise by this many degrees about the element's center. Layout, clicks and children do not turn.

name: ImageTransparency
documentation: ImageTransparency is the transparency of the image, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: Indent
documentation: Indent is how far, in pixels, each level of a tree view moves its children to the right.

name: InducedDragFactor
documentation: InducedDragFactor is the drag coefficient a wing adds per squared lift coefficient: `C_D = ZeroLiftDrag + InducedDragFactor * C_L ^ 2`.

name: InnerAngle
documentation: InnerAngle is the half-angle, in radians from 0 to 1.57, of the fully lit center of a spotlight. Between `InnerAngle` and OuterAngle the light fades to nothing.

name: InputAction
documentation: create an input action

name: InputBinding
documentation: create a key or button binding for an input action

name: InputContext
documentation: create a group of input actions

name: InputMove
documentation: InputMove lets the local character walk and jump with the movement keys, the left stick and an `InputAction` that Drives `"Move"` or `"Jump"`. It works only on the client's default camera, game.World.Camera, which starts with it true.

name: InputSteer
documentation: InputSteer lets the mouse, the camera keys, the right stick and touch steer the `CameraOrbit` or `CameraFly` rig on this camera. The default camera starts with it true; set it to false to steer the rig from a script alone.

name: InsetEdge
documentation: InsetEdge is the screen edge this element keeps clear for elements that set ScreenInsets: `"Top"`, `"Right"`, `"Bottom"` or `"Left"`. Only a visible element on the screen canvas reserves space.

name: Intensity
documentation: Intensity is the brightness of a point light or spotlight, from 0 to 1000, multiplied by LightColor.

name: InverseTransformDirection
documentation: InverseTransformDirection turns a world direction into the instance's own frame.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 90, 0)
local d = self:InverseTransformDirection(Vector3.new(1, 0, 0))
print(math.round(d.z)) -- prints 1

name: InverseTransformPoint
documentation: InverseTransformPoint turns a world position into a position in the instance's own frame.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Position = Vector3.new(10, 0, 0)
print(self:InverseTransformPoint(Vector3.new(12, 3, 0))) -- prints 2, 3, 0

name: Invulnerable
documentation: Invulnerable makes `TakeDamage` do nothing.

name: IsAlive
documentation: IsAlive returns true until the instance is destroyed, then false.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local coin = Instance.new("Part")
coin.Parent = game.World
coin:Destroy()
print(coin:IsAlive()) -- prints false

name: IsDescendantOf
documentation: IsDescendantOf returns true when the instance is below `ancestor` in the tree. Every live instance is a descendant of `game.World`; a destroyed one is a descendant of nothing.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local box = Instance.new("Part")
box.Parent = self
print(box:IsDescendantOf(self)) -- prints true
print(box:IsDescendantOf(game.World)) -- prints true
box:Destroy()
print(box:IsDescendantOf(game.World)) -- prints false

name: IsFocused
documentation: IsFocused returns true while this text box has keyboard focus.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local box = Instance.new("TextBox")
box.Parent = screen
if box:IsFocused() then
    box:ReleaseFocus()
else
    box:CaptureFocus()
end

name: IsRoot
documentation: IsRoot marks this instance as an accessory root; its descendants are placed relative to it. When false, `Attachment` marks a character socket.

name: Italic
documentation: Italic, when true, slants the text by 14 degrees.

name: ItemCount
documentation: ItemCount is the number of items in a long scrolling list, counting those off screen. The list reuses its children to show only the items in view.

name: ItemHeight
documentation: ItemHeight is the height in pixels of every item of a long list. Below 1, children are not reused.

name: ItemShown
documentation: ItemShown fires on the client when an item scrolls into view, with the reused child and the item's 1-based index.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local list = Instance.new("ScrollingFrame")
list.ItemCount = 500
list.Parent = screen
for _ = 1, 11 do
    Instance.new("TextLabel").Parent = list
end

list.ItemShown:Connect(function(item, index)
    item.Text = "Player " .. index
end)

name: Joint
documentation: Joint is where on the torso a limb attaches in its rest pose, in units in the torso's frame.

name: JumpPower
documentation: JumpPower is the speed, in units/s, a jump from the ground gives the character along `UpDirection`.

name: JumpPowerScale
documentation: JumpPowerScale multiplies JumpPower for jumps in the air.

name: Justify
documentation: Justify places the run of children along the stacking axis of a list: `"Start"`, `"Center"` or `"End"`. A `"Grow"` child fills the spare space, so Justify does nothing.

name: KeyCode
documentation: KeyCode is the Input.Key or gamepad button on an `InputBinding` that presses its `Parent` action. 0 binds no key. On a `Direction2D` action only `Input.Key.Thumbstick1` and `Input.Key.Thumbstick2` work here; use Up, Down, Left and Right for keys.

name: Keybind
documentation: Keybind is the Settings.Keybind action whose input an `InputBinding` follows, so the player's rebinds in the menu apply to it. It works only on a `Bool` action. A wheel turn fires `Pressed` and `Released` once on each frame the wheel turns.
code_sample:
-- Client script: react to the player's Player List key, whatever it is.
local keys = Instance.new("InputContext")
local toggle = Instance.new("InputAction")
toggle.Parent = keys
local binding = Instance.new("InputBinding")
binding.Keybind = "PlayerList"
binding.Parent = toggle

toggle.Pressed:Connect(function()
    print("toggle the player list")
end)

name: KnobColor3
documentation: KnobColor3 is the color of a toggle switch's knob.

name: KnobImage
documentation: KnobImage is the asset id of the image on a toggle switch's knob. `"0"` draws a plain knob in `KnobColor3`.

name: KnobInset
documentation: KnobInset is the gap in pixels between a toggle switch's track and knob.

name: KnobTransparency
documentation: KnobTransparency is the transparency of a toggle switch's knob, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: LabelText
documentation: LabelText is text drawn centered in a separator line, splitting it in two. An empty string draws a plain line.

name: Layer
documentation: Layer orders decals on the same face of a part, from -128 to 127. A higher layer draws in front, but every layer at -1 or below draws as -1, and every layer at 2 or above as 2.

name: LayoutOrder
documentation: LayoutOrder is the order of an element among its siblings in a list or grid: lower numbers come first, and equal numbers keep the order they were added in.

name: Left
documentation: Left is the Input.Key on an `InputBinding` that adds -1 on X to a `Direction2D` action while held. 0 binds no key.

name: LiftSlope
documentation: LiftSlope is the lift coefficient a wing gains per radian of angle of attack (the angle between the airflow and the chord): `C_L = LiftSlope * angle` up to `StallAngle`.

name: LightColor
documentation: LightColor is the sRGB color of a point light or spotlight.

name: LightShadowOff
documentation: LightShadowOff, when true, stops a point light or spotlight from casting shadows. At most 4 point lights and 8 spotlights cast shadows in a frame; the others light without them.

name: LimitsMax
documentation: LimitsMax is the upper angle limit of the hinge in degrees when `UseLimits` is true.

name: LimitsMin
documentation: LimitsMin is the lower angle limit of the hinge in degrees when `UseLimits` is true.

name: LineColor3
documentation: LineColor3 is the color of a separator's line.

name: LineHeight
documentation: LineHeight is the spacing of text lines as a multiple of the font's line spacing, from 1 to 3.

name: LineThickness
documentation: LineThickness is the thickness in pixels of a separator's line.

name: LineTransparency
documentation: LineTransparency is the transparency of a separator's line.

name: LinearDamping
documentation: LinearDamping is the drag that slows the body's movement. 0 is no drag.

name: LinkFrom
documentation: LinkFrom is the graph port where a wire starts.

name: LinkRequested
documentation: LinkRequested fires on the client when the player drags between ports on a node graph.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local graph = Instance.new("Frame")
graph:AddComponent("UIGraph")
graph.Parent = screen
for x = 0, 1 do
    local node = Instance.new("Frame")
    node.Parent = graph
    node.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(250 * x, 0)
    local port = Instance.new("Frame")
    port:AddComponent("UIGraphPort")
    port.Parent = node
end
graph.LinkRequested:Connect(function(from, to)
    local wire = Instance.new("Frame")
    wire.LinkFrom = from
    wire.LinkTo = to
    wire.Parent = graph
end)

name: LinkTo
documentation: LinkTo is the graph port where a wire ends.

name: LinkUrl
documentation: LinkUrl is the `http://` or `https://` address the button opens in the player's browser. Setting it underlines the button's text.

name: LocalOrientation
documentation: LocalOrientation is the rotation of the instance relative to its nearest positioned ancestor, as Euler angles in degrees: (pitch, yaw, roll), applied in YXZ order. Without a positioned ancestor, it is the last value written, or (0, 0, 0), and a write does not turn the instance. Like Orientation, it takes degrees; write radian vectors from the `rotation` library to LocalRotationVector.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local arm = Instance.new("Part")
arm.Parent = self
self.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 90, 0)
arm.LocalOrientation = Vector3.new(0, 45, 0)
print(math.round(arm.Orientation.y)) -- prints 135

name: LocalPivotTo
type: (self: Instance, position: vector, rotation: vector, pivot: vector?) -> ()
documentation: LocalPivotTo turns the instance to `rotation` in the frame of its nearest positioned ancestor and moves it so that its own point `pivot` is at `position` in that frame. Without `pivot`, it sets LocalPosition and LocalRotationVector.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: tip a lid open on its back edge.
local lid = Instance.new("Part")
lid.Parent = self
local hingeOnLid = Vector3.new(0, 1, 1)
local hingeOnSelf = Vector3.new(0, 2, 1)
lid:LocalPivotTo(hingeOnSelf, rotation.axis(Vector3.xAxis, math.rad(90)), hingeOnLid)
print(math.round(lid.LocalPosition.y)) -- prints 3

name: LocalPosition
documentation: LocalPosition is the offset of the instance from its nearest positioned ancestor, in units. Without a positioned ancestor, it is the last value written, or (0, 0, 0), and a write does not move the instance.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local lamp = Instance.new("Part")
lamp.Parent = self
lamp.LocalPosition = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)

self.Position = Vector3.new(10, 0, 0)
print(lamp.Position.y) -- prints 3

name: LocalRotationVector
documentation: LocalRotationVector is the rotation of the instance relative to its nearest positioned ancestor, as an axis-angle vector in radians like the ones the `rotation` library makes. A read gives an angle from 0 to pi, so a longer turn reads back as the same rotation about the opposite axis. Without a positioned ancestor, a write does not turn the instance.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local arm = Instance.new("Part")
arm.Parent = self
arm.LocalRotationVector = rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(270))
print(math.round(math.deg(arm.LocalRotationVector.y))) -- prints -90

name: LocalSpin
documentation: LocalSpin is the angular velocity in radians per second of an assembly member around its parent part, in that parent's frame. The server turns the member every physics step and clients turn it from the rate, so a fan or wheel spins smoothly. If a script writes the rotation every step instead, the part looks slower or reversed on clients above 1800 rpm.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a fan blade inside an assembly Model.
self.LocalSpin = Vector3.new(0, 2 * math.pi, 0) -- one turn per second

name: Locked
documentation: Locked stops Studio's viewport clicks and box selection from selecting the instance or anything under it. It does not change the game.

name: LongitudinalStiffness
documentation: LongitudinalStiffness is the forward grip a tire gains per unit of slip ratio, as a multiple of its load. A stiffer tire reaches `PeakFriction`, and starts to spin or lock, at less slip.

name: LookAt
type: (self: Instance, target: vector, up: vector?, useModelFront: boolean?) -> ()
documentation: LookAt turns the instance to face a world position. By default its -Z axis faces the target, as a camera does; pass `true` as `useModelFront` to point its +Z axis instead. When the instance is at the target or `up` is zero, it prints an error to Output without turning or stopping the script.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a turret part.
local target = Vector3.new(0, 0, -10)
self:LookAt(target, Vector3.yAxis, true)
local front = self:TransformDirection(Vector3.new(0, 0, 1))
print(math.round(front.z)) -- prints -1

name: Looped
documentation: Looped starts the clip again each time it ends, so Playing stays true. Setting it to false while the sound plays lets the current pass finish.

name: LowerTranslation
documentation: LowerTranslation is the shortest `Distance` the rope motor reels in to. The motor stops there.

name: MarginBottom
documentation: MarginBottom is the space in pixels inside the bottom edge of a list.

name: MarginLeft
documentation: MarginLeft is the space in pixels inside the left edge of a list.

name: MarginRight
documentation: MarginRight is the space in pixels inside the right edge of a list.

name: MarginTop
documentation: MarginTop is the space in pixels inside the top edge of a list.

name: Margins
documentation: Margins is the space in pixels inside the left, top, right and bottom edges of a list or grid. On a list it reads and writes MarginLeft, MarginTop, MarginRight and MarginBottom. On an element with neither layout, writing it adds a grid layout.

name: MarkerReached
documentation: MarkerReached fires when an animation playing on this character passes a named marker. The callback receives the clip name and the marker name.
code_sample:
-- Client script: print each marker the local character's clips pass.
local player = game.Players.LocalPlayer
local character = player and player.Character
if character then
    character.MarkerReached:Connect(function(clip: string, marker: string)
        print(clip, marker)
    end)
end

name: Material
documentation: Material is the name of the material this entity draws with, or `""` when it has none. A write takes a material name or the asset id that `game.Materials.DefineMaterial` returns; a read gives the name. On a character, every body part without its own material draws with the character's material.

name: MaxActivationDistance
documentation: MaxActivationDistance is the base click distance in units from a player's character to this part; the radius of the part's bounding sphere is added to it.

name: MaxDistance
documentation: MaxDistance is how far from the camera, in units, the sun casts shadows.

name: MaxEV
documentation: MaxEV is the highest exposure value, from -6 to 20, that automatic exposure uses, so bright sunlight does not darken the picture too much.

name: MaxHealth
documentation: MaxHealth is the most health the character can have through `TakeDamage`.

name: MaxJumps
documentation: MaxJumps is how many times the character can jump in the air before it lands, 0 to 255. It belongs to the `MultiJump` component, which a spawned character lacks, so the character jumps only from the ground. Setting `MaxJumps` or JumpPowerScale adds the component; the character can then jump `1 + MaxJumps` times.

name: MaxLength
documentation: MaxLength is the most bytes the player can type or paste into the text box, up to 65535; 0 sets no limit. A script that writes `Text` is not cut to the limit.

name: MaxPolyphony
documentation: MaxPolyphony is the most copies of this sound that play at once, such as overlapping footsteps. When Play would start one more, the oldest copy stops; at 1, Play restarts the sound.

name: MaxSize
documentation: MaxSize is the largest size layout gives the element; zero sets no limit. MinSize wins when it is larger.

name: MaxSlopeAngle
documentation: MaxSlopeAngle is the steepest slope, in degrees, the character walks on. On steeper ground it cannot jump and, by default, slides down.

name: MaxSteerTorque
documentation: MaxSteerTorque is the most torque the steering spring applies to turn a `Steers` wheel. 0 does not limit the spring.

name: MaxValue
documentation: MaxValue is the highest value of a slider.

name: MaximumMotorForce
documentation: MaximumMotorForce is the most force in Newtons the rope motor pulls with.

name: MenuCheck
documentation: MenuCheck, when true, makes a menu item keep room at its left edge for a check mark or radio dot.

name: Mesh
documentation: Mesh is the asset id of a 3D model drawn at the part's `Size` in place of its Type shape. `"0"` draws the shape.

name: MetallicRoughness
documentation: MetallicRoughness is the asset id of a texture whose blue channel sets metalness and green channel sets roughness. Metalness 1 looks like bare metal; low roughness is shiny and high roughness is matte. `"0"` uses the material's own settings.

name: MinEV
documentation: MinEV is the lowest exposure value, from -6 to 20, that automatic exposure uses, so night scenes and dark rooms do not look too bright.

name: MinSize
documentation: MinSize is the smallest width and height in pixels layout gives the element; a zero side sets no minimum. It wins over MaxSize.

name: MinValue
documentation: MinValue is the lowest value of a slider.

name: Mirror
documentation: create a surface view that reflects the world

name: Mixed
documentation: Mixed, when true, places a toggle switch's knob in the middle. Clicking clears Mixed and flips `On`.

name: Model
documentation: create a model with a pivot

name: MotorForce
documentation: MotorForce is the most torque in Newton-meters the hinge motor applies. At 0 the motor does not turn the part.

name: MotorSpeed
documentation: MotorSpeed is how fast the rope motor changes `Distance`, in units per second. A negative value reels in, a positive value reels out, and 0 stops the motor.
notes: The motor keeps `Distance` between `LowerTranslation` and `UpperTranslation`. A rope longer than `UpperTranslation`, which is 5 by default, jumps to that length when its motor starts.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a crate that hangs on a rope: winch it up until the rope is 2 units long.
self.LowerTranslation = 2
self.MotorSpeed = -1

name: MotorTargetVelocity
documentation: MotorTargetVelocity is the speed of the hinge motor in degrees per second. A positive value turns counterclockwise around `HingeAxis`.

name: Mount
documentation: Mount is where the wheel rests on its `Chassis`, in the chassis's frame. The engine records it when the wheel joint first forms, and the suspension springs back to it. Setting `Chassis` or `Axle` records it again.

name: MouseClick
documentation: MouseClick fires on the server when a player clicks this instance or one of its descendants within its activation distance. The callback receives the player.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a button part: open and close a door on click.
local door = Instance.new("Part")
door.Anchored = true
door.Size = Vector3.new(4, 7, 1)
door.Position = self.Position + Vector3.new(4, 2, 0)
door.Parent = game.World

self:AddComponent("ClickDetector")
self.MouseClick:Connect(function(player: Instance)
    local shut = door.Collider ~= "None"
    door.Collider = if shut then "None" else "Auto"
    door.Transparency = if shut then 0.7 else 0
    print(player.Name .. (if shut then " opened the door" else " closed the door"))
end)

name: MultiSelectColor3
documentation: MultiSelectColor3 is the color of the box a player drags to select several elements, and of the highlight behind each selected child.

name: MultiSelectTransparency
documentation: MultiSelectTransparency is the transparency of the multi-select drag box and the highlight behind each selected child.

name: MultiSelected
documentation: MultiSelected, when true, makes the element part of the current multiple selection.

name: Name
documentation: Name is the name of this instance in the scene tree.

name: NightSky
documentation: NightSky is a night texture that the atmosphere sky does not draw.
deprecation: Pick the Starry Night cube under Platform > Skies as the Panorama.

name: NoContactFriction
documentation: NoContactFriction makes the character's colliders slide with no friction.

name: NoTranslate
documentation: NoTranslate, when true, shows the element's `Text` as written, never translated to the player's language.

name: Normal
documentation: Normal is the asset id of a tangent-space normal map, with green pointing up the image as in glTF, so bumps and grooves show without more polygons. `"0"` lights the mesh by its own faces.

name: NormalCone
documentation: NormalCone is a swing limit of the swing-twist joint in degrees. The joint swings within one cone whose half-angle is the larger of `PlaneCone` and NormalCone.

name: Number
documentation: Number is the value of a number field. Player input keeps it between NumberMin and NumberMax.

name: NumberMax
documentation: NumberMax is the highest value the player can enter.

name: NumberMin
documentation: NumberMin is the lowest value the player can enter.

name: NumberStep
documentation: NumberStep is how much a number field changes per drag step or arrow key. 0 lets the value change smoothly.

name: Occlusion
documentation: Occlusion is the asset id of an ambient occlusion texture. Its red channel darkens the ambient light and the shadow fill in creases; local lights are not affected. `"0"` means none.

name: Occupant
documentation: Occupant is the character sitting on this seat, or nil. The character leaves with the seat's velocity when jumping off.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a car's seat: a part with a Seat component.
self:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Occupant"):Connect(function()
    local rider = self.Occupant
    print(if rider then rider.Name .. " got in" else "the seat is empty")
end)

while task.wait() do
    self:ApplyForce(Vector3.new(0, 0, -500 * self.SeatInput.Forward))
end

name: OffColor3
documentation: OffColor3 is the color of a toggle switch's track while `On` is false.

name: OffImage
documentation: OffImage is the asset id of the image on a toggle switch's track while it is off. `"0"` draws a plain track in `OffColor3`.

name: OffTransparency
documentation: OffTransparency is the transparency of a toggle switch's track while it is off, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: Offset
documentation: Offset slides the texture by X and Y texture widths along U and V; Z is ignored.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a conveyor part with a textured material.
self:AddComponent("UvTransform")
local SPEED = 0.5 -- widths per second

function Update(dt: number)
    local x = (self.Offset.X + SPEED * dt) % 1
    self.Offset = Vector3.new(x, 0, 0)
end

name: On
documentation: On is whether a toggle switch or UIToggleButton is on. Clicking flips it and fires `Activated`.

name: OnColor3
documentation: OnColor3 is the color of a toggle switch's track while `On` is true.

name: OnImage
documentation: OnImage is the asset id of the image on a toggle switch's track while it is on. `"0"` draws a plain track in `OnColor3`.

name: OnTransparency
documentation: OnTransparency is the transparency of a toggle switch's track while it is on, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: Op
documentation: Op is what a core menu setting control does when pressed: `"Show"` shows the current value, `"Previous"` steps back, and `"Next"` steps forward. A control outside the core menu ignores it.

name: Open
documentation: Open, when true, opens the dropdown's list. A click outside sets it to false.

name: Options
documentation: Options is the choices of a dropdown, separated by commas. The chosen entry is the one at SelectedIndex.

name: Orientation
documentation: Orientation is the world rotation of the instance as Euler angles in degrees: (pitch, yaw, roll), applied in YXZ order. A radian vector from the `rotation` library assigned to it raises no error and turns the instance by about 1/57 of the intended angle; convert it with `rotation.to_euler` or write it to RotationVector.
notes: On a camera with `CameraOrbit` or `CameraFly`, a write also sets the rig's `yaw` and `pitch`. While `CameraOrbit` follows a subject, the rig sets `Orientation` every frame; see game.World.Camera.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local r = rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(30))
self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(r)
print(math.round(self.Orientation.y)) -- prints 30

name: Other
documentation: Other is the part this part is welded to. Setting it makes the two parts one body in the pose they have at that moment; setting nil separates them again. The target must be another part with a physics body outside this part's assembly, or the weld does not form.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: weld a handle on top of it.
local handle = Instance.new("Part")
handle.Position = self.Position + Vector3.new(0, 2, 0)
handle.Parent = game.World
handle.Other = self

name: OuterAngle
documentation: OuterAngle is the half-angle, in radians from 0 to 1.57, of a spotlight's cone, which points along the instance's -Y axis.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: a warm spotlight that points down.
self:AddComponent("Light")
self:AddComponent("SpotCone")
self.LightColor = Vector3.new(1, 0.8, 0.5)
self.OuterAngle = math.rad(30)

name: OwnerUserId
documentation: OwnerUserId is the user id of the player who controls this character, or 0. Setting it on the server gives the character to that player: their movement input drives it and `CharacterAdded` fires. Setting it to 0 or another id takes the character from its player.
code_sample:
-- Server script: after 30 s, give each player without a character one.
task.delay(30, function()
    for player in game.World.Each("Player") do
        if player.Character == nil then
            local character = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
            character.Position = Vector3.new(0, 4, -12)
            character.OwnerUserId = player.UserId
        end
    end
end)

name: Page
documentation: Page is the core menu page this element belongs to. The element and everything under it show only while the core menu is on that page.

name: PanelColor3
documentation: PanelColor3 is the background color of a popup menu or dropdown list.

name: PanelTransparency
documentation: PanelTransparency is the transparency of a popup menu or dropdown list's background.

name: Panorama
documentation: Panorama is the asset id of a sky texture: a 2:1 equirectangular panorama or a cube texture. `"0"`, or a texture that fails to load, shows BackgroundColor. `AtmosphereSky` draws instead when the instance has it.

name: PanoramaEnergyMultiplier
documentation: PanoramaEnergyMultiplier is the brightness of a panorama sky, from 0 to 128, multiplied by BackgroundEnergyMultiplier.

name: PanoramaRotation
documentation: PanoramaRotation turns a panorama sky around the horizon, in degrees from 0 to 360.

name: Pants
documentation: Pants is the asset id of the clothing texture on the legs, or `"0"` for none.

name: Parent
documentation: Parent is the parent of this instance, or nil for an instance at the top of the place. Assign `game.World` to move an instance to the top. A destroyed instance reads nil, and writing its `Parent` is an error.
notes: The instance keeps its local offset and rotation, so under a positioned parent it moves to that pose in the parent's frame. Call SetParent to keep the world pose instead.
Assigning nil is deprecated and prints a warning once per run.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local lamp = Instance.new("Part")
lamp.Parent = self
lamp.Parent = game.World -- moves it to the top of the place
print(lamp.Parent == self) -- prints false

name: Part
documentation: Part is which body part this limb is: `"Head"`, `"Torso"`, `"LeftArm"`, `"RightArm"`, `"LeftLeg"` or `"RightLeg"`. It sets where the limb attaches, its collider size, and how animations map onto it.

name: Part
documentation: Part is which body part this limb is: `"Head"`, `"Torso"`, `"LeftArm"`, `"RightArm"`, `"LeftLeg"` or `"RightLeg"`. It sets where the limb attaches, its collider size, and how animations map onto it.

name: ParticleEmitter
documentation: create a particle emitter

name: Password
documentation: Password, when true, shows asterisks in the text box in place of what the player types. `Text` keeps the real characters.

name: Pause
documentation: Pause pauses a playing sound and keeps its place in the clip.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: pause the loop after 2 seconds.
self:AddComponent("Sound")
self.SoundId = "144115188075855954"
self.Looped = true
self:Play()

task.wait(2)
self:Pause()
print(self.Playing, self.Paused) -- prints false true

name: Paused
documentation: Paused is true while the sound is paused partway through. Pause sets it; Resume and Stop clear it.

name: PeakFriction
documentation: PeakFriction is the friction of a tire at its best slip. It mixes with the ground's friction like any part's friction.

name: Pivot
documentation: Pivot is the negated offset of the limb's joint, in units in the limb's frame.

name: PivotPoint
documentation: PivotPoint is the point the element turns and scales about, as a fraction of its size: `0, 0` is the top-left corner and `1, 1` the bottom-right. It applies to Rotation and Scale and moves nothing by itself.

name: PivotTo
type: (self: Instance, position: vector, rotation: vector, pivot: vector?) -> ()
documentation: PivotTo turns the instance to the world rotation `rotation` and moves it so that its own point `pivot` is at the world position `position`. Without `pivot`, it sets Position and RotationVector.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a door part 4 units wide: swing it open on its left edge.
self.Anchored = true
local hingeOnDoor = Vector3.new(-2, 0, 0)
local hinge = self:TransformPoint(hingeOnDoor)
self:PivotTo(hinge, rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(90)), hingeOnDoor)
print(math.round(self.Position.z)) -- prints -2

name: PlaceholderColor3
documentation: PlaceholderColor3 is the color of a text box's PlaceholderText. Until it is written, the placeholder draws in a dim gray.

name: PlaceholderText
documentation: PlaceholderText is the hint a text box shows while its `Text` is empty and it is not being typed in.

name: PlaneAxis
documentation: PlaneAxis is the reference axis of the swing-twist joint's swing, in the parent part's frame. The default zero vector means `(1, 0, 0)`.

name: PlaneCone
documentation: PlaneCone is a swing limit of the swing-twist joint in degrees. The joint swings within one cone whose half-angle is the larger of PlaneCone and `NormalCone`.

name: Play
documentation: Play starts the sound's clip from the beginning. The instance needs a Sound component.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: play a sound when the script starts.
self:AddComponent("Sound")
self.SoundId = "144115188075855954"
self:Play()
print(self.Playing) -- prints true

name: PlayAnimation
type: (self: Instance, clip: string, fade: number?, speed: number?) -> ()
documentation: PlayAnimation plays a clip on the character in place of its walk, idle and jump animations, until StopAnimation. `fade` is the blend time in seconds and defaults to the walk fade; `speed` multiplies the playback rate and defaults to 1.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait() -- a new character gets its animator at the next physics step
npc:PlayAnimation("sit", 0.2)

name: PlaybackSpeed
documentation: PlaybackSpeed scales the speed and pitch of the sound: 2 plays one octave up, 0.5 one octave down. Values below 0.05 play at 0.05, so 0 does not pause the sound.

name: Playing
documentation: Playing is true while the sound plays. It turns false when a clip that does not loop ends, on Pause or Stop, and when the audio fails to load.

name: PlotColor3
documentation: PlotColor3 is the color of a plot's lines or bars.

name: PlotTransparency
documentation: PlotTransparency is the transparency of a plot's lines or bars.

name: PlotType
documentation: PlotType is how a plot draws its samples: `"Lines"` joins them with a line, and `"Bars"` draws a bar from zero to each sample.

name: PointLight
documentation: create a light that shines in every direction

name: Popup
documentation: Popup, when true, closes the popup when the player clicks outside it.

name: PopupOpen
documentation: PopupOpen, when true, shows the popup panel above the rest of the interface.

name: PortColor3
documentation: PortColor3 is the wire color of a graph port.

name: PortTransparency
documentation: PortTransparency is the wire transparency of a graph port.

name: Portal
documentation: create a surface view that looks out of another face

name: Position
documentation: Position is the position of the instance in the world, in units. Descendants move with it. On a user interface element, `Position` is a `UDim2` that places the element in its parent, as UIPosition describes.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part with a light above it.
self.Anchored = true
local light = Instance.new("Part")
light.Anchored = true
light.Parent = self
light.Position = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)

self.Position = Vector3.new(10, 0, 0)
print(light.Position.x) -- prints 10

name: PrefabId
documentation: PrefabId is the id of the prefab this instance is a copy of, or 0. A linked copy saves as its prefab plus its own edits. See Prefabs.

name: Pressed
documentation: Pressed fires on the client when a mouse button or touch goes down on this control. On an `InputAction`, it fires when one of its bindings starts the action.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Parent = screen

button.Pressed:Connect(function()
    print("down")
end)

name: PressedImage
documentation: PressedImage is the asset id of the image shown in place of `Image` while the button is held down. `"0"` keeps `Image`.

name: PreviewAnimation
type: (self: Instance, clip: string, playing: boolean?, time: number?, speed: number?) -> boolean
documentation: PreviewAnimation opens an animation preview on the character, which shows one clip at a chosen `time` and `speed`, playing or paused. It returns whether the preview opened.
code_sample:
-- Server script: show the walk clip half a second in, paused.
local rig = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
print(rig:PreviewAnimation("walk", false, 0.5)) -- prints true

name: Priority
documentation: Priority is the order in which `InputContext` instances receive input, highest first. Contexts of the same priority all receive the input.

name: Progress
documentation: Progress is how full the progress bar is, from 0 to 1, drawn clamped to that range.

name: ProgressColor3
documentation: ProgressColor3 is the color of a progress bar's fill.

name: ProgressTrackColor3
documentation: ProgressTrackColor3 is the color of the track behind a progress bar's fill.

name: ProgressTrackTransparency
documentation: ProgressTrackTransparency is the transparency of the track behind a progress bar's fill.

name: ProgressTransparency
documentation: ProgressTransparency is the transparency of a progress bar's fill.

name: PushSample
documentation: PushSample adds a number to a UI plot. Once the plot is full, the oldest sample drops off. Only client scripts can call it.
code_sample:
-- Client script: plot the frame rate.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local plot = Instance.new("Frame")
plot:AddComponent("UIPlot")
plot.Parent = screen

function Update(dt: number)
    plot:PushSample(1 / dt)
end

name: Radio
documentation: Radio, when true, draws a round radio dot in place of a square check mark.

name: RadioGroup
documentation: RadioGroup is the number that ties radio buttons together: selecting one unselects the others with the same number.

name: Range
documentation: Range is how far, in units from 0 to 1000, a point light or spotlight reaches. The light fades to nothing at `Range`.

name: ReleaseFocus
documentation: ReleaseFocus takes keyboard focus away from this text box as a click elsewhere does and fires `FocusLost` with the boolean passed, or false when omitted.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local box = Instance.new("TextBox")
box.Parent = screen
box.FocusLost:Connect(function(enterPressed)
    print(enterPressed)
end)
box:CaptureFocus()
box:ReleaseFocus(true)

name: Released
documentation: Released fires on the client when a mouse button or touch comes up over this control. On an `InputAction`, it fires when the action ends.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Parent = screen

button.Released:Connect(function()
    print("up")
end)

name: Remaining
documentation: Remaining is how many seconds are left before this instance and everything under it are destroyed. A client counts down only instances it made.
code_sample:
-- Server script: make a brick that disappears after 5 seconds.
local brick = Instance.new("Part")
brick.Remaining = 5

name: RemoveComponent
documentation: RemoveComponent removes one or more components or `Tag` pairs from the instance. A component the instance does not have is skipped.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent("Light", "SpotCone")
self:RemoveComponent("SpotCone", "Light")
print(self:HasComponent("Light")) -- prints false

name: RenderDisabled
documentation: RenderDisabled, when true, hides the instance everywhere, shadows and decals included. Physics, raycasts and replication still work.

name: RepeatDelay
documentation: RepeatDelay is how many seconds a button or arrow key is held before it repeats every RepeatInterval.

name: RepeatInterval
documentation: RepeatInterval is the number of seconds between repeats while a button or key stays held.

name: ResampleMode
documentation: ResampleMode is how image pixels are sampled when the image draws larger or smaller than the texture: `"Default"` blends neighbors, and `"Pixelated"` keeps the square pixels of pixel art.

name: ResizableColumns
documentation: ResizableColumns, when true, lets players drag the dividers between table columns to resize them.

name: Restitution
documentation: Restitution is the bounciness of the part's surface. 0 does not bounce, 1 bounces back at full speed, and above 1 bounces faster. A part without its own Restitution reads its material's restitution, or 0.3 without a material.

name: Resume
documentation: Resume plays a paused sound from where it stopped.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: pause the loop for 2 seconds, then go on.
self:AddComponent("Sound")
self.SoundId = "144115188075855954"
self.Looped = true
self:Play()

self:Pause()
task.wait(2)
self:Resume()
print(self.Playing) -- prints true

name: RichText
documentation:
RichText, when true, draws `Text` as markup with lowercase `` (weight 700), ``, ``, `
` and the `<` `>` `"` `'` `&` escapes. Markup that does not parse draws as written, and a text box ignores `RichText`.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Parent = screen
label.RichText = true
label.Text = 'Score: 10 <font color="#ff4040">-2</font>'

name: Right
documentation: Right is the Input.Key on an `InputBinding` that adds +1 on X to a `Direction2D` action while held. 0 binds no key.

name: RollOffMaxDistance
documentation: RollOffMaxDistance is the distance, in units, past which the sound cannot be heard.

name: RollOffMinDistance
documentation: RollOffMinDistance is the distance, in units, within which the sound plays at full volume.

name: RollOffScale
documentation: RollOffScale is how fast the sound gets quieter past RollOffMinDistance: the volume is multiplied by `min / (min + RollOffScale * (distance - min))`, where `min` is `RollOffMinDistance`. At 0 the sound keeps full volume out to RollOffMaxDistance.

name: RollingResistance
documentation: RollingResistance is the torque against a tire's rolling, as a fraction of its load.

name: RootMotion
documentation: RootMotion adds the root bone's movement in the playing clips to the character's horizontal velocity each frame. It needs Character.

name: RopeAnchor
documentation: RopeAnchor is where the rope attaches to this part, in units in its frame.

name: Rotate
documentation: Rotate turns the instance by an angle in radians around an axis in its own frame.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:Rotate(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(90))
print(math.round(self.Orientation.y)) -- prints 90

name: Rotation
documentation: Rotation turns the element and everything under it clockwise by this many degrees about its PivotPoint, after layout, so the box keeps its place in a list.

name: RotationVector
documentation: RotationVector is the world rotation of the instance as an axis-angle vector in radians like the ones the `rotation` library makes. Descendants turn with it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.RotationVector = rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(90))
print(math.round(self.Orientation.y)) -- prints 90

name: RttMs
documentation: RttMs is the round trip time between the server and this player, in milliseconds, smoothed over recent packets. It reads 0 on clients, which read their own from Session.RttMs.

name: SampleCount
documentation: SampleCount is how many samples a plot keeps across its width, from 1 to 128. When the plot is full, each new sample pushes out the oldest.

name: Saturation
documentation: Saturation is the saturation picked in a color picker, from 0 (gray) to 1 (full color). Dragging left or right changes it.

name: ScaleMax
documentation: ScaleMax is the value at the top edge of a plot. When `ScaleMax` is at or below ScaleMin, the plot fits its height to its samples.

name: ScaleMin
documentation: ScaleMin is the value at the bottom edge of a plot. When `ScaleMin` is at or above ScaleMax, the plot fits its height to its samples.

name: ScaleType
documentation: ScaleType is how the image fills an element of a different size. `"Stretch"` scales it to the element, `"Slice"` keeps the corners at their size (see SliceCenter), `"Tile"` repeats it at TileSize, `"Fit"` fits it inside, and `"Crop"` covers the element and cuts the overflow.

name: ScreenGui
documentation: create a full-screen interface root

name: ScreenInsets
documentation: ScreenInsets is which core UI screen edges the element stays clear of, from `game.Enum.ScreenInsets`. `"CoreUISafeInsets"` lays the element out in the screen minus every edge reserved with InsetEdge, and `"TopbarSafeInsets"` minus only the top edge. It works only in the screen UI.

name: ScrollBarMax
documentation: ScrollBarMax is the end of a scroll bar's range, in units the script picks.

name: ScrollBarMin
documentation: ScrollBarMin is the start of a scroll bar's range, in units the script picks.

name: ScrollBarPage
documentation: ScrollBarPage is how much of a scroll bar's range shows at once, in the units of ScrollBarMin and ScrollBarMax.

name: ScrollBarThickness
documentation: ScrollBarThickness is the width in pixels of the bar a scrolling frame draws while its canvas is taller than the frame. 0 draws none; the wheel and keys still scroll.

name: ScrollBarValue
documentation: ScrollBarValue is the scroll position. Dragging or clicking the bar changes it and keeps it between ScrollBarMin and `ScrollBarMax - ScrollBarPage`.

name: ScrollFollowing
documentation: ScrollFollowing, when true, keeps the frame scrolled to the bottom as children are added or the scroll area grows.

name: ScrollingFrame
documentation: create a frame that scrolls

name: SearchBox
documentation: SearchBox, when true, shows a clear button at the right end of the text box while it has text. Clicking it sets `Text` to `""`.

name: Selectable
documentation: Selectable, when true, lets the arrow keys, d-pad and left stick move the selection onto the element. When it is false, the pointer can still press it.

name: Selected
documentation: Selected, when true, makes this radio button the chosen option of its group.

name: SelectedIndex
documentation: SelectedIndex is the 1-based index, in layout order, of the chosen child item, or 0 for none. The selection highlight draws behind that child. In a tab view it is the open tab.

name: SelectedTabColor3
documentation: SelectedTabColor3 is the color of the open tab's button.

name: SelectedTabTransparency
documentation: SelectedTabTransparency is the transparency of the open tab's button.

name: SelectionChanged
documentation: SelectionChanged fires on the client when this control gains or loses the keyboard and gamepad selection, `game.Input.Selected`. The callback receives true when the control becomes selected and false when the selection leaves it.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local button = Instance.new("TextButton")
button.Text = "Play"
button.Parent = screen
button.SelectionChanged:Connect(function(selected)
    button.BackgroundTransparency = if selected then 0 else 0.5
end)
game.Input.Selected = button

name: SelectionColor3
documentation: SelectionColor3 is the color of the highlight behind the selected list item.

name: SelectionGroup
documentation: SelectionGroup, when true, keeps the arrow keys, d-pad and left stick from moving the selection out of this container, so a player in an inventory window cannot step onto the hotbar behind it. A script write to `game.Input.Selected` can still select outside it.

name: SelectionRing
documentation: SelectionRing, when true, draws the blue ring around the element while it is selected. False leaves the selected look to the element, which can draw it from `SelectionChanged`.

name: SelectionScope
documentation: SelectionScope is the UI element within which an `InputContext` is active: the context receives input only while `game.Input.Selected` is that element or inside it, or everywhere when nil. A scoped context receives input before every unscoped one, whatever their `Priority`.
notes: An inner `SelectionGroup` stops the scope, so a popup that has the selection turns off the keys of the list it opens from.
With `Sink`, the keys its actions bind go to those actions instead of moving or activating the selection or opening the menu.

name: SelectionStart
documentation: SelectionStart is the byte position, counted from 1, of the end of the selection opposite the caret in a focused text box, or -1 when nothing is selected or the box has no focus. Writing it selects the text between it and the caret.

name: SelectionTransparency
documentation: SelectionTransparency is the transparency of the highlight behind the selected list item, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: SetAngularVelocity
documentation: SetAngularVelocity sets the world angular velocity of the physics body in radians per second.
deprecation: Attach `AngVelocity` with Instance:AddComponent and write the `AngVelocity` column on World.Query.

name: SetBodyMotion
documentation: SetBodyMotion switches the physics body between moving under physics (`"dynamic"`) and moving only where a script puts it (`"kinematic"`).
deprecation: Attach or remove the Kinematic component with Instance:AddComponent and Instance:RemoveComponent.

name: SetHearingSense
type: function SetHearingSense(self, sensitivity: number, collisionMask: number?): ()
documentation: SetHearingSense sets how well the instance hears and which collision groups it hears. A mask of 0 hears all groups.
deprecation: Attach `HearingSense` with Instance:AddComponent and configure fields with World.Query.

name: SetLinearVelocity
documentation: SetLinearVelocity sets the world velocity of the physics body in units per second.

name: SetParent
documentation: SetParent moves the instance under a new parent and keeps its world pose, unless `keepWorld` is false.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local wheel = Instance.new("Part")
wheel.Parent = game.World
wheel.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
wheel:SetParent(self) -- keeps its world position
print(wheel.Position.y) -- prints 10

name: SetStateEnabled
documentation: SetStateEnabled sets whether a character enters a movement state by itself. With `"Jumping"` off it ignores the jump input; with `"GettingUp"` off a character in `"Ragdoll"` or `"FallingDown"` stays down. To keep a character from falling over, turn off both `"Ragdoll"`, which a hard hit causes, and `"FallingDown"`, which tipping too far causes.
code_sample:
-- Server script: a character that carries a crate cannot jump or fall over.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:SetStateEnabled("Jumping", false)
npc:SetStateEnabled("Ragdoll", false)
npc:SetStateEnabled("FallingDown", false)

name: SetSwingTwistJoint
documentation: SetSwingTwistJoint sets the angle limits, anchor and axes of the instance's swing-twist joint.
deprecation: Assign the `SwingTwistJoint` properties (Anchor, TwistAxis, PlaneAxis, PlaneCone, NormalCone, TwistMin, TwistMax, FrictionTorque).

name: SetVisionCone
type: function SetVisionCone(self, range: number, fieldOfView: number, eyeOffsetY: number?, collisionMask: number?): ()
documentation: SetVisionCone sets how far and how wide the instance sees, its eye height (1.5 by default), and which collision groups it sees (0 sees all).
deprecation: Attach `VisionCone` with Instance:AddComponent and configure fields with World.Query.

name: Setting
documentation: Setting is the player setting a core menu control changes, such as `"Quality"`, `"FieldOfView"` or `"MusicVolume"`. A control outside the core menu ignores it.

name: ShadeFill
documentation: ShadeFill, when true, lightens the fill of a clickable element under the pointer, and more while pressed.

name: ShadowOff
documentation: ShadowOff, when true, stops the instance from casting shadows. It still receives shadows.

name: Shirt
documentation: Shirt is the asset id of the clothing texture on the torso and arms, or `"0"` for none.

name: Shortcut
documentation: Shortcut is text shown at the right of a menu item, such as `"Ctrl+S"`. It does not bind the key.

name: Side
documentation: Side is the face of the parent part that a decal shows on: `"Right"` (+X), `"Top"` (+Y), `"Back"` (+Z), `"Left"` (-X), `"Bottom"` (-Y) or `"Front"` (-Z). A parent with a mesh places the decal by the mesh's UVs.

name: Sink
documentation: Sink stops the keys and UI buttons of an `InputContext`'s enabled actions from reaching lower-priority contexts and the character controls.
code_sample:
-- Client script: Space fires a jetpack instead of jumping.
local jetpack = Instance.new("InputContext")
jetpack.Sink = true
local thrust = Instance.new("InputAction")
thrust.Parent = jetpack
local space = Instance.new("InputBinding")
space.KeyCode = game.Input.Key.Space
space.Parent = thrust

thrust.Pressed:Connect(function()
    print("thrust")
end)

name: Size
documentation: Size is the size of the instance along its local axes in units: (width, height, depth). On a user interface element, `Size` is a `UDim2` relative to its parent, as UISize describes.

name: SizeModeX
documentation: SizeModeX is how the element's width is set. `"Fixed"` uses `Size.X`, `"Fit"` fits the width to the children, and `"Grow"` fills the room the parent gives, shared among a list's `"Grow"` children.

name: SizeModeY
documentation: SizeModeY is how the element's height is set, as SizeModeX sets the width.

name: SkyboxBk
documentation: SkyboxBk is the asset id of the back face (+Z) of a six-sided sky. If every face is `"0"` or any face fails to load, the sky shows BackgroundColor. `AtmosphereSky` and `PanoramaSky` draw instead when the instance has either.

name: SkyboxDn
documentation: SkyboxDn is the asset id of the bottom face (-Y) of a six-sided sky.

name: SkyboxEnergyMultiplier
documentation: SkyboxEnergyMultiplier is the brightness of a six-sided sky, from 0 to 128, multiplied by BackgroundEnergyMultiplier.

name: SkyboxFt
documentation: SkyboxFt is the asset id of the front face (-Z) of a six-sided sky.

name: SkyboxLf
documentation: SkyboxLf is the asset id of the left face (-X) of a six-sided sky.

name: SkyboxRotation
documentation: SkyboxRotation turns a six-sided sky around the horizon, in degrees from 0 to 360.

name: SkyboxRt
documentation: SkyboxRt is the asset id of the right face (+X) of a six-sided sky.

name: SkyboxUp
documentation: SkyboxUp is the asset id of the top face (+Y) of a six-sided sky.

name: SliceCenter
documentation: SliceCenter is the stretching middle of a `"Slice"` image, in image pixels. The pixels left of `Min.X`, above `Min.Y`, right of `Max.X` and below `Max.Y` are corners and edges that keep their size.

name: SliceScale
documentation: SliceScale is the size of a `"Slice"` image's corners and edges as a multiple of their image size.

name: Slider
documentation: create a slider

name: SliderFormat
documentation: SliderFormat is a format string for the slider's value label, with string formatting specifiers for the number. An empty string shows the plain number.

name: SliderValue
documentation: SliderValue is the current value of a slider. Dragging moves it between MinValue and MaxValue and fires `Activated`.

name: Slot
documentation: Slot is the socket an accessory attaches to: `"Hat"`, `"Hair"`, `"Face"`, `"Back"`, `"LeftShoulder"`, `"RightShoulder"`, `"Waist"`, `"Front"` or `"Neck"`.

name: SortColumn
documentation: SortColumn is the column, counted from 0, that a table sorts by, or -1 for none. Clicking a sortable column header changes `SortColumn`; a column that does not exist turns sorting off.

name: SortDescending
documentation: SortDescending, when true, sorts the table from highest to lowest.

name: Sound
documentation: create a sound

name: SoundId
documentation: SoundId is the asset id of the audio clip, as a string of digits such as `"144115188075855954"`. Write it in quotes: a Luau number cannot represent every digit, so an unquoted id names a different asset. In Studio, Copy ID on the sound field gives the id, and Import… imports an `.ogg` file.

name: Spacing
documentation: Spacing is the gap in pixels between a list's children along the direction it stacks them.

name: SpawnPoint
documentation: SpawnPoint lets characters spawn at this instance's position.

name: Sphere
documentation: create a sphere part

name: SpinSpeed
documentation: SpinSpeed is the spin in radians per second that the wheel's motor drives the wheel toward, with up to `DriveTorque`. At 0 the motor brakes. The engine limits the spin to 754 radians per second.

name: SpotLight
documentation: create a cone of light

name: SpringDamping
documentation: SpringDamping is how fast a wheel's suspension stops bouncing. At 1 the wheel settles without bouncing, and at 0 it bounces forever.

name: SpringFrequency
documentation: SpringFrequency is the stiffness of a wheel's suspension in bounces per second, whatever the masses. At 0 the wheel slides freely within `Travel`.

name: StallAngle
documentation: StallAngle is the angle of attack in degrees past which a wing's lift coefficient stops growing.

name: StarLuminance
documentation: StarLuminance is the star brightness of a night texture that the atmosphere does not draw.
deprecation: Pick the Starry Night cube as the Panorama and set PanoramaEnergyMultiplier.

name: StartTimer
documentation: StartTimer starts or restarts the countdown timer on the instance.

name: State
documentation: State is what the character is doing: `"Running"`, `"FreeFall"`, `"Jumping"`, `"Climbing"`, `"Swimming"`, `"Seated"`, `"Ragdoll"`, `"FallingDown"`, `"GettingUp"`, `"Dead"`, `"PlatformStanding"` or `"Physics"`.
code_sample:
-- Server script: print each state a character enters.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:GetPropertyChangedSignal("State"):Connect(function()
    print(npc.State)
end)
npc:ChangeState("Ragdoll")

name: StateChanged
documentation: StateChanged fires on the client when an `InputAction` turns on or off, passing `true` or `false`, or when a `Direction2D` action's vector changes, passing the new vector. A tap within one frame fires it twice, `true` then `false`.
code_sample:
-- Client script: report when the player presses and releases F.
local tools = Instance.new("InputContext")
local flashlight = Instance.new("InputAction")
flashlight.Parent = tools
local f = Instance.new("InputBinding")
f.KeyCode = game.Input.Key.F
f.Parent = flashlight

flashlight.StateChanged:Connect(function(on)
    print(if on then "pressed" else "released")
end)

name: Steer
documentation: Steer is the right input of the character sitting on this seat, from -1 to 1.

name: SteerLimit
documentation: SteerLimit is how far in degrees a `Steers` wheel may turn either way. At 0 the wheel stays straight.

name: SteerTarget
documentation: SteerTarget is the angle in degrees the steering spring turns a `Steers` wheel toward, within `SteerLimit`.

name: Steers
documentation: Steers lets a wheel turn about the chassis's up direction toward `SteerTarget`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a front wheel: let it steer up to 30 degrees and turn it 20.
self.Steers = true
self.SteerLimit = 30
self.SteerTarget = 20

name: Steps
documentation: Steps is the number of stops along a slider's track, from 2 to 255.

name: StickCenter
documentation: StickCenter is the base of the thumbstick, from the element's center, as fractions of its width and height from -0.5 to 0.5. In `"Dynamic"` and `"Following"` modes the base moves to where the touch starts.

name: StickDeadzone
documentation: StickDeadzone is how far the thumb must move, as a fraction of StickRadius, before StickDirection leaves (0, 0).

name: StickDirection
documentation: StickDirection is the direction from the thumbstick's base toward the thumb, X and Y from -1 to 1 with +Y down.

name: StickMode
documentation: StickMode is how the thumbstick base follows the touch: `"Fixed"` keeps it at StickCenter, `"Dynamic"` moves it to where the touch starts, and `"Following"` drags it along when the thumb goes past StickRadius.

name: StickRadius
documentation: StickRadius is how far, in pixels, the thumb can move from the center of the base.

name: StickTip
documentation: StickTip is where the thumb is relative to the base, in multiples of StickRadius. It returns to (0, 0) on release.

name: Stop
documentation: Stop stops the sound and goes back to the start of the clip.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: an alarm that rings for 2 seconds.
self:AddComponent("Sound")
self.SoundId = "144115188075855954"
self.Looped = true
self:Play()

task.wait(2)
self:Stop()
print(self.Playing) -- prints false

name: StopAnimation
