documentation: StopAnimation stops the clips a script played and any preview, so the walk, idle and jump animations play again. `fade` is the fade-out time in seconds.
code_sample:
-- Server script: sit for 3 seconds.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
npc:PlayAnimation("sit")
task.wait(3)
npc:StopAnimation(0.2)

name: StopPreview
documentation: StopPreview closes the animation preview on the character and returns whether one was open.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local rig = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
task.wait()
rig:PreviewAnimation("walk", false)
print(rig:StopPreview()) -- prints true

name: StopTimer
documentation: StopTimer stops the countdown timer on the instance and sets `TimeLeft` to 0.

name: StripeColor3
documentation: StripeColor3 is the color of every other line of a list or grid.

name: StripeTransparency
documentation: StripeTransparency is the transparency of the stripes, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: SunDiskScale
documentation: SunDiskScale is the size of the sun disk of the place's Sun.

name: SurfaceCanvasSizeX
documentation: SurfaceCanvasSizeX is the width in pixels of the 2D canvas drawn on a face of the parent part.

name: SurfaceCanvasSizeY
documentation: SurfaceCanvasSizeY is the height in pixels of the 2D canvas drawn on a face of the parent part.

name: SurfaceFace
documentation: SurfaceFace is the face of the parent part the surface UI draws on: `"Right"`, `"Top"`, `"Back"`, `"Left"`, `"Bottom"` or `"Front"`.

name: SurfaceGui
documentation: create an interface surface on a part face

name: SurfaceLightInfluence
documentation: SurfaceLightInfluence is how much scene lighting shades the surface canvas, from 0 (always full brightness) to 255 (lit like the scene).

name: SurfaceMaxDistance
documentation: SurfaceMaxDistance is how far, in world units, the local character can be from the surface and still use its controls; 0 allows any distance.

name: SurfacePixelsPerUnit
documentation: SurfacePixelsPerUnit is how many canvas pixels cover one world unit of the face. When positive it sets the canvas size; 0 uses SurfaceCanvasSizeX and SurfaceCanvasSizeY.

name: SurfaceView
documentation: create a surface view that shows a camera

name: SuspensionDamping
documentation: SuspensionDamping is the damping against suspension speed, as a multiple of the parent part's mass. At 0 the parent part keeps bouncing.

name: SuspensionDirection
documentation: SuspensionDirection is the direction the wheel drops from `SuspensionHardpoint`, in the parent part's frame. A zero vector turns the suspension off.

name: SuspensionHardpoint
documentation: SuspensionHardpoint is where the raycast suspension of a wheel part mounts on the wheel's parent part, in units in the parent's frame. A ray from this point finds the ground, and the spring pushes the parent upward at this point.

name: SuspensionMaxLength
documentation: SuspensionMaxLength is the farthest the wheel hangs from `SuspensionHardpoint`, in units. Past it the wheel leaves the ground.

name: SuspensionMinLength
documentation: SuspensionMinLength is the shortest the suspension compresses to, in units. The spring pushes no harder past it.

name: SuspensionRestLength
documentation: SuspensionRestLength is the distance in units from `SuspensionHardpoint` where the spring pushes with no force.

name: SuspensionStiffness
documentation: SuspensionStiffness is the spring force per unit of compression, as a multiple of the parent part's mass.

name: SuspensionWheelRadius
documentation: SuspensionWheelRadius is the radius of the wheel in units for the raycast suspension.

name: SwatchColor3
documentation: SwatchColor3 is the color of a color swatch button.

name: SwatchPreview
documentation: SwatchPreview is how a color swatch shows transparency: `"Opaque"` ignores it, `"Checker"` draws the color over a checkerboard, and `"Half"` draws the solid color on the left half and the checkerboard on the right.

name: SwatchTransparency
documentation: SwatchTransparency is the transparency of the color swatch.

name: SwitchWidth
documentation: SwitchWidth is the width in pixels of a toggle switch's track; 0 makes it twice the element's height.

name: TabColor3
documentation: TabColor3 is the color of the buttons of tabs that are not open.

name: TabTransparency
documentation: TabTransparency is the transparency of the buttons of tabs that are not open.

name: TakeDamage
type: function TakeDamage(self, amount: number, attacker: Instance?): ()
documentation: TakeDamage lowers the health of a character, or of the character a body part belongs to, and records `attacker`. A negative amount heals.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:TakeDamage(30)
print(npc.Health) -- prints 70

name: Team
documentation: Team is the team number of this player or character, or 0 for none.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local red = Instance.new("Team")
red.Name = "Red"
red.TeamColor = Vector3.new(1, 0, 0)
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Instance)
    player.Team = red.TeamId
end)

name: TeamColor
documentation: TeamColor is the team color in the player list and chat.

name: TeamId
documentation: TeamId is this team's number.

name: Text
documentation: Text is the text of a label, text box or button. With a `"Fit"` size mode, the element sizes to it.

name: TextBox
documentation: create a text field

name: TextButton
documentation: create a clickable text label

name: TextColor3
documentation: TextColor3 is the color of the text.

name: TextLabel
documentation: create a text interface element

name: TextSize
documentation: TextSize is the height of the text in pixels, from 1 to 512.

name: TextStrokeColor3
documentation: TextStrokeColor3 is the color of the outline around the text.

name: TextStrokeScale
documentation: TextStrokeScale, from 0 to 0.1, adds `TextStrokeScale * TextSize` pixels to TextStrokeWidth, so the outline keeps its ratio to the text at any size. Larger values make outlines overlap neighboring letters.

name: TextStrokeTransparency
documentation: TextStrokeTransparency is the transparency of the text outline, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: TextStrokeWidth
documentation: TextStrokeWidth is how many pixels, from 0 to 64, the text outline grows outward, clamped to about `TextSize / 6`. With TextStrokeScale also 0, there is no outline.

name: TextTransparency
documentation: TextTransparency is the transparency of the text, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: TextTruncate
documentation: TextTruncate is how a line of text that runs past the element's width ends. `"AtEnd"` ends the line at the last letter that fits and draws an ellipsis; `"None"` lets it run past. A text box and wrapped text are not affected.

name: TextWrapped
documentation: TextWrapped, when true, breaks lines at spaces to fit the element's width. When false, a long line is cut off or runs past the element.

name: TextXAlignment
documentation: TextXAlignment aligns the text horizontally in the element: `"Left"`, `"Center"` or `"Right"`.

name: TextYAlignment
documentation: TextYAlignment aligns the text vertically in the element: `"Top"`, `"Center"` or `"Bottom"`.

name: Texture
documentation: Texture is the asset id of the image a decal shows. `"0"` draws nothing. `Color` tints the image and `Transparency` fades it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: put a sign on its top face.
local sign = Instance.new("Decal")
sign.Texture = "123456789" -- the asset id of your image
sign.Side = "Top"
sign.Parent = self

name: Throttle
documentation: Throttle is the forward input of the character sitting on this seat, from -1 to 1.

name: ThumbColor3
documentation: ThumbColor3 is the color of the slider's thumb.

name: ThumbCornerRadius
documentation: ThumbCornerRadius is the corner radius in pixels, 0 to 1000, of the slider's thumb. 0 draws a round thumb.

name: ThumbImage
documentation: ThumbImage is the asset id of the image on the slider's thumb. `"0"` draws a plain thumb in `ThumbColor3`.

name: ThumbSize
documentation: ThumbSize is the diameter of a round slider thumb or the side of a square one, in pixels from 0 to 1000.

name: ThumbTransparency
documentation: ThumbTransparency is the transparency of the slider's thumb, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: TickColor3
documentation: TickColor3 is the color of the tick marks along the slider's track.

name: TickLength
documentation: TickLength is the length in pixels, 0 to 1000, of the tick marks across the slider's track; 0 draws none.

name: TickTransparency
documentation: TickTransparency is the transparency of the tick marks, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: TileSize
documentation: TileSize is the size of one tile of a `"Tile"` image: the scale is a fraction of the element's size and the offset is pixels. A zero side draws one tile across that side.

name: Tiling
documentation: Tiling scales the U and V texture coordinates by X and Y; Z is ignored. Values above 1 repeat the texture, values between 0 and 1 stretch it, and negative values mirror it. Triplanar and stud materials, and the clothing layer that Color describes, ignore `UvTransform`.

name: TimeLeft
documentation: TimeLeft is the number of seconds left on the countdown, or 0 when the timer is not running.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent("Timer")
self.WaitTime = 10
self:AddComponent("TimerRunning")

task.wait(4)
print(math.round(self.TimeLeft)) -- prints 6

name: Timeout
documentation: Timeout fires each time the countdown reaches zero.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: chime 3 times, 1 second apart.
self:AddComponent("Timer")
self.WaitTime = 1

local count = 0
self.Timeout:Connect(function()
    count += 1
    print("chime", count)
    if count == 3 then
        self:RemoveComponent("TimerRunning")
    end
end)

self:AddComponent("TimerRunning")

name: TimerAutostart
documentation: TimerAutostart starts the timer from `WaitTime` when the instance enters the world, then sets itself back to `false`.

name: TimerOneShot
documentation: TimerOneShot stops the timer after one countdown. Without it, the timer starts over each time it fires.

name: TimerPaused
documentation: TimerPaused pauses the countdown and keeps `TimeLeft`.

name: TitleHeight
documentation: TitleHeight is the height in pixels of a window's title bar, which the player drags to move the window.

name: Toggle
documentation: create an on and off switch

name: TogglePrefab
documentation: TogglePrefab is the name of a prefab whose spawned UI root this button shows or hides when clicked. The engine sets the button's `On` while that root is visible.

name: ToggleTarget
documentation: ToggleTarget is the `UIRoot` that TogglePrefab names, or nil while none exists.

name: TouchEnded
documentation: TouchEnded fires when a body stops touching this part. The other instance may already be destroyed; check IsAlive before indexing it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a pressure plate part.
self.Anchored = true
self.TouchEnded:Connect(function(other: Instance)
    if other:IsAlive() then
        print(other.Name, "stepped off")
    end
end)

local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.Name = "Crate"
crate.Position = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
crate.Parent = game.World
task.wait(1)
crate.Position = Vector3.new(20, 3, 0)

name: Touched
documentation: Touched fires when a body starts touching this part. For a player, the other instance is a limb such as `Left Leg`, or the character itself when its capsule overlaps the part; `game.Players.FromCharacter` takes either. A tool a character holds fires `Touched` for what it touches, but never for its holder. Reading `Touched`, `TouchEnded` or `Hit` on an instance without a `Shape` or `Collider` raises an error.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a lava part: destroy whatever lands on it.
self.Anchored = true
self.Touched:Connect(function(other: Instance)
    print(other.Name, "burns")
    other:Destroy()
end)

local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.Name = "Crate"
crate.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
crate.Parent = game.World

name: TrackAxis
documentation: TrackAxis is the way the slider runs: `"Horizontal"` left to right, or `"Vertical"` up and down.

name: TrackColor3
documentation: TrackColor3 is the color of the unfilled part of the slider's track.

name: TrackImage
documentation: TrackImage is the asset id of the image on the unfilled part of the slider's track. `"0"` draws a plain track in `TrackColor3`.

name: TrackThickness
documentation: TrackThickness is the thickness in pixels, 0 to 1000, of the slider's track.

name: TrackTransparency
documentation: TrackTransparency is the transparency of the unfilled track, from 0 (opaque) to 1 (invisible).

name: TransformDirection
documentation: TransformDirection turns a direction in the instance's own frame into a world direction.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 90, 0)
local forward = self:TransformDirection(Vector3.new(0, 0, -1))
print(math.round(forward.x)) -- prints -1

name: TransformPoint
documentation: TransformPoint turns a position in the instance's own frame into a world position.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a gun part: find the muzzle 2 units in front of it.
self.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
self.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 90, 0)
local muzzle = self:TransformPoint(Vector3.new(0, 0, -2))
print(math.round(muzzle.x)) -- prints -2

name: Transparency
documentation: Transparency is how see-through the surface is, from 0 (solid) to 1 (invisible). It does not change collisions or raycasts.

name: Travel
documentation: Travel is how far in units a wheel moves up and down from its `Mount`. 0 is a rigid axle.

name: Trigger
documentation: Trigger lets parts and characters pass through this part while it still fires `Touched` and `TouchEnded`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a checkpoint part that crates fall through.
self.Anchored = true
self.Trigger = true
self.Touched:Connect(function(other: Instance)
    print(other.Name, "passed")
end)

local crate = Instance.new("Part")
crate.Name = "Crate"
crate.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
crate.Parent = game.World

name: TwistAxis
documentation: TwistAxis is the axis `TwistMin` and `TwistMax` limit rotation around, in the parent part's frame. The default zero vector means `(0, 1, 0)`.

name: TwistMax
documentation: TwistMax is the upper rotation limit in degrees around `TwistAxis`, from the rest pose.

name: TwistMin
documentation: TwistMin is the lower rotation limit in degrees around `TwistAxis`, from the rest pose.

name: Type
documentation: Type is the basic shape of a part, used for drawing, raycasts and its default collider: `"Box"`, `"Sphere"`, `"Cylinder"` (along Y), `"Cone"` (pointing +Y) or `"Wedge"` (sloping along -Z), scaled by `Size`. A part with a `Mesh` draws the mesh instead. On an `InputAction`, Type is an Input.ActionType.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: drop a ball above it.
local ball = Instance.new("Part")
ball.Type = "Sphere"
ball.Size = Vector3.new(2, 2, 2)
ball.Position = self.Position + Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
ball.Parent = game.World

name: UIButton
documentation: UIButton is the UI button that presses the binding's `Parent` action when the player presses or taps it; nil binds no button. On a `Direction2D` action, a thumbstick button adds its `StickDirection` with up as +Y.

name: UIClickable
documentation: UIClickable, when true, makes the element take pointer clicks and fire click signals. When it is false, clicks pass through to the elements behind.

name: UIPosition
documentation: UIPosition is the old name of a UI element's Position. Reading or writing it warns `Instance.UIPosition is deprecated; use Instance.Position`.

name: UIRoot
documentation: UIRoot, when true, makes the element the top of its own screen layer. An element under `game.Overlay` draws only when it or an ancestor below `game.Overlay` has UIRoot set to true.

name: UISize
documentation: UISize is the old name of a UI element's Size. Reading or writing it warns `Instance.UISize is deprecated; use Instance.Size`.

name: UISurfaceAlwaysOnTop
documentation: UISurfaceAlwaysOnTop, when true, draws the surface UI in front of everything in the 3D scene.

name: UIToggleButton
documentation: UIToggleButton, when true, makes the button stay pressed after a click and pop back up on the next click.

name: Underlay
documentation: Underlay is the asset id of a second texture drawn under Albedo and over the surface color. It draws only when the instance has its own Color, is a character part with a body color, or has a mesh file that colors the sub-mesh. `"0"` means none.

name: UnequipTools
documentation: UnequipTools puts the tool the character holds back in its hotbar slot.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
npc:EquipTool(Instance.new("Tool"))
npc:UnequipTools()
print(npc:GetTool()) -- prints nil

name: Unequipped
documentation: Unequipped fires when a character unequips or drops this tool. On the server it also fires when the holding character dies. The callback receives the player, or nil for a character no player controls.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local npc = assert(game.Prefabs.Spawn("Character"))
local sword = Instance.new("Tool")
sword.Unequipped:Connect(function()
    print("put away")
end)
npc:EquipTool(sword)
npc:UnequipTools() -- prints put away

name: Up
documentation: Up is the Input.Key on an `InputBinding` that adds +1 on Y to a `Direction2D` action while held. 0 binds no key. The action adds all its bindings and shortens a sum longer than 1, so W and D together read about (0.707, 0.707).
code_sample:
-- Client script: read WASD as one direction.
local gameplay = Instance.new("InputContext")
local steer = Instance.new("InputAction")
steer.Type = "Direction2D"
steer.Parent = gameplay
local wasd = Instance.new("InputBinding")
wasd.Up = game.Input.Key.W
wasd.Down = game.Input.Key.S
wasd.Left = game.Input.Key.A
wasd.Right = game.Input.Key.D
wasd.Parent = steer

steer.StateChanged:Connect(function(direction)
    print(direction)
end)

name: UpDirection
documentation: UpDirection is the direction the character stands along. Floor checks, jumps and the force that keeps it upright follow it.

name: UpperTranslation
documentation: UpperTranslation is the longest `Distance` the rope motor reels out to. The motor stops there.

name: UseLimits
documentation: UseLimits keeps the hinge angle between `LimitsMin` and `LimitsMax`. With both limits at their default of 0, the hinge does not turn.

name: UseMotor
documentation: UseMotor turns the hinge at `MotorTargetVelocity` with up to `MotorForce`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: spin a platform on top of it a quarter turn per second.
self.Anchored = true

local top = Instance.new("Part")
top.Size = Vector3.new(6, 0.5, 6)
top.Position = self.Position + Vector3.new(0, 1.5, 0)
top.Parent = game.World
top.HingeAxis = Vector3.new(0, 1, 0)
top.MotorForce = 10000
top.MotorTargetVelocity = 90
top.UseMotor = true
top.ConnectedBody = self

name: UserId
documentation: UserId is the account user id of this player, or 0.

name: Value
documentation: Value is the step the slider's thumb is on, from 0 to `Steps - 1`. Dragging the thumb changes it and fires `Activated`.

name: VectorCount
documentation: VectorCount is how many fields a vector input shows: 2 (X, Y) or 3 (X, Y, Z).

name: VectorMax
documentation: VectorMax is the highest value a vector input's fields take, ignored at or below VectorMin.

name: VectorMin
documentation: VectorMin is the lowest value a vector input's fields take, ignored at or above VectorMax.

name: VectorSpeed
documentation: VectorSpeed is how much a vector input field changes per pixel the pointer drags sideways.

name: VectorValue
documentation: VectorValue is the vector a vector input shows and edits. Dragging or typing in a field changes it and fires `Activated`.

name: Velocity
documentation: Velocity is the linear velocity of the body in units per second, in world space. On a member of a welded assembly, Velocity is the velocity of that member's point.
notes: On an anchored part, Velocity moves the surface while the part stays put, as on a conveyor belt. Parts and characters on it ride along. An `AngVelocity` on the anchored part spins the surface like a turntable.
On an anchored part with a water material, Velocity is the current that floating parts and swimming characters drift with.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a jump pad part.
local launch = Vector3.new(0, 60, 0)

self.Touched:Connect(function(hit: Instance)
    local character = hit.Character
    if character then
        character.Velocity = launch
    end
end)

name: ViewSource
documentation: ViewSource is the camera whose view game.World.Screen shows, or nil for none.

name: ViewportFrame
documentation: create a frame that shows a camera's image

name: Visible
documentation: Visible is whether a UI element and everything under it show and take the pointer. On any other instance, Visible is the opposite of RenderDisabled.

name: Volume
documentation: Volume is how loud the sound plays. 0 is silent and 1 is the recorded loudness.

name: WaitForChild
type: (self: Instance, name: string, timeout: number?) -> Instance?
documentation: WaitForChild returns the direct child with a matching `Name`, and waits for it when it is not there yet. A client script needs it for anything the server creates, which arrives after the script starts.
notes: When the child is missing, the script pauses and checks again once per tick.
A wait without a timeout prints `Infinite yield possible on '<parent>:WaitForChild("<name>")'` once after 5 seconds, then keeps waiting.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
task.delay(1, function()
    local blade = Instance.new("Part")
    blade.Name = "Blade"
    blade.Parent = self
end)

local blade = self:WaitForChild("Blade", 5) -- pauses about 1 second
print(blade ~= nil) -- prints true

name: WaitTime
documentation: WaitTime is how many seconds the timer counts down. Set it before you attach `TimerRunning`; a change takes effect on the next countdown.

name: WalkSpeed
documentation: WalkSpeed is how fast the character walks, in units/s.

name: Wedge
documentation: create a wedge part

name: WheelRadius
documentation: WheelRadius is the radius of a tire in units for the tire model. The tire rolls without slip when its spin times WheelRadius equals its ground speed.

name: WireCurvature
documentation: WireCurvature is how much graph wires curve, from 0 (straight) to 1.

name: ZIndex
documentation: ZIndex is which of overlapping siblings draws on top: higher numbers draw in front, and equal numbers draw in tree order, later siblings on top.

name: ZeroLiftDrag
documentation: ZeroLiftDrag is a wing's drag coefficient when it makes no lift.

name: attr
documentation: attr is the map of named values that scripts store on this instance: numbers, booleans, strings of at most 64 bytes, or vectors. Assigning nil removes an attribute. Iterate it with `for ... in part.attr`; `pairs()` fails on it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.attr.Coins = 10
self.attr.Coins += 5
self.attr.Owner = "Igor"
for name, value in self.attr do
    print(name, value)
end
self.attr.Owner = nil -- removes it

name: new
documentation: `Instance.new` creates an object of kind `name` at the top of the place and sets its `Name` to `name`. Set `Parent` after the other properties; `Instance.new` takes no parent argument.
notes: `Part` is a gray 4 by 2 by 2 box with a physics body. `Sphere`, `Cylinder`, `Cone`, `Wedge`, `SpawnLocation`, `PointLight`, `SpotLight`, `Decal`, `ParticleEmitter`, `Team`, `Tool`, `Model`, `Sound`, `BillboardGui`, `ScreenGui`, `SurfaceGui`, `Frame`, `ScrollingFrame`, `TextLabel`, `TextButton`, `TextBox`, `ImageLabel`, `ImageButton`, `Slider`, `Toggle`, `InputContext`, `InputAction`, `InputBinding` and `LeaderboardColumn` make that object; `WedgePart` makes a `Wedge`.
Any other name makes an empty instance that shows nothing until you add a shape with AddComponent.
code_sample:
-- Server script: build a staircase of five steps.
for height = 1, 5 do
    local step = Instance.new("Part")
    step.Name = "Step"
    step.Anchored = true
    step.Position = Vector3.new(0, height, height * 2)
    step.Parent = game.World
end

name: Clips
documentation: Clips is an array of 1 to 4 audio asset ID strings.

name: Gain
documentation: Gain is the volume multiplier, at least 0 (default 1).

name: PitchSpread
documentation: PitchSpread is the random playback speed variation around 1, from 0 to 0.9 (default 0).

name: Intensity
documentation: Intensity is the brightness multiplier (default 1).

name: Texture
documentation: Texture is the emission map asset ID, or `nil`.

name: Tint
documentation: Tint is the `{r, g, b}` color multiplier from 0 to 1 (default `{r = 1, g = 1, b = 1}`).

name: Id
documentation: Id is the material asset ID string.

name: Model
documentation: Model is `"UV"`, `"Triplanar"`, or `"Stud"` (`game.Enum.SurfaceModel`).

name: Name
documentation: Name is the material name, 1 to 31 bytes.

name: Pipeline
documentation: Pipeline is `"Opaque"`, `"Cutout"`, `"Transparent"`, `"Water"`, or `"Decal"` (`game.Enum.MaterialPipeline`).

name: Density
documentation: Density is mass per unit volume, greater than 0 (default 1). On an anchored `"Water"` part, `Density` sets buoyancy.

name: Friction
documentation: Friction is sliding resistance, at least 0 (default 0.5).

name: Restitution
documentation: Restitution is bounciness, at least 0 (default 0).

name: Blend
documentation: Blend is `"Alpha"` or `"Additive"` (`game.Enum.MaterialBlend`, default `"Alpha"`). Requires `Shader`; see transparent materials.

name: Emission
documentation: Emission is the `MaterialEmission` table, or `nil`.

name: Faces
documentation: Faces is `"Front"`, `"Back"`, or `"Both"` (`game.Enum.MaterialFaces`, default `"Front"`). Requires `Shader`; see faces.

name: Footsteps
documentation: Footsteps is the `MaterialAudio` table for footsteps, or `nil`.

name: Id
documentation: Id is the material asset ID string.

name: Impacts
documentation: Impacts is the `MaterialAudio` table for impacts, or `nil`.

name: Model
documentation: Model is `"UV"`, `"Triplanar"`, or `"Stud"` (`game.Enum.SurfaceModel`), defaulting to `"UV"` when `Shader` is set.

name: Name
documentation: Name is 1 to 31 bytes, defaulting to the next unused `"Material<n>"`.

name: Params
documentation: Params maps up to 16 shader field names to numbers, vectors, booleans, or texture asset IDs, or is `nil`. Update values at runtime with `Materials.SetParam`.

name: Physics
documentation: Physics is the `MaterialPhysics` table, or `nil`.

name: Pipeline
documentation: Pipeline is `"Opaque"`, `"Cutout"`, `"Transparent"`, `"Water"`, or `"Decal"` (`game.Enum.MaterialPipeline`). `"Water"` and `"Decal"` require `Model` `"UV"`; when `Shader` is set, `Pipeline` defaults to `"Opaque"` and allows `"Opaque"` or `"Transparent"`.

name: Shader
documentation: Shader is a shader file name in `shaders/` without `.slang`, or `nil`; see writing a material shader.

name: Studs
documentation: Studs is the `MaterialStuds` table when `Model` is `"Stud"`, or `nil`.

name: Surface
documentation: Surface is the `MaterialSurface` table, optional when `Shader` is set.

name: Water
documentation: Water is the `MaterialWater` table when `Pipeline` is `"Water"`, or `nil`.

name: ColorBottom
documentation: ColorBottom is the bottom-face color and alpha-occlusion texture asset ID, or `nil`.

name: ColorTop
documentation: ColorTop is the top-face color and alpha-occlusion texture asset ID, or `nil`.

name: NormalBottom
documentation: NormalBottom is the bottom-face normal map asset ID, or `nil`, with the same channels as `NormalTop`.

name: NormalTop
documentation: NormalTop is the top-face normal map asset ID, or `nil`. Red and green point opposite to `MaterialSurface` `Normal`.

name: StudsPerTile
documentation: StudsPerTile is units per texture repeat, greater than 0 (default 1).

name: AlphaCutoff
documentation: AlphaCutoff is the opacity cutoff from 0 to 1 for `"Cutout"` and `"Decal"` surfaces (default 0.5).

name: BaseColor
documentation: BaseColor is the color and alpha texture asset ID, or `nil`. Required for `"Cutout"` and `"Decal"` pipelines.

name: MetallicMult
documentation: MetallicMult scales metalness from 0 (non-metal) to 1 (metal), default 1.

name: Neon
documentation: Neon is `true` when surface color emits light (default `false`).

name: Normal
documentation: Normal is the normal map asset ID (green points up), or `nil`.

name: NormalStrength
documentation: NormalStrength is the normal map strength multiplier (default 1).

name: Orm
documentation: Orm is the occlusion (red), roughness (green), and metallic (blue) texture asset ID, or `nil`.

name: RoughnessMult
documentation: RoughnessMult scales roughness from 0 (glossy) to 1 (matte), default 1.

name: TileSize
documentation: TileSize is the texture repeat size in units, greater than 0 (default 1).

name: Tint
type: {r: number, g: number, b: number, a: number}?
documentation: Tint is the `{r, g, b, a}` color and opacity multiplier from 0 to 1 (default `{r = 1, g = 1, b = 1, a = 1}`).

name: TintVertex
documentation: TintVertex, when `true`, tints textured meshes by the part's `Color` (default `false`).

name: Absorption
documentation: Absorption is the `{r, g, b}` light absorption rate per unit of depth (default `{r = 0, g = 0, b = 0}`).

name: DepthScale
documentation: DepthScale scales optical water depth (default 1).

name: FlowMap
documentation: FlowMap is the flow normal map asset ID, or `nil`.

name: FlowScale
documentation: FlowScale sets the UV repeat scale for `FlowMap` and `Foam` (default 1).

name: FlowSpeed
documentation: FlowSpeed sets the animation speed for `FlowMap` and `Foam` (default 0).

name: Foam
documentation: Foam is the foam texture asset ID, or `nil`.

name: FoamDepth
documentation: FoamDepth sets the shoreline depth in units where foam appears (default 0).

name: FoamScale
documentation: FoamScale scales wave-crest foam intensity (default 1).

name: Refraction
documentation: Refraction sets underwater distortion strength (default 0).

name: WaveAmplitude
documentation: WaveAmplitude scales wave height (default 0). When `WaveAmplitude` is nonzero, box water parts displace their top face and cast caustics.

name: WaveScale
documentation: WaveScale scales spatial wave frequency (default 1).

name: WaveSpeed
documentation: WaveSpeed scales wave speed (default 0).

name: jump
documentation: jump is true when a jump is requested.

name: shiftLock
documentation: shiftLock is true when shift lock aligns facing with the camera.

name: targetYaw
documentation: targetYaw is the target yaw around world `+Y` in radians (`0` faces `-Z`, positive is counter-clockwise from above).

name: x
documentation: x is the target world-X velocity in units/s.

name: z
documentation: z is the target world-Z velocity in units/s.

name: Max
documentation: Max is the upper bound, at least `Min`.

name: Min
documentation: Min is the lower bound.

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns `true` when `Min` and `Max` match.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns `"NumberRange(min, max)"`.

name: new
documentation: `NumberRange.new` creates a range from `min` to `max`, or of the one number `min` when `max` is left out.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: each spark lives between 0.5 and 1.5 seconds.
local sparks = Instance.new("Sparks")
sparks:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate")
sparks.ParticleEmitter.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(0.5, 1.5)
sparks.Parent = self

name: Keypoints
documentation: Keypoints returns a new array of the 2 to 8 `NumberSequenceKeypoint` values in time order.

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns `true` when both sequences have the same keypoints.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns `"NumberSequence(t1 v1 e1, t2 v2 e2, ...)"`.

name: new
documentation: `NumberSequence.new` creates a sequence of one number, a ramp from `n0` to `n1`, or a sequence from a list of `NumberSequenceKeypoint` values. A list must start at time 0, end at time 1 and be in time order.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: particles that shrink to nothing.
local puffs = Instance.new("Puffs")
puffs:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleSizeCurve")
puffs.ParticleSizeCurve.Curve = NumberSequence.new(1, 0)
puffs.Parent = self

name: Envelope
documentation: Envelope is the non-negative random spread around `Value` (`0` for none).

name: Time
documentation: Time is the position on the curve (`0` at the start, `1` at the end).

name: Value
documentation: Value is the number at `Time`.

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns `true` when `Time`, `Value`, and `Envelope` match.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns `"NumberSequenceKeypoint(time, value, envelope)"`.

name: new
type: (time: number, value: number, envelope: number?) -> NumberSequenceKeypoint
documentation: `NumberSequenceKeypoint.new` creates a keypoint with `value` at `time`, from 0 to 1. The optional `envelope` lets values read from the curve vary at random by up to that much above or below `value`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: embers whose peak opacity varies from 0.5 to 1.
local embers = Instance.new("Embers")
embers:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleColorRamp")
embers.ParticleColorRamp.Opacity = NumberSequence.new({
    NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, 0.5),
    NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0.5, 0.75, 0.25),
    NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 0),
})
embers.Parent = self

name: Execute
documentation: Execute is called as `Execute(ctx, params)` to apply edits through `ctx.Edit`. Return `true` and an optional Output message to keep the edits, or return `false` (or raise an error) to undo every edit of the run.

name: Icon
documentation: Icon is a button icon path inside the plugin folder, such as `"icons/hollow.svg"`, or `nil`.

name: Id
documentation: Id is the operator identifier, such as `"build.hollow"`, exposed as the Studio command `plugin.build.hollow`.

name: Label
documentation: Label is the button text.

name: Params
documentation: Params lists up to 32 `ParamSpec` entries in order, or is `nil`.

name: Poll
documentation: Poll is called as `Poll(ctx)` to test whether the operator can run, or is `nil` when it always can. Return `true` to enable the button, or `false` and an optional tooltip reason to disable it.

name: Prefab
documentation: Prefab is a `.ldv` UI prefab path (relative to the plugin folder) opened before a button run, or `nil` to run at once. When a descendant's `Name` matches a visible parameter, Studio fills it from the last confirmed run or that parameter's `Default`; Studio runs on `"OK"` or `Enter` and closes on `"Cancel"` or `Escape`.

name: Tooltip
documentation: Tooltip is the button hover text, or `nil`.

name: get
type: function get(self, key: number | string, callback: (number?, string?) -> ()): ()
documentation: get loads the score saved under `key`. The callback receives `(score, nil)` when found, `(nil, nil)` when missing, or `(nil, "get failed")` on failure.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local wins = game.CloudStore.open_ordered("total_wins")

wins:get(1001, function(score, err)
    if not err then
        print(score or 0)
    end
end)

name: get_sorted
type: function get_sorted(self, ascending: boolean, limit: number, min_score: number?, max_score: number?, after: {key: string, value: number}?, callback: ({{key: string, value: number}}, string?) -> ()): ()
documentation: get_sorted loads up to `limit` (1 to 100) `{ key, value }` entries sorted by score: lowest first when `ascending` is `true`, highest first when `false`. Optional `min_score`, `max_score`, and `after` arguments before `callback` bound the score range or continue after the last entry of the previous page.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local wins = game.CloudStore.open_ordered("total_wins")

-- Load the top 10 scores.
wins:get_sorted(false, 10, nil, nil, nil, function(entries, err)
    if err then
        warn(err)
        return
    end
    for rank, entry in entries do
        print(rank, entry.key, entry.value)
    end
end)

name: set
type: function set(self, key: number | string, score: number, callback: ((boolean, string?) -> ())?): ()
documentation: set saves an integer `score` under `key`, replacing any earlier score. The optional callback receives `(true, nil)` when saved, or `(false, "set failed")` on failure.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local wins = game.CloudStore.open_ordered("total_wins")

game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player: Instance)
    wins:set(player.UserId, 1, function(ok, err)
        if not ok then
            warn(err)
        end
    end)
end)

name: A
documentation: A is the line start.

name: At
documentation: At is the label anchor.

name: B
documentation: B is the line end.

name: Color
documentation: Color is an RGB `vector` from 0 to 1, or `nil` for white `(1, 1, 1)`.

name: Face
documentation: Face is the `"faceGrid"` side: `"Right"` (default), `"Left"`, `"Top"`, `"Bottom"`, `"Back"`, or `"Front"`.

name: Fill
documentation: Fill draws translucent box faces when `true`, or edges only when `false` or `nil`.

name: Kind
documentation: Kind is `"box"` (`Min`, `Max`, `Fill`), `"faceGrid"` (`Face`, `Step`), `"line"` (`A`, `B`), or `"label"` (`At`, `Text`).

name: Max
documentation: Max is the upper box corner.

name: Min
documentation: Min is the lower box corner.

name: Part
documentation: Part is the instance whose position and rotation set the coordinate frame.

name: Step
documentation: Step is grid spacing in units, or `nil` or 0 for the border only.

name: Text
documentation: Text is the label string.

name: Default
documentation: Default is the fallback number, boolean, string, or `vector` when a call omits the parameter, or `nil`. `"MoveIncrement"` and `"RotateIncrement"` use Studio's snap steps at call time.

name: From
documentation: From is `"Selection"` to fill an omitted `"instance"` or `"instances"` parameter from Studio's selection, or `nil`.

name: Hidden
documentation: Hidden omits the parameter from an operator prefab's prefilled fields when `true`.

name: Label
documentation: Label is the display name, or `nil` to use `Name`.

name: Labels
documentation: Labels lists up to 64 choice strings for an `"enum"` parameter.

name: Name
documentation: Name is the key in `Execute`'s `params` table and in `Name=value` command arguments.

name: Type
documentation: Type is `"number"`, `"integer"`, `"boolean"`, `"string"`, `"enum"`, `"Vector3"`, `"instance"`, or `"instances"`.

name: CollisionFidelity
documentation: CollisionFidelity sets how the operation collides. `"Default"` gives an anchored operation its exact shape and an unanchored one a convex hull per separate piece, so the space between the arms of an unanchored U shape is solid. `"Hull"` uses one convex hull around the whole shape, and `"Box"` the bounding box.

name: Type
documentation: Type is `"Union"`, `"Intersect"` or `"Negate"`. A union adds its parts together, an intersection keeps only the volume every part shares, and a negative part cuts its shape out of the operation it is in. `game.Csg` sets it.

name: UsePartColor
documentation: UsePartColor draws every face in the operation's own color and material instead of those of the part it came from.

name: Operator
documentation: Operator registers an undoable Studio action exposed as `plugin.<Id>`.

name: Ribbon
documentation: Ribbon adds a button group of declared operators and tools to Studio's Plugins tab.

name: Tool
documentation: Tool registers an interactive 3D viewport tool whose confirmed gesture runs a declared operator. `"Escape"` is always sent to `Modal` even when `Keys` omits it.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.raise",
    Label = "Raise",
    Params = { { Name = "Part", Type = "instance", Hidden = true } },
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext, params)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        local part = params.Part :: Instance
        edit:Set(part, "Position", part.Position + Vector3.new(0, 1, 0))
        return true
    end,
})

plugin:Tool({
    Id = "build.pick",
    Label = "Pick",
    Operator = "build.raise",
    Modal = function(ctx: PluginContext, event)
        if event.Kind == "key" and event.Key == "Escape" then
            return "exit"
        end
        local hit = event.Hit
        if event.Kind == "press" and event.Button == 1 and hit then
            return "confirm", nil, nil, { Part = hit.Part }
        end
        return "running", nil, "Click a part to raise it"
    end,
})

name: Camera
type: {Position: vector, Pivot: vector, Yaw: number, Pitch: number, Distance: number, Focused: boolean}
documentation: Camera is Studio's edit camera table: `Position` and `Pivot` in world units, `Yaw` and `Pitch` in radians, `Distance` in units, and `Focused` (`true` when right-drag orbits `Pivot`).

name: Edit
documentation: Edit is the `PluginEdit` handle inside `Execute`, or `nil` in `Poll` and `Modal`. Changing the place directly outside `ctx.Edit` raises an error.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.paint_red",
    Label = "Paint Red",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        for _, part in ctx.Selection do
            edit:Set(part, "Color", Color3.new(1, 0, 0))
        end
        return true
    end,
})

name: MoveIncrement
documentation: MoveIncrement is Studio's move snap step in units.

name: RotateIncrement
documentation: RotateIncrement is Studio's rotate snap step in degrees.

name: Seats
type: {{Id: number, Name: string, Kind: "person" | "agent", Color: vector, You: boolean, Selection: {Instance}}}

name: Selection
documentation: Selection is the array of instances selected in Studio at call time.

name: Snap
type: (value: number, increment: number, from: number, to: number) -> number
documentation: Snap takes `(value, increment, from, to)` and clamps `value` between `from` and `to`, rounding to steps of `increment` from `math.min(from, to)` when `increment > 0`.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.snap_height",
    Label = "Snap Height",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        for _, part in ctx.Selection do
            local y = ctx.Snap(part.Position.Y, ctx.MoveIncrement, 0, 100)
            edit:Set(part, "Position", Vector3.new(part.Position.X, y, part.Position.Z))
        end
        return true
    end,
})

name: AddAccessory
type: function AddAccessory(self, character: Instance, assetId: string, sha256: string?): (Instance?, string?)

name: Copy
type: function Copy(self, inst: Instance, props: {[string]: any}?): Instance
documentation: Copy duplicates `inst` under the same parent without children, scripts, decals, attachments, or welds, and returns the copy.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.stack",
    Label = "Stack Copy",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        local part = ctx.Selection[1]
        if part then
            edit:Copy(part, { Position = part.Position + Vector3.new(0, part.Size.Y, 0) })
        end
        return true
    end,
})

name: Create
type: function Create(self, class: string, props: {[string]: any}?, parent: Instance?): Instance
documentation: Create takes `(class, props, parent)`, adds a new instance of `class` under `parent` (or the place root when `nil`), and returns it. In `props`, `Frame` copies the world pose of an instance.

name: Destroy
documentation: Destroy removes `inst` and its descendants from the place.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.delete_selected",
    Label = "Delete Selected",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        for _, inst in ctx.Selection do
            edit:Destroy(inst)
        end
        return true
    end,
})

name: Reshape
type: function Reshape(self, part: Instance, size: vector, position: vector): ()
documentation: Reshape sets `part`'s size and world center while keeping children and welded parts at their world poses.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.slab",
    Label = "Make Slab",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        for _, part in ctx.Selection do
            edit:Reshape(part, Vector3.new(part.Size.X, 1, part.Size.Z), part.Position)
        end
        return true
    end,
})

name: Select
documentation: Select sets Studio's selection (up to 4,096 instances) when `Execute` succeeds.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.create_and_select",
    Label = "New Block",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        local block = edit:Create("Part", { Position = ctx.Camera.Pivot })
        edit:Select({ block })
        return true
    end,
})

name: Set
type: function Set(self, inst: Instance, name: string, value: any): ()
documentation: Set assigns `inst[name] = value`, moving descendants and welded parts on pose changes the same way Studio does.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.anchor",
    Label = "Anchor Selected",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        for _, part in ctx.Selection do
            edit:Set(part, "Anchored", true)
        end
        return true
    end,
})

name: SetCamera
type: function SetCamera(self, position: vector, yaw: number, pitch: number, distance: number?): ()
documentation: SetCamera takes `(position, yaw, pitch, distance)` (with `yaw` and `pitch` in radians) and moves Studio's edit camera when `Execute` succeeds. Passing `distance` focuses an orbit pivot that many units ahead of `position`.

name: SetParent
type: function SetParent(self, inst: Instance, parent: Instance?): ()
documentation: SetParent moves `inst` under `parent` (or the place root when `nil`) while preserving its world transform.
code_sample:
-- Plugin script (plugins/build/init.lua).
plugin:Operator({
    Id = "build.group",
    Label = "Group Selection",
    Execute = function(ctx: PluginContext)
        local edit = ctx.Edit :: PluginEdit
        local folder = edit:Create("Folder", { Name = "Group" })
        for _, inst in ctx.Selection do
            edit:SetParent(inst, folder)
        end
        return true
    end,
})

name: Alt
documentation: Alt is `true` while Alt is held.

name: Button
documentation: Button is `1` for left button (`"press"`, `"release"`, and `"move"` while held), `2` on `"press"` and `"release"` for a stationary right click, or `0` otherwise.

name: Ctrl
documentation: Ctrl is `true` while Ctrl is held.

name: DeltaX
documentation: DeltaX is horizontal cursor motion in pixels since the last press or release.

name: DeltaY
documentation: DeltaY is vertical cursor motion in pixels since the last press or release.

name: Hit
documentation: Hit is the `PluginHit` for the nearest unlocked part within 1,000 units, or `nil`.

name: Key
documentation: Key is `"Escape"`, `"Return"`, `"Backspace"`, `"Tab"`, `"Space"`, `"Delete"`, `"A"` to `"Z"`, or `"0"` to `"9"` on `"key"`, or `nil` otherwise.

name: Kind
documentation: Kind is `"move"`, `"press"`, `"release"`, `"wheel"`, or `"key"`.

name: RayDirection
documentation: RayDirection is the world-space unit ray direction through the cursor.

name: RayOrigin
documentation: RayOrigin is the world-space camera ray origin through the cursor.

name: Shift
documentation: Shift is `true` while Shift is held.

name: WheelSteps
documentation: WheelSteps is the signed wheel delta (`-127` to `127`) on `"wheel"`, or `0` otherwise.

name: Face
documentation: Face is the hit side: `"Right"`, `"Left"`, `"Top"`, `"Bottom"`, `"Back"`, or `"Front"`.

name: LocalNormal
documentation: LocalNormal is the outward face normal in `Part`'s frame.

name: LocalPosition
documentation: LocalPosition is the hit point in `Part`'s frame.

name: Normal
documentation: Normal is the outward face normal in world space.

name: Part
documentation: Part is the hit part.

name: Position
documentation: Position is the hit point in world space.

name: PlayerId
documentation: PlayerId is the buyer's user ID; pass it to `Players.Get` to find the player.

name: Price
documentation: Price is the price paid in Lunes (`0` in Studio Play).

name: ProductId
documentation: ProductId is the bought developer product ID.

name: PurchaseId
documentation: PurchaseId is the unique purchase identifier string.

name: Entity
documentation: Entity is the column of matched `Instance` handles from `1` to `count`.

name: Instance
documentation: Instance is the column of matched `Instance` handles from `1` to `count`, or `nil` where an entity was destroyed after `Refresh`.

name: Refresh
documentation: Refresh compiles the query on first call, snapshots matching entities into its columns, and returns `count`.
notes: Calling `With` or `Without` after the first `Refresh` raises an error.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent(game.World.Pair("Tag", "Hazard"))

local hazards = game.World.Query("Position", game.World.Pair("Tag", "Hazard"))
local count = hazards:Refresh()
print(count, hazards.Instance[1] == self) -- prints 1   true

name: With
type: function With(self, name: string | Pair): Query
documentation: With adds a required component or `Pair` before the first `Refresh` and returns the query (up to 8 terms total).
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent("Timer")

local timed = game.World.Query("Position"):With("Timer")
print(timed:Refresh()) -- prints 1

name: Without
type: function Without(self, name: string | Pair): Query
documentation: Without excludes entities with a component or `Pair` before the first `Refresh` and returns the query.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Anchored = false

local moving = game.World.Query("Position"):Without("Anchored")
print(moving:Refresh() >= 1) -- prints true

name: count
documentation: count is the number of entities matched by the last `Refresh`, or 0 before the first refresh.

name: AtTick
documentation: AtTick rewinds character hitboxes on a server `Raycast` to a past `ServerTick` (up to 64 ticks back). Other colliders and other query functions ignore `AtTick`.

name: CollisionGroup
documentation: CollisionGroup names the registered collision group for the query, which hits only colliders whose group collides with that group, or `nil` to test every group.

name: ExcludeInstances
documentation: ExcludeInstances lists up to 128 instances (and their descendants) to skip.

name: IncludeInstances
documentation: IncludeInstances restricts the query to up to 128 instances and their descendants; `{}` hits nothing.

name: Distance
documentation: Distance is the distance in units from the ray origin to `Position`.

name: Entity
documentation: Entity is the hit `Instance`, or `nil` if destroyed.

name: Instance
documentation: Instance is the hit `Instance`, or `nil` if destroyed.

name: Normal
documentation: Normal is the outward unit normal at `Position`.

name: Position
documentation: Position is the hit point in world units.

name: Height
documentation: Height is `Max.y - Min.y`.

name: Max
documentation: Max is the `(maxX, maxY, 0)` vector.

name: Min
documentation: Min is the `(minX, minY, 0)` vector.

name: Width
documentation: Width is `Max.x - Min.x`.

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns true when all four coordinates match.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns `"Rect(minX, minY, maxX, maxY)"`.

name: new
type: (minX: number?, minY: number?, maxX: number?, maxY: number?) -> Rect
documentation: `Rect.new` creates a rectangle from `minX`, `minY`, `maxX` and `maxY`.
code_sample:
-- Client script: a panel with rounded top corners only.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local panel = Instance.new("Frame")
panel.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(300, 200)
panel.CornerRadii = Rect.new(16, 16, 0, 0)
panel.Parent = hud

name: Group
documentation: Group is the group title on the Plugins tab.

name: Items
documentation: Items lists up to 64 operator and tool ids in button order.

name: avg
documentation: avg is the smoothed per-frame run time in milliseconds across `Update`, `PhysicsUpdate`, and `World.System`.

name: calls
documentation: calls is the number of `Update`, `PhysicsUpdate`, and `World.System` runs so far in the current frame.

name: entity
documentation: entity is the numeric ID of the script's instance (use `path` to identify the script).

name: path
documentation: path is the project script path without a leading `@`.

name: Entity
documentation: Entity is the hit `Instance`.

name: Fraction
documentation: Fraction is the sweep progress from `from` (`0`) to `to` (`1`) at contact.

name: Instance
documentation: Instance is the hit `Instance`.

name: Normal
documentation: Normal is the outward unit normal at `Point`, or `(0, 0, 0)` when shapes start deeply overlapping.

name: Point
documentation: Point is the world-space contact point on the hit shape in units.

name: Connect
documentation: Connect runs a function every time the signal emits, until it is disconnected or the instance is destroyed. Each call runs on its own thread, so it may call `task.wait`, and an error in one function does not stop the others.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local scored = self:GetSignal("Scored")

scored:Connect(function(points: number, by: string)
    print(by .. " scored " .. points)
end)

scored:Emit(3, "Ana") -- prints Ana scored 3

name: Disconnect
documentation: Disconnect stops a function passed to `Connect` from running. Pass the same function value.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local alarm = self:GetSignal("Alarm")

local function onAlarm()
    print("alarm")
    alarm:Disconnect(onAlarm)
end

alarm:Connect(onAlarm)
alarm:Connect(function()
    print("still on")
end)

alarm:Emit() -- prints alarm, then still on
alarm:Emit() -- prints still on

name: Emit
documentation: Emit runs every connected function with the given values before it returns. Values cannot be or contain functions or threads, and a table may have at most 16 levels and fewer than 4096 entries.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local wave = self:GetSignal("WaveStarted")

wave:Connect(function(number: number)
    print("wave " .. number)
end)

wave:Emit(1) -- prints wave 1

name: Once
documentation: Once runs a function the next time the signal emits, then disconnects it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local opened = self:GetSignal("Opened")

opened:Once(function()
    print("first time")
end)
opened:Connect(function()
    print("opened")
end)

opened:Emit() -- prints first time, then opened
opened:Emit() -- prints opened

name: Wait
documentation: Wait pauses the script until the signal next emits, then returns the emitted values. It cannot pause `Update` or another callback that must return at once; call it from the top of the script or from `task.spawn`. If the instance is destroyed first, Wait never returns.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local ready = self:GetSignal("Ready")

task.delay(1, function()
    ready:Emit("go")
end)

print(ready:Wait()) -- prints go after one second

name: Connected
documentation: Connected is `true` while subscribed, and `false` after `Disconnect`, after a `Once` callback runs, when the script stops, or when the signal's `Instance` is destroyed or `Tween` ends.

name: Disconnect
documentation: Disconnect unsubscribes the callback and sets `Connected` to `false`.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local ping = self:GetSignal("Ping")
local conn: SignalConnection
conn = ping:Connect(function()
    conn:Disconnect()
    print("once") -- prints once
end)
ping:Emit()
task.wait()
print(conn.Connected) -- prints false

name: get
type: function get(self, key: number | string): {[string]: any}?
documentation: get reads `key` from memory and returns a copy of its stored table, or `nil` when `key` has no entry.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local saves = game.Store.open("player_gold")
saves:put(1001, { gold = 50 })

local data = saves:get(1001)
print(data and data.gold) -- prints 50

name: put
type: function put(self, key: number | string, value: {[string]: any}): ()
documentation: put writes table `value` under `key` and flushes it to disk before returning. Tables hold numbers, booleans, strings, `Vector3`s, and nested tables (up to 8 levels and 65,536 encoded bytes).
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local saves = game.Store.open("player_gold")
saves:put(1001, { gold = 120, home = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0) })
local saved = saves:get(1001)
print(saved and saved.gold) -- prints 120

name: Active
documentation: Active is `true` while the player has an active subscription to the product.

name: CancelAtPeriodEnd
documentation: CancelAtPeriodEnd is `true` when `Active` is `true` and renewal was canceled.

name: CurrentPeriodEnd
documentation: CurrentPeriodEnd is the UTC Unix timestamp in seconds when the paid period ends, or `nil` when `Active` is `false`.

name: Anchor
documentation: Anchor is the joint pivot in the parent part's frame, in units.

name: Friction
documentation: Friction is the optional opposing torque in Newton-meters, or `nil` for none.

name: NormalCone
documentation: NormalCone is a swing half-angle limit in degrees (`0` to `180`); the active cone uses `math.max(PlaneCone, NormalCone)`.

name: PlaneAxis
documentation: PlaneAxis is the swing reference axis perpendicular to `TwistAxis` (`(0, 0, 0)` defaults to `(1, 0, 0)`).

name: PlaneCone
documentation: PlaneCone is a swing half-angle limit in degrees (`0` to `180`); the active cone uses `math.max(PlaneCone, NormalCone)`.

name: RestAxis
documentation: RestAxis is the optional child resting direction in the parent part's frame, or `nil` to match `TwistAxis`.

name: TwistAxis
documentation: TwistAxis is the twist axis in the parent part's frame (`(0, 0, 0)` defaults to `(0, 1, 0)`).

name: TwistMax
documentation: TwistMax is the upper twist limit around `TwistAxis` in degrees (`-180` to `180`).

name: TwistMin
documentation: TwistMin is the lower twist limit around `TwistAxis` in degrees (`-180` to `180`).

name: Anchor
documentation: Anchor is the joint pivot in the parent part's frame, in units.

name: Friction
documentation: Friction is the opposing torque in Newton-meters.

name: NormalCone
documentation: NormalCone is a swing half-angle limit in degrees (`0` to `180`); the active cone uses `math.max(PlaneCone, NormalCone)`.

name: PlaneAxis
documentation: PlaneAxis is the swing reference axis in the parent part's frame.

name: PlaneCone
documentation: PlaneCone is a swing half-angle limit in degrees (`0` to `180`); the active cone uses `math.max(PlaneCone, NormalCone)`.

name: RestAxis
documentation: RestAxis is the child's resting direction in the parent part's frame, or `(0, 0, 0)` when aligned with `TwistAxis`.

name: TwistAxis
documentation: TwistAxis is the twist axis in the parent part's frame.

name: TwistMax
documentation: TwistMax is the upper twist limit around `TwistAxis` in degrees (`-180` to `180`).

name: TwistMin
documentation: TwistMin is the lower twist limit around `TwistAxis` in degrees (`-180` to `180`).

name: Icon
documentation: Icon is a button icon path inside the plugin folder, or `nil`.

name: Id
documentation: Id is the tool identifier referenced in `RibbonSpec.Items`.

name: Keys
documentation: Keys lists up to 64 key names (`"Escape"`, `"Return"`, `"Backspace"`, `"Tab"`, `"Space"`, `"Delete"`, `"A"` to `"Z"`, `"0"` to `"9"`) sent to `Modal` instead of viewport shortcuts; `"Escape"` is always included.

name: Label
documentation: Label is the button text.

name: Modal
documentation: Modal handles `PluginEvent`s as `Modal(ctx, event)` while the tool is active. When the tool activates, Studio calls `Modal` once with `"Escape"` so the tool can reset its Lua state and ignores that call's return values.

name: Operator
documentation: Operator is the `Id` of the declared operator run on `"confirm"`.

name: Tooltip
documentation: Tooltip is the button hover text, or `nil`.

name: a
documentation: a is the first instance.

name: b
documentation: b is the second instance.

name: began
documentation: began is `true` on contact start and `false` on separation.

name: Finished
documentation: Finished fires once with no arguments when the tween reaches its final value, is overridden on the same property, or ends because its `Instance` was destroyed or lost the tweened component. `Kill` does not fire `Finished`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Transparency", 1, 0.2)
tween.Finished:Connect(function()
    print("faded") -- prints faded
    self:Destroy()
end)

name: IsRunning
documentation: IsRunning returns `true` while advancing or waiting out a delay, and `false` when paused or ended.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Transparency", 1, 0.2)
print(tween:IsRunning()) -- prints true

name: IsValid
documentation: IsValid returns `true` until the tween reaches its final value, is overridden, is killed, or ends because its `Instance` was destroyed or lost the tweened component.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Transparency", 1, 0.2)
print(tween:IsValid()) -- prints true
task.wait(0.3)
print(tween:IsValid()) -- prints false

name: Kill
documentation: Kill stops the tween at its current value without firing `Finished`, leaving threads in `Finished:Wait()` suspended.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Transparency", 1, 1)
task.wait(0.2)
tween:Kill()
print(tween:IsValid()) -- prints false

name: Pause
documentation: Pause freezes the tween at its current elapsed time and value.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Transparency", 1, 0.4)
tween:Pause()
print(tween:IsRunning()) -- prints false

name: Play
documentation: Play resumes a paused tween from where it stopped.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Transparency", 1, 0.4)
tween:Pause()
tween:Play()
print(tween:IsRunning()) -- prints true

name: SetBehavior
documentation: SetBehavior sets `"Normal"` (default) or `"AllowDiscrete"` (`game.Enum.TweenBehavior`) and returns the tween. `"AllowDiscrete"` keeps a UI element with `Visible = false` drawn (without receiving input) until the tween ends or pauses.
code_sample:
-- Client script in a part.
local frame = Instance.new("Frame")
frame.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(200, 80)
frame.Visible = false

local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(frame, "Position", UDim2.fromScale(1, 0), 0.2)
    :SetBehavior("AllowDiscrete")
print(tween:IsRunning()) -- prints true

name: SetDelay
documentation: SetDelay waits `seconds` before reading the start value and advancing, and returns the tween. Once the tween starts, `SetDelay` does nothing.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Transparency", 1, 0.2):SetDelay(0.2)
task.wait(0.1)
print(self.Transparency) -- prints 0
task.wait(0.4)
print(self.Transparency) -- prints 1

name: SetEase
documentation: SetEase sets which end eases (`"In"`, `"Out"`, `"InOut"`, or `"OutIn"` from `game.Enum.TweenEase`, default `"InOut"`) and returns the tween.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Anchored = true
self.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)

game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Position", Vector3.new(0, 2, 0), 0.5)
    :SetTrans("Bounce")
    :SetEase("Out")
task.wait(0.6)
print(math.round(self.Position.Y)) -- prints 2

name: SetTrans
documentation: SetTrans sets the curve (`game.Enum.TweenTransition` or a name such as `"Sine"`, `"Quad"`, `"Cubic"`, `"Bounce"`, or `"Spring"`, default `"Linear"`) and returns the tween.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Anchored = true
self.Position = Vector3.new(0, 2, 0)

game.Tween.TweenProperty(self, "Position", Vector3.new(0, 12, 0), 0.5)
    :SetTrans("Sine")
task.wait(0.6)
print(math.round(self.Position.Y)) -- prints 12

name: Offset
documentation: Offset is the pixel offset added after `Scale`.

name: Scale
documentation: Scale is the fraction of the parent size on this axis (`1` is 100%).

name: __add
documentation: __add adds two `UDim` values component-wise.

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns `true` when `Scale` and `Offset` match.

name: __sub
documentation: __sub subtracts `other` from `self` component-wise.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns `"UDim(scale, offset)"`.

name: __unm
documentation: __unm negates `Scale` and `Offset`.

name: new
documentation: `UDim.new` creates an axis from a scale and a pixel offset. Scripts usually build both axes at once with `UDim2.new` and use `UDim` to compare one axis.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local bar = Instance.new("Frame")
bar.UIRect.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 0, 48)
bar.Parent = hud
print(bar.UIRect.Size.X == UDim.new(1, 0)) -- prints true

name: Lerp
type: (self: UDim2, goal: UDim2, alpha: number) -> UDim2
documentation: Lerp linearly interpolates from `self` (`alpha = 0`) to `goal` (`alpha = 1`).
code_sample:
-- Client script in a part.
local closed = UDim2.fromScale(1, 0)
local open = UDim2.new(1, -240, 0, 0)
print(closed:Lerp(open, 0.5).X.Offset) -- prints -120

name: X
documentation: X is the horizontal `UDim` axis.

name: Y
documentation: Y is the vertical `UDim` axis.

name: __add
documentation: __add adds two coordinates component-wise.
code_sample:
-- Client script in a part.
local pos = UDim2.fromOffset(10, 20) + UDim2.fromOffset(5, -4)
print(pos) -- prints UDim2(0, 15, 0, 16)

name: __eq
documentation: __eq returns `true` when all four numbers match.

name: __sub
documentation: __sub subtracts `other` from `self` component-wise.

name: __tostring
documentation: __tostring returns `"UDim2(scaleX, offsetX, scaleY, offsetY)"`.

name: __unm
documentation: __unm negates both scales and both offsets.

name: fromOffset
documentation: `UDim2.fromOffset` creates a `UDim2` from pixel offsets alone.
code_sample:
-- Client script: a 96 by 96 pixel frame 20 pixels from the top left.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local portrait = Instance.new("Frame")
portrait.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20, 20)
portrait.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(96, 96)
portrait.Parent = hud

name: fromScale
documentation: `UDim2.fromScale` creates a `UDim2` from scales alone.
code_sample:
-- Client script: a frame that covers the right half of the screen.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local pane = Instance.new("Frame")
pane.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0)
pane.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 1)
pane.Parent = hud

name: new
type: (scaleX: number?, offsetX: number?, scaleY: number?, offsetY: number?) -> UDim2
documentation: `UDim2.new` creates a `UDim2` from `scaleX`, `offsetX`, `scaleY` and `offsetY`.
code_sample:
-- Client script: a sidebar 240 pixels wide and as tall as the screen.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local sidebar = Instance.new("Frame")
sidebar.UIRect.Position = UDim2.new(0, 0, 0, 0)
sidebar.UIRect.Size = UDim2.new(0, 240, 1, 0)
sidebar.Parent = hud

name: new
documentation: `Vector2.new` creates a 2D vector from `x` and `y`.
code_sample:
-- Client script: a label centered on the screen.
local hud = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
hud.Parent = game.Overlay

local label = Instance.new("TextLabel")
label.Text = "Ready?"
label.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 0.5)
label.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromScale(0.5, 0.5)
label.Parent = hud

name: new
type: (x: number?, y: number?, z: number?) -> vector
documentation: `Vector3.new` creates a vector from `x`, `y` and `z`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)

name: one
documentation: `Vector3.one` is the vector with every component 1.

name: xAxis
documentation: `Vector3.xAxis` is the unit vector along +X.

name: yAxis
documentation: `Vector3.yAxis` is the unit vector along +Y, which points up.

name: zAxis
documentation: `Vector3.zAxis` is the unit vector along +Z.

name: zero
documentation: `Vector3.zero` is the vector with every component 0.

name: Camera
documentation: Camera is the Camera the root Screen views through. Only the client makes it, so it is nil in a server script. A part parented below the Camera keeps its `LocalPosition` on screen, as a viewmodel needs.
code_sample:
-- Client script: zoom in and attach a viewmodel.
local cam = game.World.Camera
if cam then
    cam.CameraLens.fovY = math.rad(30)
    local vm = Instance.new("Part")
    vm.Anchored = true
    vm.Collider = "None"
    vm.Parent = cam
    vm.LocalPosition = Vector3.new(1, -1, -3)
end

name: DumpAttributes
documentation: DumpAttributes prints every attribute name with its id to the engine log. With an entity, it also prints that entity's attributes with their values.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.attr.Locked = true
game.World:DumpAttributes(self)

name: Each
type: ((component: string | Pair) -> () -> Instance?) & ((self: World, component: string | Pair) -> () -> Instance?)
documentation: Each visits every scene entity that has a component or relationship pair. Every loop over the result takes a fresh snapshot, so a script can keep the result and loop it again later.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
for part in game.World:Each("Anchored") do
    part.Transparency = 0.5
end

name: FindFirstChild
type: ((name: string, recursive: boolean?) -> Instance?) & ((self: World, name: string, recursive: boolean?) -> Instance?)
documentation: FindFirstChild returns the first entity at the top of the place with the given name, or nil. With `recursive` true it also searches every level below.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local part = Instance.new("Part")
part.Name = "FinishLine"
part.Parent = game.World
print(game.World:FindFirstChild("FinishLine") == part) -- prints true

name: GetChildren
documentation: GetChildren returns every entity at the top of the place.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
for _, entity in game.World:GetChildren() do
    print(entity.Name)
end

name: GetComponentAddedSignal
type: ((component: string | Pair) -> Signal<(entity: Instance) -> ()>) & ((self: World, component: string | Pair) -> Signal<(entity: Instance) -> ()>)
documentation: GetComponentAddedSignal returns a signal that fires with each entity that gains the component. It does not fire for entities that already have it, so pair it with `World.Each`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
game.World:GetComponentAddedSignal("Admin"):Connect(function(entity: Instance)
    print("admin", entity.Name)
end)
self:AddComponent("Admin")

name: GetComponentRemovedSignal
type: ((component: string | Pair) -> Signal<(entity: Instance) -> ()>) & ((self: World, component: string | Pair) -> Signal<(entity: Instance) -> ()>)
documentation: GetComponentRemovedSignal returns a signal that fires with each entity that loses the component or is destroyed while it has it. A destroyed entity still works as a table key, so a script can clean up its own data.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local admins: { [Instance]: boolean } = {}
game.World:GetComponentAddedSignal("Admin"):Connect(function(entity: Instance)
    admins[entity] = true
end)
game.World:GetComponentRemovedSignal("Admin"):Connect(function(entity: Instance)
    admins[entity] = nil
    print("admin removed")
end)
self:AddComponent("Admin")
task.wait()
self:RemoveComponent("Admin")

name: GetDescendants
documentation: GetDescendants returns every entity in the place, the top level first.
notes: `GetDescendants` builds the whole array on each call, so call it while the script loads, not every tick.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local coins = 0
for _, entity in game.World:GetDescendants() do
    if entity.Name == "Coin" then
        coins += 1
    end
end
print(coins)

name: HasComponent
type: ((component: string | Pair) -> boolean) & ((self: World, component: string | Pair) -> boolean)
documentation: HasComponent returns false, because the World has no components.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
print(game.World:HasComponent("Anchored")) -- prints false

name: IsAlive
documentation: IsAlive returns true, because the World lasts as long as the place.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
print(game.World:IsAlive()) -- prints true

name: IsDescendantOf
type: ((ancestor: Instance | World) -> boolean) & ((self: World, ancestor: Instance | World) -> boolean)
documentation: IsDescendantOf returns false, because nothing is above the World.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
print(self:IsDescendantOf(game.World)) -- prints true
print(game.World:IsDescendantOf(self)) -- prints false

name: Name
documentation: Name is the name of the World, always `World`.

name: Pair
type: ((relation: EnumPairRelation, target: Instance | World | string) -> Pair) & ((self: World, relation: EnumPairRelation, target: Instance | World | string) -> Pair)
documentation: Pair makes a relationship pair for `World.Query`, `World.Each`, `World.Spawn`, `Instance:AddComponent` and `Instance:HasComponent`. The relation is `"ChildOf"`, `"Tag"` or `"WornBy"`, and the target `"*"` matches any target.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent(game.World:Pair("Tag", "Projectile"))
print(self:HasComponent(game.World:Pair("Tag", "Projectile"))) -- prints true

name: Parent
documentation: Parent is always nil, because the World is the top of the place.

name: Query
documentation: Query builds a cached query over scene entities that have every given component and pair. `Refresh` fills its columns; QueryColumn lists them.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self:AddComponent(game.World:Pair("Tag", "Projectile"))
local bullets = game.World:Query("Position", game.World:Pair("Tag", "Projectile"))
bullets:Refresh()
for i = 1, bullets.count do
    bullets.Position[i] += Vector3.new(0, 0, -1)
end

name: Screen
documentation: Screen is the root Screen entity. Only the client makes it, so it is nil in a server script. UI parented below it draws on the player's screen, and its `AbsoluteSize` is the viewport size in UI points.

name: ScreenToRay
type: ((screenPos: vector) -> (vector, vector)) & ((self: World, screenPos: vector) -> (vector, vector))
documentation: ScreenToRay returns the origin and unit direction of the ray from the camera through a screen position in UI points.
code_sample:
-- Client script: print what the mouse clicks.
function Update(_dt: number)
    if game.Input.ButtonPressed(game.Input.Button.Left) then
        local origin, dir = game.World.ScreenToRay(game.Input.MousePosition)
        local hit = game.Physics.Raycast(origin, dir, 200)
        if hit and hit.Instance then
            print("Clicked", hit.Instance.Name)
        end
    end
end

name: Spawn
documentation: Spawn creates an entity named `Instance` at the top of the place with the given components and tag pairs.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local target = game.World:Spawn("Shape", "Anchored", game.World:Pair("Tag", "Target"))
target.Position = Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)
print(target.Name) -- prints Instance

name: System
type: ((name: string, q: Query, fn: (Query, number) -> (), phase: EnumSystemPhase?, after: string?) -> ()) & ((self: World, name: string, q: Query, fn: (Query, number) -> (), phase: EnumSystemPhase?, after: string?) -> ())
documentation: System registers a callback that runs over a query every tick of its phase. The engine refreshes the query before each run. `phase` defaults to `"Default"`, and `after` names a system in the same phase that runs first.
notes: 5 consecutive runs over the instruction or memory budget stop the script's systems.
code_sample:
-- Server script: move every projectile forward.
local bullets = game.World:Query("Position", game.World:Pair("Tag", "Projectile"))
game.World:System("MoveBullets", bullets, function(q: Query, dt: number)
    for i = 1, q.count do
        q.Position[i] += Vector3.new(0, 0, -10 * dt)
    end
end)

name: WaitForChild
type: ((name: string, timeout: number?) -> Instance?) & ((self: World, name: string, timeout: number?) -> Instance?)
documentation: WaitForChild returns the entity at the top of the place with the given name, and waits for it when it is not there yet. It returns nil when `timeout` seconds pass first.
code_sample:
-- Client script: wait up to 10 seconds for the server's Arena.
local arena = game.World:WaitForChild("Arena", 10)
if arena then
    print(arena.Name)
end

name: WorldToScreen
type: ((worldPos: vector) -> (vector, boolean)) & ((self: World, worldPos: vector) -> (vector, boolean))
documentation: WorldToScreen projects a world position onto the screen. It returns `(x, y, depth)`, with `x` and `y` in UI points from the top-left, and whether the point is inside the view.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screenPos, onScreen = game.World.WorldToScreen(Vector3.new(0, 5, 0))
print(onScreen, screenPos.x, screenPos.y)

name: Animation
documentation: Animation has the numbers scripts need to write a character's AnimLayers: the first layer scripts may write and the limb mask flags. Layers 1 through 4 play the built-in clips `idle`, `walk`, `jump`, `tread`, `swim`, `sit`, `climb`, and `hang`; layers FirstScriptLayer through 8 are free for scripts.

name: Bool
documentation: Bool is the field type of a boolean. Any value other than false and nil is sent as true.

name: Buffer
documentation: binary buffer field, 4096 bytes or less

name: Color
documentation: Color is the field type of an RGB color with 8 bits per channel. Each component of a sent vector clamps to 0 to 1.

name: Content
documentation: Content downloads published assets by id, spawns downloaded scenes, and looks up player avatars and headshots. An asset id is a decimal string that names a published scene, mesh, texture, or audio clip; for prefabs saved with the place, use Prefabs.

name: Csg
documentation: Csg combines parts into one solid shape, called a union, and takes unions apart again. A union draws one outer surface and collides as one body.

name: Entity
documentation: Entity is the same token as Instance.

name: EventTable
type: ((name: string, direction: EventDirection?, fields: {{string | EventFieldType}}?, options: {Coalesce: EnumEventCoalesce?, Timing: EnumEventTiming?, Delivery: EnumEventDelivery?}?) -> EventTable) & {
documentation: EventTable declares a network event table that sends events between the server and clients, such as a player's request to attack or the server's report of a hit. It returns an EventTable handle for firing and reading events.

name: F32
documentation: F32 is the field type of a 32-bit float. A sent number is rounded to a 32-bit float, and in a `ToServer` event the server drops the packet on NaN or infinity.

name: I32
documentation: I32 is the field type of a signed 32-bit whole number. A sent number loses its fraction.

name: Input
documentation: Input reads the local player's keyboard, mouse, gamepad and touch input and sets the cursor and UI selection. It works in client scripts only. To tell the server about a player action, fire an EventTable event.
