name: Instance
documentation: Instance is the field type of a reference to an instance, or nil. A read returns the receiver's instance with the same network ID, or nil when it does not exist there.

name: Lighting
documentation: Lighting has the place-wide sun, ambient light, sky, clouds, fog and camera exposure. For lamps on parts, add `Light` or `SpotCone` instead.

name: Locale
documentation: Locale gets and sets the player's language and translates text into it. Only clients have a language; on the server `Get` returns `"en"`, `Set` returns `false` and `"unavailable"`, and `Translate` returns its key.

name: Materials
documentation: Materials lists, reads, defines, and removes the surface materials of a place. A material sets how its parts look, collide, and sound. A material with a `Shader` draws its parts with a shader from the project's `shaders` folder; see Writing a material shader.

name: Navigation
documentation: Navigation finds walkable paths across the place and walks characters along them, around walls, up ramps, and through doorways.

name: Particles
documentation: Particles plays and stops particle effects, and bursts and clears emitters. See particle effects for how to build them. A call on the server shows on every client; a call on a client shows on that client alone.

name: Physics
documentation: Physics has the place-wide simulation settings, the collision groups, and the spatial queries against collider shapes. The server and each client step their own physics world, and a call acts on the world of the side that makes it.

name: Players
documentation: Players looks up players and their characters, fires signals when players join, leave, chat or spawn, and reports friend status.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local red = Instance.new("Team")
red.Name = "Red"
red.TeamId = 1
red.TeamColor = Vector3.new(1, 0.25, 0.25)

local spectators = Instance.new("Team")
spectators.Name = "Spectators"
spectators.TeamId = 2
spectators:RemoveComponent("AutoAssignable")

name: Prefabs
documentation: Prefabs spawns copies of prefabs and resets edited copies to their prefab's values. A prefab is a saved tree of instances that Studio exports with File > Export Selection... to an `.ldv` file named after the prefab.

name: Profiler
documentation: Profiler reads frame times and per-script times on the machine that runs the script. To time one block of code, use `tick`.

name: Session
documentation: Session reports the place, the server clock, and the connection of this client. All of its functions and signals are deprecated; use Players instead.

name: Sound
documentation: Sound plays one-shot sounds at world positions and sets how loud touching parts sound. For a sound that loops or needs Play and Stop, use a `Sound` instance or a `Sound` component on a part instead.

name: Store
documentation: Store saves tables by key to disk on the server machine, so they survive a server restart. Use `game.CloudStore` when players need their data across servers.

name: String
documentation: String is the field type of a string of at most 64 bytes with no zero byte.

name: Tags
documentation: Tags signals when instances gain or lose a tag. A tag is a name with no fields, added with `instance:AddComponent(game.World.Pair("Tag", name))` and found with World.Each or World.Query and the same pair. Tags replicate to clients and save with the place.

name: ToClients
documentation: ToClients is the direction of a table whose events go from the server to clients. Server scripts fire them with `FireAllClients` or `FireClient`.

name: ToServer
documentation: ToServer is the direction of a table whose events go from clients to the server. Client scripts fire them with `FireServer`, and the server gets each event with the player who sent it. The server drops the whole packet and disconnects the player if a packet has malformed data, a non-finite number or a boolean byte above 1.

name: Trails
documentation: short-lived beam and bullet trails

name: Tween
documentation: Tween animates a property from its current value to a target value over time.

name: U8
documentation: U8 is the field type of a whole number from 0 to 255. A sent number clamps to that range and loses its fraction.

name: VR
documentation: client VR poses, controller inputs, haptics, and play-space state

name: Vec3
documentation: Vec3 is the field type of a vector of three 32-bit floats. In a `ToServer` event, the server drops the packet on NaN or infinity.

name: World
documentation: World is the top of the place's tree of parts and entities. It also runs queries over scene entities and schedules per-frame systems. The server and each client have their own world, and a call acts on the world of the side that makes it.

name: DrainMarkers
type: @[deprecated {use = "Instance.MarkerReached"}] () -> ({{Entity: Instance, Clip: string, Marker: string}}, boolean)
documentation: DrainMarkers returns the clip markers that playback crossed.

name: FirstScriptLayer
documentation: FirstScriptLayer is the lowest AnimLayers index a script may write. Writing a lower layer raises an error.

name: GetJoints
documentation: read the rig's joints parents first, each with its bind pivot in the rig

name: Part
type: {Head: number, Torso: number, LeftArm: number, RightArm: number, LeftLeg: number, RightLeg: number}
documentation: Part has the limb flags for the `mask` of an animation layer. A masked layer moves only those limbs; the rest of the body keeps playing the lower layers.

name: Avatar
type: (player: Instance, cb: (avatar: AvatarManifest?, err: string?) -> ()) -> ContentRequest
documentation: Avatar looks up the avatar a player wears and returns a `ContentRequest` handle. The callback receives a manifest table with `UserId`, `Body` and `BodyColors` (keyed by `"Head"`, `"Torso"`, `"LeftArm"`, `"RightArm"`, `"LeftLeg"`, and `"RightLeg"`), `Face`, `Shirt`, `Pants`, and up to 24 `Accessories` (`Asset`, `Slot`, `Sha256`).
notes: The callback receives `nil, nil` when the player has no platform account, or on a local playtest server when the player is not the signed-in editor.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    game.Content.Avatar(player, function(manifest, _err)
        -- nil on error or when the player has no avatar
        if not manifest then
            return
        end
        for _, item in manifest.Accessories do
            game.Content.Fetch(item.Asset, item.Sha256, function(asset, _fetchErr)
                local character = player.Character
                if asset and character then
                    character:AddAccessory(asset)
                end
            end)
        end
    end)
end)

name: Fetch
type: (id: string, sha256: string?, cb: (asset: ContentAsset?, err: string?) -> ()) -> ContentRequest
documentation: Fetch downloads an asset into the memory cache and returns a `ContentRequest` handle. The callback receives a `ContentAsset`, or `nil` and an error string.
notes: The callback runs on a later frame, even when the asset is already cached.
The cache keeps up to 128 assets and 32 MiB of scenes, and drops the least recently used asset when full. A larger scene fails with `"the asset is larger than the memory the runtime holds"`.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
-- pass nil to skip the SHA-256 check
local request = game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset, err)
    if not asset then
        warn("Fetch failed: " .. tostring(err))
        return
    end
    if asset.Type == "scene" then
        game.Content.Spawn(asset)
    end
end)

-- give up if the download takes longer than 10 seconds
task.delay(10, function()
    if request.Pending then
        request:Cancel()
    end
end)

name: Headshot
type: ((userId: number) -> string) & ((self: any, userId: number) -> string)
documentation: Headshot returns the texture asset id of a user's headshot portrait, or `""` when `userId` is 0 or less. The user does not need to be in the server.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local hud = Instance.new("HUD")
hud.UIRoot = true
hud.UIRect.Size = UDim2.new(1, 0, 1, 0)
hud.Parent = game.World

local slots = 0
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    local portrait = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
    portrait.UIRect.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(96, 96)
    portrait.UIRect.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(20 + slots * 104, 20)
    -- the label draws nothing until the portrait downloads
    portrait.Image = game.Content.Headshot(player.UserId)
    portrait.Parent = hud
    slots += 1
end)

name: ReadData
type: ((path: string) -> buffer?) & ((self: any, path: string) -> buffer?)
documentation: read a bundled read-only binary file under data/ into a Luau buffer, or nil if not present

name: Spawn
type: ((asset: ContentAsset) -> Instance?) & ((self: any, asset: ContentAsset) -> Instance?)
documentation: Spawn creates the instance tree of a fetched scene and returns its root. It returns `nil` when the asset is not a scene or was dropped from the cache.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Content.Fetch("1000000000000001", nil, function(asset, _err)
    if asset and asset.Type == "scene" then
        local root = game.Content.Spawn(asset)
        if root then
            -- place the spawned scene 10 units up
            root.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)
        end
    end
end)

name: Intersect
documentation: Intersect replaces the parts with one union that keeps only the volume they all share.
notes: Returns `nil, "result is empty"` when the parts do not overlap.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local left = Instance.new("Part")
left.Anchored = true
left.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)

local right = Instance.new("Part")
right.Anchored = true
right.Position = Vector3.new(2, 5, 0)

-- keep only the overlap of the two boxes
local overlap, err = game.Csg.Intersect({ left, right })
if not overlap then
    warn("intersect failed: " .. (err or ""))
end

name: Negate
documentation: Negate wraps each part in a negative instance named `"Negate"` that cuts the part's volume out of any union it joins. Outside a union, a negative instance draws translucent pink and does not collide.
notes: Passing a negative instance unwraps its part instead, like Separate.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local wall = Instance.new("Part")
wall.Anchored = true
wall.Size = Vector3.new(12, 8, 1)
wall.Position = Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)

local window = Instance.new("Part")
window.Anchored = true
window.Size = Vector3.new(3, 3, 2)
window.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)

-- turn the window into a hole, then join it with the wall
local holes = game.Csg.Negate({ window })
if holes then
    table.insert(holes, 1, wall)
    game.Csg.Union(holes)
end

name: Separate
type: ((union: Instance) -> ({Instance}?, string?)) & ((self: any, union: Instance) -> ({Instance}?, string?))
documentation: Separate destroys a union or negative instance after moving its children to its parent, and returns the children.
notes: If the union was resized, the stretch is applied to the children's positions and sizes.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local a = Instance.new("Part")
a.Anchored = true
local b = Instance.new("Part")
b.Anchored = true
b.Position = Vector3.new(4, 0, 0)

local union = game.Csg.Union({ a, b })
if union then
    -- break the union back into its parts
    local pieces = game.Csg.Separate(union)
    if pieces then
        for _, piece in pieces do
            piece.Name = "Debris"
        end
    end
end

name: Subtract
type: ((main: Instance, cutters: {Instance}) -> (Instance?, string?)) & ((self: any, main: Instance, cutters: {Instance}) -> (Instance?, string?))
documentation: Subtract cuts `cutters` out of `main` and returns one union of what remains, such as a wall with a doorway. The union takes `main`'s parent, rotation, color, material, and anchoring.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local wall = Instance.new("Part")
wall.Anchored = true
wall.Size = Vector3.new(12, 8, 1)
wall.Position = Vector3.new(0, 4, 0)

local doorway = Instance.new("Part")
doorway.Anchored = true
doorway.Size = Vector3.new(4, 6, 2)
doorway.Position = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)

-- cut the doorway out of the wall
local cut, err = game.Csg.Subtract(wall, { doorway })
if cut then
    cut.Name = "WallWithDoor"
else
    warn("doorway failed: " .. (err or ""))
end

name: Union
documentation: Union joins parts into one union that draws and collides as a single solid. The parts move inside the union and keep their identity, so existing references to them stay valid.
notes: Returns `nil` and `"union is too complex (<triangles> triangles, limit 20000)"` when the surface needs too many triangles; use fewer parts or fewer round parts.
Returns `nil` and `"too many operands (limit 4096)"` when the call names too many parts.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local left = Instance.new("Part")
left.Anchored = true
left.Size = Vector3.new(1, 6, 1)
left.Position = Vector3.new(-3, 3, 0)

local right = Instance.new("Part")
right.Anchored = true
right.Size = Vector3.new(1, 6, 1)
right.Position = Vector3.new(3, 3, 0)

local beam = Instance.new("Part")
beam.Anchored = true
beam.Size = Vector3.new(7, 1, 1)
beam.Position = Vector3.new(0, 6.5, 0)

-- join two posts and a beam into one arch
local arch, err = game.Csg.Union({ left, right, beam })
if arch then
    arch.Name = "Arch"
else
    warn("arch failed: " .. (err or ""))
end

name: ActionType
documentation: ActionType has the kinds of `InputAction`, for its `Type` property.

name: Behavior
documentation: Behavior has the values of `MouseBehavior`.

name: Button
type: {Left: number, Right: number, Middle: number, X1: number, X2: number}
documentation: Button has the mouse buttons for ButtonDown and ButtonPressed.

name: ButtonDown
type: ((button: number) -> boolean) & ((self: any, button: number) -> boolean)
documentation: ButtonDown returns true while a mouse button is held down.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
function Update(dt: number)
    if game.Input.ButtonDown(game.Input.Button.Right) then
        print("aiming")
    end
end

name: ButtonPressed
type: ((button: number) -> boolean) & ((self: any, button: number) -> boolean)
documentation: ButtonPressed returns true on the frame a mouse button goes down, and false after. A trackpad tap between two frames reads true for that frame.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
function Update(dt: number)
    if game.Input.ButtonPressed(game.Input.Button.Left) then
        print("fire")
    end
end

name: CaptureControls
documentation: suppresses built-in locomotion and jump controls while raw key reads and Escape keep working

name: CaptureText
documentation: enables OS text input and routes committed UTF-8 text to Input.TextInput while menu and console are closed

name: Cursor
type: {Auto: number, Arrow: number, Pointer: number, Text: number, Crosshair: number, ResizeEW: number, ResizeNS: number, ResizeNWSE: number, ResizeNESW: number, Grab: number, Grabbing: number, Wait: number, Progress: number, NotAllowed: number, Move: number, Hidden: number}
documentation: Cursor has the cursor shapes for `MouseCursor` and the UI `Cursor` property. A UI `Cursor` also takes the name, as in `frame.Cursor = "Pointer"`.

name: Device
type: {KeyboardAndMouse: number, Gamepad: number, Touch: number, VR: number}
documentation: Device has the values of `PreferredInput`.

name: InputBegan
documentation: InputBegan fires with `input` and `processed` when a key or mouse button goes down. `input` has `Key` (or 0), `Button` (or -1) and `Device`. `processed` is true when the UI took the press, such as typing in a text box or clicking a UI element, and while the escape menu is open.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
game.Input.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, processed)
    if not processed and input.Key == game.Input.Key.E then
        print("use")
    end
end)

name: InputEnded
documentation: InputEnded fires with `input` and `processed`, as in InputBegan, when a key or mouse button comes up.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
game.Input.InputEnded:Connect(function(input, processed)
    if input.Button == game.Input.Button.Left then
        print("released")
    end
end)

name: Key
type: {Backspace: number, Tab: number, Return: number, Pause: number, CapsLock: number, Escape: number, Space: number, PageUp: number, PageDown: number, End: number, Home: number, Left: number, Up: number, Right: number, Down: number, Insert: number, Delete: number, Zero: number, One: number, Two: number, Three: number, Four: number, Five: number, Six: number, Seven: number, Eight: number, Nine: number, S: number, T: number, U: number, V: number, W: number, X: number, Y: number, Z: number, LeftGui: number, RightGui: number, Numpad0: number, Numpad1: number, Numpad2: number, Numpad3: number, Numpad4: number, Numpad5: number, Numpad6: number, Numpad7: number, Numpad8: number, Numpad9: number, NumpadMultiply: number, NumpadAdd: number, NumpadSubtract: number, NumpadDecimal: number, NumpadDivide: number, F1: number, F2: number, F3: number, F4: number, F5: number, F6: number, F7: number, F8: number, F9: number, F10: number, F11: number, F12: number, NumLock: number, ScrollLock: number, LeftShift: number, RightShift: number, LeftControl: number, RightControl: number, LeftAlt: number, RightAlt: number, Semicolon: number, Equals: number, Comma: number, Minus: number, Period: number, Slash: number, Backquote: number, LeftBracket: number, Backslash: number, RightBracket: number, Apostrophe: number, ButtonA: number, ButtonB: number, ButtonX: number, ButtonY: number, ButtonL1: number, ButtonR1: number, ButtonL2: number, ButtonR2: number, ButtonSelect: number, ButtonStart: number, ButtonL3: number, ButtonR3: number, DPadUp: number, DPadDown: number, DPadLeft: number, VRPrimaryRight: number, VRSecondaryRight: number, VRThumbstickLeft: number, VRThumbstickRight: number, VRMenu: number}
documentation: Key has the key codes for KeyDown and KeyPressed.

name: KeyDown
type: ((keyCode: number) -> boolean) & ((self: any, keyCode: number) -> boolean)
documentation: KeyDown returns true while a key is held down.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
function Update(dt: number)
    if game.Input.KeyDown(game.Input.Key.W) then
        print("moving forward")
    end
end

name: KeyPressed
type: ((keyCode: number) -> boolean) & ((self: any, keyCode: number) -> boolean)
documentation: KeyPressed returns true on the frame a key goes down, and false after. A key that goes down and up between two frames reads true for that frame.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
function Update(dt: number)
    if game.Input.KeyPressed(game.Input.Key.Space) then
        print("jump")
    end
end

name: KeysDown
documentation: KeysDown returns the key codes held down, in ascending order. Keys that a text box or UI selection takes are left out.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
function Update(dt: number)
    local held = game.Input.KeysDown()
    if table.find(held, game.Input.Key.LeftControl)
        and table.find(held, game.Input.Key.S) then
        print("save")
    end
end

name: LookDelta
documentation: LookDelta is the mouse movement since the last script update, in the units the built-in camera turns by, with Z 0. It reads the same at every UI Scale and window size, before the player's sensitivity and invert settings.

name: MouseBehavior
documentation: MouseBehavior is whether the cursor moves freely or is locked, a value from `game.Input.Behavior`.

name: MouseCursor
documentation: MouseCursor is the cursor shape over the 3D world and over UI elements whose `Cursor` is `"Auto"`, a value from `game.Input.Cursor`. A UI element's own `Cursor`, the I-beam over a text box and the pointing hand over a `ClickDetector` part show instead.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
game.Input.MouseCursor = game.Input.Cursor.Crosshair

name: MouseDelta
documentation: MouseDelta is the cursor movement since the last script update, in UI points, with Z 0. Use it to drag UI; to turn a camera, read LookDelta.

name: MouseIconEnabled
documentation: MouseIconEnabled shows the cursor when true and hides it everywhere when false. `MousePosition`, `PointerRay` and UI signals still follow the hidden cursor, so a script can draw its own reticle.

name: MousePosition
documentation: MousePosition is the cursor position in UI points from the top-left corner of the game view, with Z 0. A Frame at this offset is under the cursor. While the mouse is locked, the position stays still.

name: PointerRay
documentation: PointerRay returns the origin and unit direction of the ray from the camera through the cursor. It returns nil before the game view has a size.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local origin, direction = game.Input.PointerRay()
if origin and direction then
    local hit = game.Physics.Raycast(origin, direction, 100)
    if hit and hit.Instance then
        print(hit.Instance.Name)
    end
end

name: PreferredInput
documentation: PreferredInput is the kind of device the player used last, a value from `game.Input.Device`.

name: PreferredInputChanged
documentation: PreferredInputChanged fires with the new `PreferredInput` when the player switches between keyboard and mouse, gamepad, and touch.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
game.Input.PreferredInputChanged:Connect(function(device)
    print(device == game.Input.Device.Touch)
end)

name: Rotation
documentation: Rotation has the values of `RotationType`.

name: RotationType
documentation: RotationType is whether the character faces the way it walks or the way the camera looks, a value from `game.Input.Rotation`.

name: Scroll
documentation: Scroll is the mouse wheel movement since the last script update, positive up.

name: Selected
documentation: Selected is the UI element that has the gamepad and keyboard selection, or nil. The arrow keys, the d-pad and the left stick move the selection to the nearest element in that direction, and Enter or A clicks it. Those keys do not reach `KeyDown`, `KeyPressed` or the character while an element is selected; B, Escape and other keys still do.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local screen = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screen.Parent = game.Overlay
local play = Instance.new("TextButton")
play.Text = "Play"
play.Parent = screen
play.Activated:Connect(function()
    print("play")
end)
game.Input.Selected = play -- Enter or A now clicks Play

name: SetCustomCursor
type: ((shape: number, image: string?, hotX: number?, hotY: number?) -> ()) & ((self: any, shape: number, image: string?, hotX: number?, hotY: number?) -> ())
documentation: SetCustomCursor shows an image in place of one cursor shape (other than `Auto` and `Hidden`), with an optional click point in image pixels. Setting `Pointer` changes the cursor over every button, and setting `Arrow` changes it over the 3D world; passing `nil` for `image` brings the theme cursor back. The image can be at most 256 by 256 pixels; if it is larger or fails to load, the engine prints a warning and keeps the theme cursor.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local SWORD_CURSOR = "72057594037927978"
game.Input.SetCustomCursor(game.Input.Cursor.Arrow, SWORD_CURSOR, 2, 2)
task.wait(10)
game.Input.SetCustomCursor(game.Input.Cursor.Arrow, nil)

name: TextInput
documentation: fires (text: string) with committed UTF-8 text when Input.CaptureText is true

name: Ambient
type: { Tint: vector, Intensity: number, Source: EnumAmbientSource, Contribution: number }
documentation: Ambient is the indirect light on surfaces in shadow.
code_sample:
-- Server script: dim blue night light.
local amb = game.Lighting.Ambient
amb.Source = "Color"
amb.Tint = Vector3.new(0.3, 0.35, 0.5)
amb.Intensity = 0.2

name: AtmosphereSky
type: { SunDiskScale: number, NightSky: string, StarLuminance: number }
documentation: AtmosphereSky is a deprecated group; `AtmosphereSky` on the Environment has no settings.

name: Background
type: { Mode: EnumBackgroundMode, Color: vector, Energy: number }
documentation: Background is the color behind the scene when there is no sky, and the brightness of the background and sky.

name: Clouds
type: { Coverage: number, Density: number, Color: vector, BaseHeight: number, Thickness: number, WindX: number, WindZ: number, WindSpeed: number, EvolutionSpeed: number, Seed: number, Quality: number, Anisotropy: number, Erosion: number, MultipleScattering: number, PowderStrength: number, BottomDarkening: number, ShadowStrength: number }
documentation: Clouds is the volumetric cloud layer, drawn in front of every kind of sky.
code_sample:
-- Server script: an overcast sky.
local clouds = game.Lighting.Clouds
clouds.Coverage = 0.9
clouds.BottomDarkening = 0.5

name: Exposure
documentation: Exposure is the range of the camera's automatic exposure, in exposure values (EV). The camera picks an EV between `MinEV` and `MaxEV` from the brightness in view; equal values fix the exposure.
code_sample:
-- Server script: fixed exposure for a cave level.
local exposure = game.Lighting.Exposure
exposure.MinEV = 5
exposure.MaxEV = 5

name: Flare
type: { Intensity: number, Scale: number, Tint: vector, Ghost: number, Rays: number }
documentation: Flare is the lens flare and sun rays that show when the camera faces the sun.

name: Fog
type: { Color: vector, Mode: EnumFogMode, Density: number, Start: number, End: number }
documentation: Fog is the distance fog that fades far parts into a color. It leaves the sky clear.
code_sample:
-- Server script: thick fog that hides parts past 80 units.
local fog = game.Lighting.Fog
fog.Mode = "Linear"
fog.Start = 10
fog.End = 80
fog.Color = Vector3.new(0.7, 0.75, 0.8)

name: PanoramaSky
type: { Panorama: string, Rotation: number, Energy: number }
documentation: PanoramaSky is a sky drawn from one panorama or cube texture.

name: Shadows
type: { Mode: EnumShadowMode, Fill: number, MaxDistance: number }
documentation: Shadows is how the sun casts shadows.

name: SixSidedSky
type: { SkyboxBk: string, SkyboxDn: string, SkyboxFt: string, SkyboxLf: string, SkyboxRt: string, SkyboxUp: string, Rotation: number, Energy: number }
documentation: SixSidedSky is a sky drawn from six square face textures.

name: Stars
documentation: Stars is a deprecated group; the atmosphere sky draws no stars.

name: Sun
type: { Azimuth: number, Elevation: number, Tint: vector, Intensity: number }
documentation: Sun is the direction, color and strength of sunlight. Writing `Azimuth` or `Elevation` turns the Sun instance.
code_sample:
-- Server script: the sun circles the sky once every 2 minutes.
function Update(dt: number)
    local sun = game.Lighting.Sun
    sun.Azimuth = (sun.Azimuth + dt * 3) % 360
end

name: SunDisk
documentation: SunDisk is the size of the sun's disk in an atmosphere sky. A panorama or six-sided sky draws whatever sun its texture has.

name: Get
documentation: Get returns the active language tag, `"en"` until something changes it.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local lang = game.Locale.Get()
if lang == "ja" or string.sub(lang, 1, 2) == "zh" then
    print("use a CJK font")
end

name: Set
type: ((tag: string) -> (boolean, string)) & ((self: any, tag: string) -> (boolean, string))
documentation: Set switches the active language. It returns `true` and `"changed"` or `"unchanged"`, or `false` and `"rejected"` when the tag is not valid.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local ok, status = game.Locale.Set("pt-BR")
if not ok then
    warn("cannot switch language: " .. status)
end

name: Translate
type: ((key: string) -> string) & ((self: any, key: string) -> string)
documentation: Translate returns the translation of an English key in the active language, or the key itself when there is none.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local template = game.Locale.Translate("Welcome, {name}!")
print((string.gsub(template, "{name}", "Ana")))

name: DefineMaterial
type: ((spec: MaterialSpec, parent: string?) -> string) & ((self: any, spec: MaterialSpec, parent: string?) -> string)
documentation: DefineMaterial defines a material, or redefines the one with the same `Id`, and returns its asset id. Without a `Name`, the material gets the next free name.
notes: Passing `parent`, a material asset id, saves it in the material file. When the file loads, every table that `spec` leaves out comes from `parent`.
Updates the material's surfaces and their physics. When the server runs from a project, it also writes the material file to the project's `materials` folder.

name: GetMaterial
type: ((idOrName: string) -> MaterialSpec) & ((self: any, idOrName: string) -> MaterialSpec)
documentation: GetMaterial returns the MaterialSpec of a material by asset id or name, in the form `DefineMaterial` takes.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local spec = game.Materials.GetMaterial("Plastic")

-- Surface can be nil
if spec.Surface then
    local roughness = spec.Surface.RoughnessMult
end

name: GetMaterials
documentation: GetMaterials returns an array of MaterialEntry tables with the asset id, name, pipeline, and surface model of every material in the place.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local materials = game.Materials.GetMaterials()

-- count the materials in this place
local count = #materials

name: ReloadMaterial
type: ((idOrName: string) -> boolean) & ((self: any, idOrName: string) -> boolean)
documentation: ReloadMaterial reads a material file from the project's `materials` folder again and redefines the material with it. Its surfaces keep the material.
code_sample:
-- Server script, after editing materials/Lagoon in the project.
game.Materials.ReloadMaterial("Lagoon")

name: RemoveMaterial
type: ((idOrName: string, replacementIdOrName: string?) -> boolean) & ((self: any, idOrName: string, replacementIdOrName: string?) -> boolean)
documentation: RemoveMaterial removes a material and moves its surfaces to `replacementIdOrName`, or when that is omitted, to the material's parent or `Plastic`.
notes: When the server runs from a project, deletes the material file from the project's `materials` folder.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Materials.DefineMaterial({
    Id = "2810246167479189505",
    Name = "OldBrick",
    Pipeline = "Opaque",
    Model = "UV",
    Surface = {},
})

-- parts made of OldBrick now use Plastic
game.Materials.RemoveMaterial("OldBrick", "Plastic")

name: ReplaceMaterial
type: ((oldIdOrName: string, newIdOrName: string) -> boolean) & ((self: any, oldIdOrName: string, newIdOrName: string) -> boolean)
documentation: ReplaceMaterial moves every surface from one material to another and removes the first.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Materials.DefineMaterial({
    Id = "2810246167479189505",
    Name = "CrackedConcrete",
    Pipeline = "Opaque",
    Model = "UV",
    Surface = {},
})

-- move every CrackedConcrete surface to Plastic
game.Materials.ReplaceMaterial("CrackedConcrete", "Plastic")

name: SetParam
type: ((idOrName: string, name: string, value: number | vector | boolean | string) -> ()) & ((self: any, idOrName: string, name: string, value: number | vector | boolean | string) -> ())
documentation: SetParam sets one field of a material's shader on this client from the next frame. Pass a number, `Vector3` or `Color3`, boolean, or texture asset id string that matches the field; see parameters.
notes: Sends nothing over the network; the material file, the server, and other players keep the material's `Params`. A shader that animates with time alone can read SurfaceInput.time instead.
code_sample:
-- Client script in a place whose Ink material has an inkWeight shader field.
local clock = 0

-- pulse the ink width of the Ink material every frame
function Update(dt: number)
    clock += dt
    game.Materials.SetParam("Ink", "inkWeight", 4 + 2 * math.sin(clock * 2))
end

name: AgentHeight
documentation: AgentHeight is the lowest ceiling a path passes under, in units. It must be above 0 and at most 255 times `CellHeight`.

name: AgentHeight
documentation: AgentHeight is the lowest ceiling a path passes under, in units. It must be above 0 and at most 255 times `CellHeight`.

name: AgentMaxClimb
documentation: AgentMaxClimb is the highest step a path climbs, in units. It must be above 0 and at most `AgentHeight`.

name: AgentMaxClimb
documentation: AgentMaxClimb is the highest step a path climbs, in units. It must be above 0 and at most `AgentHeight`.

name: AgentMaxSlope
documentation: AgentMaxSlope is the steepest slope a path walks up, in degrees, above 0 and below 90.

name: AgentMaxSlope
documentation: AgentMaxSlope is the steepest slope a path walks up, in degrees, above 0 and below 90.

name: AgentRadius
documentation: AgentRadius is how far paths keep from walls and edges, in units. It must be above 0 and at most 64 times `CellSize`.

name: AgentRadius
documentation: AgentRadius is how far paths keep from walls and edges, in units. It must be above 0 and at most 64 times `CellSize`.

name: CellHeight
documentation: CellHeight is the height of one mesh cell, from 0.05 to 4 units.

name: CellHeight
documentation: CellHeight is the height of one mesh cell, from 0.05 to 4 units.

name: CellSize
documentation: CellSize is the width of one mesh cell, from 0.05 to 4 units. Smaller cells follow walls more closely and take longer to build.

name: CellSize
documentation: CellSize is the width of one mesh cell, from 0.05 to 4 units. Smaller cells follow walls more closely and take longer to build.

name: ComputePath
type: ((from: vector, to: vector, out: {vector}?) -> (EnumPathStatus, {vector})) & ((self: any, from: vector, to: vector, out: {vector}?) -> (EnumPathStatus, {vector}))
documentation: ComputePath returns a `PathStatus` and up to 256 corners along the shortest walkable path between `from` and `to`, filling `out` when given. `Success` reaches `to`, `ClosestNoPath` ends at the reachable point closest to `to`, and `NoPath` returns an empty array.
notes: Looks for the mesh within twice `AgentRadius` sideways and `AgentHeight` above or below each point, so pass points on or slightly above the floor.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local floor = Instance.new("Part")
floor.Anchored = true
floor.Size = Vector3.new(100, 1, 100)

-- pass a table to fill so repeated queries can reuse it
local corners: {vector} = {}
local status = game.Navigation.ComputePath(
    Vector3.new(-40, 1, -40),
    Vector3.new(40, 1, 40),
    corners
)
if status == "Success" then
    local marker = Instance.new("Part")
    marker.Anchored = true
    marker.Position = corners[#corners]
end

name: MoveTo
type: ((character: Instance, target: vector) -> EnumPathStatus) & ((self: any, character: Instance, target: vector) -> EnumPathStatus)
documentation: MoveTo walks `character` along the shortest walkable path to `target` and returns its `PathStatus` (see ComputePath). Calling it again replaces the path.
notes: The walk ends when `PathFollower.Status` becomes `Arrived` or `Stuck`, when the character dies, or when Stop is called. On `NoPath` the character stays where it is.
When the mesh changes along the path, the character plans again from where it is, and stops if no path remains.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local floor = Instance.new("Part")
floor.Anchored = true
floor.Size = Vector3.new(100, 1, 100)

-- a custom NPC needs CharacterPhysics and Locomotion
local guard = Instance.new("Part")
guard.Position = Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
guard:AddComponent("CharacterPhysics")
guard:AddComponent("Locomotion")

game.Navigation.MoveTo(guard, Vector3.new(30, 1, 30))

name: Stop
documentation: Stop ends the walk that MoveTo started and sets `PathFollower.Status` to `Idle`. It sets the move input to zero, so the character slows down like a player who releases the movement keys.

name: TileSize
documentation: TileSize is the number of cells along one side of a mesh tile, from 16 to 256. A changed part rebuilds the tiles it touches, so smaller tiles rebuild faster.

name: TileSize
documentation: TileSize is the number of cells along one side of a mesh tile, from 16 to 256. A changed part rebuilds the tiles it touches, so smaller tiles rebuild faster.

name: Clear
documentation: Clear removes every live particle of an emitter at once.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: three bursts of sparks, then clear them.
local sparks = Instance.new("Sparks")
sparks:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
sparks.Parent = self

for i = 1, 3 do
    game.Particles.Emit(sparks, 32)
    task.wait(0.5)
end
game.Particles.Clear(sparks)

name: Emit
type: ((emitter: Instance, count: number?) -> ()) & ((self: any, emitter: Instance, count: number?) -> ())
documentation: Emit spawns a burst of particles from an emitter, 16 when no count is given.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: burst 50 sparks.
local sparks = Instance.new("Sparks")
sparks:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
sparks.Parent = self
game.Particles.Emit(sparks, 50)

name: Play
documentation: Play starts a particle effect, or restarts it from the beginning.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: a flame that burns for 2 seconds.
local flame = Instance.new("Flame")
flame:AddComponent("ParticleEffect")
local embers = Instance.new("Embers")
embers:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
embers.Parent = flame
flame.Parent = self

game.Particles.Play(flame)
task.wait(2)
game.Particles.Stop(flame, "Finish") -- live particles fade out

name: PlayAt
type: ((effect: string, position: vector) -> Instance) & ((self: any, effect: string, position: vector) -> Instance)
documentation: PlayAt spawns a particle effect at a world position and plays it. `effect` is a prefab name, an asset, or `"ParticleEmitter"` for default sparks. The new instance is removed after 5 seconds unless the prefab sets its own `Lifetime`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: a 5-second stream of sparks at the part.
local sparks = game.Particles.PlayAt("ParticleEmitter", self.Position)
print(sparks.Name) -- prints ParticleEmitter

name: Stop
type: ((effect: Instance, mode: EnumParticleStopMode?) -> ()) & ((self: any, effect: Instance, mode: EnumParticleStopMode?) -> ())
documentation: Stop stops a particle effect. `"Finish"`, the default, lets live particles fade out; `"Clear"` removes them at once.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: burn for 1 second, then clear live particles at once.
local flame = Instance.new("Flame")
flame:AddComponent("ParticleEffect")
local embers = Instance.new("Embers")
embers:AddComponent("ParticleEmitter", "ParticleSpawnRate", "ParticleShapeSphere",
    "ParticleVelocityCone", "ParticleSprite")
embers.Parent = flame
flame.Parent = self

game.Particles.Play(flame)
task.wait(1)
game.Particles.Stop(flame, "Clear")

name: DrainTouchEvents
documentation: DrainTouchEvents returns the touches that began or ended since this script last called it.
deprecation: Connect `Instance.Touched` and `Instance.TouchEnded` on the part instead.

name: EmitAcousticStimulus
type: ((position: vector, radius: number, loudness: number, emitter: Instance?, tag: number?) -> number) & ((self: any, position: vector, radius: number, loudness: number, emitter: Instance?, tag: number?) -> number)
documentation: EmitAcousticStimulus makes a sound at `position` that listeners with `HearingSense` hear within `radius * loudness` units, scaled by each listener's sensitivity, and returns how many heard it. The `emitter` never hears itself.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local heard = game.Physics.EmitAcousticStimulus(self.Position, 20, 2, self)
print(heard)

name: Explode
type: ((position: vector, radius: number, force: number) -> number) & ((self: any, position: vector, radius: number, force: number) -> number)
documentation: Explode breaks welds and pushes unanchored bodies away from `position` within `radius` units, and returns how many bodies it pushed. A negative `force` pulls bodies in.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a grenade part.
task.wait(3)
game.Physics.Explode(self.Position, 15, 4000)
self:Destroy()

name: FallenPartsDestroyHeight
documentation: FallenPartsDestroyHeight is the world Y below which moving parts are destroyed and characters die. Anchored parts are never destroyed this way.

name: Gravity
documentation: Gravity is the acceleration along the world Y axis, in units per second squared, that pulls every unanchored body. Negative values pull down. A server write replicates to clients.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Physics.Gravity = -50
print(math.round(game.Physics.Gravity)) -- prints -50

name: Gravity
documentation: Gravity is the acceleration along the world Y axis, in units per second squared, that pulls every unanchored body. Negative values pull down. A server write replicates to clients.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Physics.Gravity = -50
print(math.round(game.Physics.Gravity)) -- prints -50

name: IsSleeping
type: ((e: Instance) -> boolean) & ((self: any, e: Instance) -> boolean)
documentation: IsSleeping returns true when the physics body of `e` is at rest and the simulation skips it.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local floor = Instance.new("Part")
floor.Size = Vector3.new(20, 1, 20)
floor.Position = Vector3.new(0, -2, 0)
floor.Anchored = true
floor.Parent = game.World

self.Anchored = false
task.wait(2)
print(game.Physics.IsSleeping(self)) -- prints true

name: IsStatic
type: ((e: Instance) -> boolean) & ((self: any, e: Instance) -> boolean)
documentation: whether the assembly of an entity is static, so forces and impulses on it are ignored

name: OverlapBox
type: (center: vector, half: vector, rotation: vector?, out: {Instance} | QueryParams | nil, params: QueryParams?) -> (number, {Instance})
documentation: OverlapBox returns the count and the entities whose shapes overlap a box with half size `half`, rotated by `rotation` in degrees.

name: OverlapSphere
type: (center: vector, radius: number, out: {Instance} | QueryParams | nil, params: QueryParams?) -> (number, {Instance})
documentation: OverlapSphere returns the count and the entities whose shapes overlap a sphere. It fills `out` when you pass one, so a script can reuse one table.

name: Raycast
type: (origin: vector, dir: vector, maxDist: number, params: QueryParams | Instance | nil, mask: number?) -> RaycastResult?
documentation: Raycast returns the first surface hit from `origin` along `dir` within `maxDist` units, or nil. The hit has `Position`, `Normal`, `Instance` and `Distance`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
local hit = game.Physics.Raycast(self.Position, Vector3.new(0, -1, 0), 1000, {
    ExcludeInstances = {self},
})
if hit and hit.Instance then
    print(hit.Instance.Name, hit.Distance)
end

name: RegisterCollisionGroup
documentation: RegisterCollisionGroup adds a collision group named `name`. A part joins it when its `CollisionGroup` is set to that name. A new group collides with every group until `SetCollisionRule` changes that. A place has 32 group slots, and `Default`, `Character` and `CharacterNoCollide` take three of them.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup("Projectile")
game.Physics.SetCollisionRule("Projectile", "Projectile", false)
self.CollisionGroup = "Projectile"
print(self.CollisionGroup) -- prints Projectile

name: RenameCollisionGroup
type: ((from: string, to: string) -> ()) & ((self: any, from: string, to: string) -> ())
documentation: RenameCollisionGroup renames group `from` to `to` and keeps its rules and parts.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup("TeamA")
self.CollisionGroup = "TeamA"
game.Physics.RenameCollisionGroup("TeamA", "Red")
print(self.CollisionGroup) -- prints Red

name: SetCollisionRule
type: ((a: string, b: string, collidable: boolean) -> ()) & ((self: any, a: string, b: string, collidable: boolean) -> ())
documentation: SetCollisionRule sets whether parts of group `a` collide with parts of group `b`. Pass the same group twice to set whether it collides with itself.
notes: Spatial queries follow the rules only when their params name a `CollisionGroup`.
A character still stands on a part whose group does not collide with `Character`.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup("Projectiles")
game.Physics.RegisterCollisionGroup("Debris")
game.Physics.SetCollisionRule("Projectiles", "Debris", false)

name: Shapecast
type: (shape: EnumShapecastShape, size: vector, from: vector, to: vector, rotation: vector?, out: {ShapecastHit} | QueryParams | nil, params: QueryParams?) -> (number, {ShapecastHit})
documentation: Shapecast sweeps a `"Box"`, `"Sphere"` or `"Capsule"` from `from` to `to` and returns the count and every hit, nearest first. Each hit has `Instance`, `Point`, `Normal` and `Fraction` (0 at `from`, 1 at `to`). For `"Box"`, `size` is half the size on each axis. For `"Sphere"`, `size.X` is the radius. For `"Capsule"`, `size.X` is the radius and `size.Y` is half the length of the straight middle.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a sword part.
local from = self.Position
local to = from + Vector3.new(0, 0, -5)
local n, hits = game.Physics.Shapecast("Box", Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 2), from, to, nil, nil, {
    ExcludeInstances = {self},
})
if n > 0 then
    print(hits[1].Instance.Name)
end

name: AliveCharacters
documentation: every live character in the place

name: All
documentation: All returns every player in the session.

name: BindCharacter
documentation: BindCharacter makes an instance the character of a player.

name: CharacterAdded
documentation: CharacterAdded fires with a player and its new character. On the server, a `Position` set in the handler decides where the character appears.
code_sample:
-- Server script: spawn every character 50 units up.
game.Players.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(player, character)
    character.Position = Vector3.new(0, 50, 0)
end)

name: CharacterDied
type: Signal<(player: Instance?, character: Instance?, attacker: Instance?) -> ()>
documentation: CharacterDied fires with the player, the character and the attacker when a character dies. The attacker is the one passed to the last `TakeDamage`, or nil. A fall below `FallenPartsDestroyHeight` clears the attacker.
code_sample:
-- Server script: count kills.
game.Players.CharacterDied:Connect(function(player, character, attacker)
    local killer = attacker and game.Players.FromCharacter(attacker)
    if killer and killer ~= player then
        killer.attr.Kills = (killer.attr.Kills or 0) + 1
    end
end)

name: CharacterOf
documentation: CharacterOf returns the character of a player, or nil.

name: Chat
documentation: Chat sends a chat message from the local player. The server relays it to every client, where `PlayerChatted` fires.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
game.Players.Chat("hello")

name: FriendStatus
type: ((player: Instance) -> EnumFriendStatus) & ((self: any, player: Instance) -> EnumFriendStatus)
documentation: FriendStatus returns the relation of the local player to another player, one of the items of `game.Enum.FriendStatus`. It returns `"Unknown"` on the server.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
for player in game.World.Each("Player") do
    if player ~= game.Players.LocalPlayer then
        print(player.Name, game.Players.FriendStatus(player))
    end
end

name: FriendStatusChanged
documentation: FriendStatusChanged fires with a player and the new `FriendStatus` when the local player's relation to that player changes.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
game.Players.FriendStatusChanged:Connect(function(player, status)
    if status == "FriendRequestReceived" then
        print(player.DisplayName .. " sent you a friend request")
    end
end)

name: FriendsReceived
documentation: FriendsReceived fires with the answer to `RequestFriends`: an array of friends with `UserId`, `Name`, `DisplayName`, `Presence` and `PlaceName`. Only engine CoreScripts may use it.
code_sample:
-- CoreScript.
game.Players.FriendsReceived:Connect(function(friends)
    for _, friend in friends do
        print(friend.DisplayName, friend.Presence)
    end
end)

name: FromCharacter
type: ((character: Instance) -> Instance?) & ((self: any, character: Instance) -> Instance?)
documentation: FromCharacter returns the player that controls a character or one of its body parts, or nil.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: mark players who touch it.
self.Touched:Connect(function(other)
    local player = game.Players.FromCharacter(other)
    if player then
        player.attr.Eliminated = true
    end
end)

name: GameAnnounce
documentation: GameAnnounce fires with a line the server sends to the local player only, such as a notice that the chat filter rejected a message.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
game.Players.GameAnnounce:Connect(function(message)
    print("[Server] " .. message)
end)

name: Get
type: ((userId: number) -> Instance?) & ((self: any, userId: number) -> Instance?)
documentation: Get returns the player with the given user ID, or nil.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    print(game.Players.Get(player.UserId) == player)
end)

name: InviteFriend
documentation: InviteFriend invites a friend to this server by chat message. The outcome arrives through `InviteResult`. Only engine CoreScripts may call it.
code_sample:
-- CoreScript.
game.Players.InviteFriend(12345)

name: InviteResult
type: Signal<(userId: number, success: boolean, reason: string) -> ()>
documentation: InviteResult fires with the friend's user ID, whether the invite was sent, and a reason from `game.Enum.InviteFailure`, once for each `InviteFriend`. Only engine CoreScripts may use it.
code_sample:
-- CoreScript.
game.Players.InviteResult:Connect(function(userId, ok, reason)
    if not ok then
        print("invite to " .. userId .. " failed: " .. reason)
    end
end)

name: IsAdmin
documentation: IsAdmin returns whether a player is an admin of the place.

name: Kick
type: ((player: Instance, reason: string?) -> boolean) & ((self: any, player: Instance, reason: string?) -> boolean)
documentation: Kick disconnects a player from the server and shows them the reason.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerChatted:Connect(function(player, message)
    if message == "!leave" then
        game.Players.Kick(player, "Goodbye")
    end
end)

name: LocalPlayer
documentation: LocalPlayer is the player of this client, or nil on the server and before the player reaches the client. The server owns the player, so a client script cannot write its `attr`.

name: PlayerAdded
documentation: PlayerAdded fires with each player that joins. On the server, every `PlayerAdded` handler runs before `CharacterAdded` fires for that player. On a client, it fires only for players who join after the client scripts start.
code_sample:
-- Server script: show Points on the player list.
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    local stats = Instance.new("leaderstats")
    stats.attr.Points = 0
    stats.Parent = player
end)

name: PlayerChatted
documentation: PlayerChatted fires with the speaker and the text of each chat message.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerChatted:Connect(function(player, message)
    if message == "!ready" then
        player.attr.Ready = true
    end
end)

name: PlayerRemoving
documentation: PlayerRemoving fires with each player that leaves, and for every player when the server shuts down. On shutdown, the world waits up to 30 seconds for `CloudStore` requests started before the handler yields, so a handler can save player data.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    print(player.Name .. " left with " .. (player.attr.Points or 0) .. " points")
end)

name: RequestFriends
documentation: RequestFriends asks the server for the local player's friends who are not on this server. The answer arrives through `FriendsReceived`. Only engine CoreScripts may call it.
code_sample:
-- CoreScript.
game.Players.RequestFriends()

name: Social
type: ((player: Instance, verb: EnumSocialVerb, reason: EnumReportReason?) -> ()) & ((self: any, player: Instance, verb: EnumSocialVerb, reason: EnumReportReason?) -> ())
documentation: Social sends a friend request, friend removal, block, unblock or report for another player. Only engine CoreScripts may call it.
code_sample:
-- CoreScript: send a friend request to each player who joins.
game.Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    game.Players.Social(player, "FriendRequest")
end)

name: Exists
type: ((name: string) -> boolean) & ((self: any, name: string) -> boolean)
documentation: Exists returns whether the place or the platform has a prefab named `name`.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
if game.Prefabs.Exists("TreasureChest") then
    local chest = game.Prefabs.Spawn("TreasureChest")
    if chest then
        chest.Position = Vector3.new(0, 2, 10)
    end
end

name: Id
type: ((name: string) -> number) & ((self: any, name: string) -> number)
documentation: Id returns the numeric id of the prefab `name`, or 0 when there is none. The root of a spawned copy has this id in its `PrefabId` property.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local bulletId = game.Prefabs.Id("Bullet")
local bullet = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Bullet")
-- compare numbers instead of names
if bullet and bullet.PrefabId == bulletId then
    bullet.Position = Vector3.new(0, 5, 0)
end

name: Name
type: ((id: number) -> string?) & ((self: any, id: number) -> string?)
documentation: Name returns the name of the prefab with numeric id `id`, or `nil` when there is none.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local crate = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Crate")
if crate then
    -- look up the prefab name from the copy
    local prefabName = game.Prefabs.Name(crate.PrefabId)
    if prefabName then
        crate.Name = prefabName .. "Copy"
    end
end

name: RevertAddedComponent
type: ((entity: Instance, name: string) -> ()) & ((self: any, entity: Instance, name: string) -> ())
documentation: RevertAddedComponent removes a component that a script or Studio added to an instance of a prefab copy. To reset a component that the prefab has, use RevertObjectOverride.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local gate = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Gate")
if gate then
    gate:AddComponent("Anchored")
    -- remove the added component
    game.Prefabs.RevertAddedComponent(gate, "Anchored")
end

name: RevertObjectOverride
documentation: RevertObjectOverride resets every component shared by `entity` and the prefab to the prefab's values. It leaves children, added or removed components, and tags unchanged.
notes: On the root of the copy, `Name`, `Position`, rotation, `LocalTransform`, and `Pivot` keep their values.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local door = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Door")
if door then
    door.Size = Vector3.new(10, 10, 10)
    -- restore the prefab's size
    game.Prefabs.RevertObjectOverride(door)
end

name: Spawn
type: ((prefab: number | string) -> Instance?) & ((self: any, prefab: number | string) -> Instance?)
documentation: Spawn creates a copy of the prefab `name` and returns its root, or `nil` when no prefab has that name. It places the root at the top of the place, at the position saved in the prefab.
notes: On a client, `Spawn` spawns only platform prefabs and returns `nil` for place prefabs, though `Exists` and `Id` also find place prefabs there.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local enemy = game.Prefabs.Spawn("Goblin")
if enemy then
    -- move the copy to its spawn point
    enemy.Position = Vector3.new(24, 0, -50)
end

name: Dropped
documentation: Dropped returns how many script runs went unrecorded because Scripts already had 64 entries.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
task.wait(10)
if game.Profiler.Dropped() > 0 then
    warn("more scripts run than the profiler tracks")
end

name: Frame
documentation: Frame returns a `FrameStats` table for the last finished frame, or `nil` before the first frame ends.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
function Update(dt)
    local stats = game.Profiler.Frame()
    if stats and stats.interval > 50 then
        warn(string.format("slow frame: %d ms", math.round(stats.interval)))
    end
end

name: Scripts
documentation: Scripts returns a `ScriptCost` table for each of up to 64 scripts that ran recently, in no fixed order.
code_sample:
-- Server script: print the slowest script every 5 seconds.
while true do
    task.wait(5)
    local slowest = nil
    for _, cost in game.Profiler.Scripts() do
        if not slowest or cost.avg > slowest.avg then
            slowest = cost
        end
    end
    if slowest then
        print(slowest.path, slowest.avg)
    end
end

name: BindCharacter
documentation: BindCharacter makes `character` the character of the player `userId`.

name: CharacterDied
type: Signal<(character: Instance?, userId: number?, attacker: Instance?) -> ()>
documentation: CharacterDied fires with the dead character, its owner's user id, and the attacker; each may be `nil`.

name: CharacterOf
documentation: CharacterOf returns the character of the player `userId`, or `nil`.

name: CreatorName
documentation: CreatorName is the creator name that the platform lists for this place. It is `""` in a local test session and before the server sends it at join.

name: Kick
documentation: Kick disconnects the player `userId` at the end of the current server step.

name: LocalCharacter
documentation: LocalCharacter returns the character of the local player, or `nil`.

name: MaxPlayers
documentation: MaxPlayers is how many players this server takes, or `0` until the server sends it at join.

name: PlaceName
documentation: PlaceName is the name of the place this client joined. It is `""` in a local test session and before the server sends it at join.

name: PlayerJoined
documentation: PlayerJoined fires with the user id of each player who joins.

name: PlayerLeft
documentation: PlayerLeft fires with the character, or `nil`, and the user id of each player who leaves.

name: RttMs
documentation: RttMs is the smoothed round trip time between this client and the server, in milliseconds, or `0` before the first clock sync probe returns. The server keeps one per player in Instance.RttMs.

name: ServerTick
documentation: ServerTick is the network tick of the server. On a client it estimates the current server tick, with a fractional part, and reads `0` until its first clock sample, a few frames after joining.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
-- count the network ticks of a one-second wait
local start = game.Session.ServerTick
task.wait(1)
print(game.Session.ServerTick - start)

name: ServerTime
documentation: ServerTime is ServerTick divided by TickRate, the server clock in seconds.

name: TickRate
documentation: TickRate is the number of network ticks the server runs per second.

name: TimeInSession
documentation: TimeInSession is the number of seconds since this client joined. It has no change signal, so read it each frame in `Update`.
code_sample:
-- Client script.
local clock = Instance.new("TextLabel")

function Update(_dt: number)
    -- show minutes and seconds since joining
    local t = math.floor(game.Session.TimeInSession)
    clock.Text = string.format("%dm %02ds", t // 60, t % 60)
end

name: GetBusVolumeDb
documentation: GetBusVolumeDb returns the volume of a mixer bus in decibels.

name: PlayAt
type: (assetId: string, position: vector, volume: number | SoundPlayOptions | nil, options: SoundPlayOptions?) -> boolean
documentation: PlayAt plays a one-shot sound at a world position, with a volume from 0 to 1. Pass the asset id as a string: a number cannot represent every digit of a 64-bit id. It plays at full volume within 10 units and fades to 1/20 at 200 units. The server does not send it to players whose character is farther than 200 units away.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: play a chime at the part every 2 seconds.
local CHIME = "144115188075855954" -- an audio asset id
while true do
    game.Sound.PlayAt(CHIME, self.Position, 0.8)
    task.wait(2)
end

name: SetBusVolumeDb
documentation: SetBusVolumeDb sets the volume of a mixer bus in decibels.
deprecation: Write the `MasterVolume`, `MusicVolume`, `SFXVolume`, and `UIVolume` fields of the `SoundConfig` singleton through World.Query.

name: SurfaceSoundsVolume
documentation: SurfaceSoundsVolume is the volume of the impact and sliding sounds of touching parts, from 0 (silent) to 1.

documentation: SurfaceSoundsVolume is the volume of the impact and sliding sounds of touching parts, from 0 (silent) to 1.

name: open
type: ((name: string) -> Store) & ((self: any, name: string) -> Store)
documentation: open opens or creates the store `name` and returns its `Store` handle. Opening the same name again returns the same store.
code_sample:
-- Server script: count how many times this server has started.
local stats = game.Store.open("server_stats")
local data = stats:get(1) or { starts = 0 }
data.starts += 1
stats:put(1, data)
print("starts: " .. data.starts) -- prints "starts: 1" the first time

name: Add
documentation: Add adds a tag to an instance.

name: Find
documentation: Find returns every instance that has a tag.
deprecation: Use World.Each or World.Query with `game.World.Pair("Tag", tag)`.

name: Get
documentation: Get returns the tag names on an instance.

name: GetInstanceAddedSignal
documentation: GetInstanceAddedSignal returns a signal that fires with each instance that gains the tag, including tagged instances that spawn or replicate.
code_sample:
-- Server script: print each part that becomes an enemy.
game.Tags.GetInstanceAddedSignal("Enemy"):Connect(function(enemy: Instance)
    print(enemy.Name .. " is an enemy")
end)

local goblin = Instance.new("Part")
goblin.Name = "Goblin"
goblin:AddComponent(game.World.Pair("Tag", "Enemy")) -- prints "Goblin is an enemy"

name: GetInstanceRemovedSignal
documentation: GetInstanceRemovedSignal returns a signal that fires with each instance that loses the tag or is destroyed while it has the tag.
code_sample:
-- Server script: keep a set of live enemies.
local enemies: { [Instance]: boolean } = {}

game.Tags.GetInstanceAddedSignal("Enemy"):Connect(function(enemy: Instance)
    enemies[enemy] = true
end)
game.Tags.GetInstanceRemovedSignal("Enemy"):Connect(function(enemy: Instance)
    enemies[enemy] = nil -- a destroyed instance still works as a key
    print("enemy gone")
end)

local goblin = Instance.new("Part")
goblin:AddComponent(game.World.Pair("Tag", "Enemy"))
task.wait(1)
goblin:Destroy() -- prints "enemy gone"

name: Has
documentation: Has returns whether an instance has a tag.

name: Remove
documentation: Remove removes a tag from an instance.

name: Add
type: ((from: vector, to: vector, width: number, color: vector, life: number, transparency: number?) -> ()) & ((self: any, from: vector, to: vector, width: number, color: vector, life: number, transparency: number?) -> ())
documentation: spawn a short-lived trail segment between two world positions

name: TweenProperty
type: ((target: Instance | Component, property: string, final: any, duration: number) -> Tween) & ((self: any, target: Instance | Component, property: string, final: any, duration: number) -> Tween)
documentation: TweenProperty animates a property of an instance to `final` over `duration` seconds and returns a `Tween` handle.
notes: Writes the property after `Update` callbacks run, so it overrides a script that writes the same property in that frame.
When the tween starts, it ends any older tween on the same property.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
local platform = Instance.new("Part")
platform.Anchored = true
platform.Position = Vector3.new(0, 10, 0)

-- slide 20 units along x in 3 seconds
local tween = game.Tween.TweenProperty(platform, "Position", Vector3.new(20, 10, 0), 3)
tween:SetTrans("Sine")
tween.Finished:Connect(function()
    platform.Transparency = 0.5
end)

name: triangulate_polygon
type: (points: buffer, count: number, indices: buffer) -> number
documentation: `geometry.triangulate_polygon` splits a polygon of `count` points into triangles. `points` has two 32-bit floats (x, y) per point, and `indices` receives three 32-bit indices per triangle, counterclockwise. It returns the number of indices written, or 0 when it cannot split the outline.
code_sample:
-- Server script: split a square outline into two triangles.
local corners = { 0, 0, 10, 0, 10, 10, 0, 10 }
local points = buffer.create(#corners * 4)
for i, value in corners do
    buffer.writef32(points, (i - 1) * 4, value)
end

local indices = buffer.create(6 * 4)
print(geometry.triangulate_polygon(points, 4, indices)) -- prints 6

name: apply
documentation: `rotation.apply` turns the vector `v` by the rotation `r`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: launch it forward the way it faces.
self.Anchored = false
local facing = rotation.from_euler(self.Orientation)
self.Velocity = rotation.apply(facing, Vector3.new(0, 0, -30))

name: axis
documentation: `rotation.axis` returns the rotation by `angle` radians about `axis`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a propeller part: spin about Z twice a second.
local angle = 0

function Update(dt: number)
    angle += 4 * math.pi * dt
    self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.axis(Vector3.zAxis, angle))
end

name: compose
documentation: `rotation.compose` returns the rotation that turns by `b` first, then by `a`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a turret part: tilt 10 degrees up, then turn 45 degrees left.
local yaw = rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(45))
local pitch = rotation.axis(Vector3.xAxis, math.rad(10))
self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.compose(yaw, pitch))

name: from_euler
documentation: `rotation.from_euler` converts an `Orientation` in degrees into a rotation vector.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part.
self.Orientation = Vector3.new(0, 90, 0)
local facing = rotation.apply(rotation.from_euler(self.Orientation), Vector3.new(0, 0, -1))
print(math.round(facing.X)) -- prints -1

name: look
documentation: `rotation.look` returns the rotation that points -Z along `forward` with +Y as close to `up` (`Vector3.yAxis` by default) as it can.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: face the world origin.
local direction = Vector3.zero - self.Position
if direction.Magnitude > 0 then
    self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.look(direction))
end

name: slerp
type: (a: vector, b: vector, t: number) -> vector
documentation: `rotation.slerp` blends from rotation `a` at `t` 0 to rotation `b` at `t` 1 along the shortest turn.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: swing a quarter turn over 2 seconds.
local from = rotation.from_euler(self.Orientation)
local to = rotation.compose(rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.pi / 2), from)
local elapsed = 0

function Update(dt: number)
    elapsed = math.min(elapsed + dt, 2)
    self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.slerp(from, to, elapsed / 2))
end

name: to_euler
documentation: `rotation.to_euler` converts a rotation vector into an `Orientation` in degrees.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: face 30 degrees to the left.
self.Orientation = rotation.to_euler(rotation.axis(Vector3.yAxis, math.rad(30)))
print(math.round(self.Orientation.Y)) -- prints 30

name: cancel
documentation: `task.cancel` stops a thread from `task.delay`, `task.defer` or `task.spawn` so it never resumes.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: despawn in 30 seconds unless something touches it.
local despawn = task.delay(30, function()
    self:Destroy()
end)

self.Touched:Connect(function()
    task.cancel(despawn)
end)

name: defer
documentation: `task.defer` runs a function at the end of this tick, after every `Update`, and returns its thread.
code_sample:
-- Server script.
task.defer(print, "second")
print("first")

name: delay
documentation: `task.delay` runs a function after `seconds`, and returns its thread.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: the part disappears after 2 seconds.
task.delay(2, function()
    self:Destroy()
end)

name: spawn
documentation: `task.spawn` runs a function at once, until it waits or ends, and returns its thread. An error in the function logs a `Task error` warning and does not stop the caller.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: blink while the rest of the script goes on.
task.spawn(function()
    while true do
        self.Transparency = 1
        task.wait(0.5)
        self.Transparency = 0
        task.wait(0.5)
    end
end)
print("blinking")

name: wait
documentation: `task.wait` pauses the running thread for at least `seconds`, or one tick when `seconds` is left out, and returns the seconds that passed.
notes: `Update`, `PhysicsUpdate` and `World.System` callbacks cannot wait; start the waiting code with `task.spawn` instead.
A script finishes loading at its first top-level wait, so declare `Update`, `PhysicsUpdate` and `Migrate` before it; see `Update`.
code_sample:
-- Server script in a part: a platform that moves up and down every 3 seconds.
local low = self.Position
local high = low + Vector3.new(0, 6, 0)

while true do
    task.wait(3)
    self.Position = high
    task.wait(3)
    self.Position = low
end

type: function Lerp(self, other: vector, alpha: number): vector
